issue.title: Daemon logging: rolling file appender + in-memory ring buffer + StoreLayer
issue.context:
Right now the daemon's tracing output only goes to stderr via `tracing_subscriber::fmt().init()` in crates/wisphive_cli/src/commands/daemon.rs:22-26, so long-running sessions flood the terminal and logs are lost when the terminal scrollback rolls. DaemonConfig::log_dir (~/.wisphive/logs) is already declared and ensure_dirs()'d, but nothing writes there.

This issue introduces a new `wisphive_daemon::logging` module containing:

1. `LogRecord` — serde-serializable { ts (RFC3339), level, target, message, fields }.
2. `LogStore` — Arc-wrapped ring buffer (VecDeque + std Mutex, default capacity 4096) + tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<LogRecord> fanout with channel size 256. Methods: tail(n, min_level), subscribe(), push() (pop_front on overflow, then tx.send ignoring NoReceivers).
3. `StoreLayer` — implements tracing_subscriber::Layer<S>::on_event, using a field Visit impl to capture message + fields into a formatted string, timestamps with chrono::Utc::now(), calls store.push.
4. `init(log_dir, store, stderr_level) -> LogGuards` — composes Registry::default() with EnvFilter (RUST_LOG or default "info"), stderr fmt layer filtered to stderr_level (default WARN so the terminal stays quiet), JSON fmt layer writing via tracing_appender::rolling::daily(&log_dir, "wisphive.log") wrapped in non_blocking (returns WorkerGuard), and StoreLayer. Returns LogGuards holding the WorkerGuard.
5. `prune_old_files(log_dir, retention_days)` — read_dir + modified() < cutoff, unlink; called once at startup.

Wiring in crates/wisphive_cli/src/commands/daemon.rs: replace the existing fmt().init() block with LogStore::new(4096) + logging::init(&config.log_dir, log_store.clone(), Level::WARN)? + prune_old_files(&config.log_dir, 14).ok(). Explicitly `drop(_log_guards);` above the std::process::exit(0) at :84 to flush the non-blocking appender.

Add `log_retention_days: Option<u64>` to UserConfig (default 14) in crates/wisphive_daemon/src/config.rs and plumb through to the pruner call.

No web wiring in this issue — subsequent issues thread the LogStore into wisphive_web::serve.

issue.title: Web API: GET /api/logs/ws live-tail WebSocket with lag marker
issue.context:
After the backfill endpoint lands, add a WebSocket endpoint that pushes new log records to the browser in real time.

- Add route `.route("/api/logs/ws", get(logs_ws))`. Reuses the existing security_middleware (path starts with /api/), so the frontend passes the bearer via ?token= as it does for the main /ws endpoint.
- Handler: upgrade the WS, immediately send a backfill of the last 500 records (serde_json::to_string each, Message::Text), then loop on a broadcast::Receiver<LogRecord>::recv():
  - Ok(rec) → send as Text JSON
  - Err(RecvError::Lagged(n)) → send {"type":"lagged","count":n} marker, continue (don't crash)
  - Err(RecvError::Closed) → break
- When log_store is None (standalone web), close the WS with a 1011 Internal Error close frame or reject the upgrade with 503. Either is acceptable; document the choice in the handler.
- Use tokio::select! to also poll for ws close so a disconnecting browser ends the loop promptly.
- Test: spawn a LogStore, open a WS via tower::ServiceExt::oneshot or axum::test harness, push records, assert they arrive. Separate test: push N > channel_capacity records without reading, then assert next read yields a `lagged` marker rather than crashing.

issue.title: Protocol: SubscribeLogs/LogEvent so standalone `wisphive web` can stream daemon logs
issue.context:
The initial /api/logs implementation only exposes logs when the web server runs in-process with the daemon (`wisphive daemon start --web`). Standalone `wisphive web` returns 503 because it has no LogStore of its own.

Close that gap by adding a protocol subscription:

- Extend wisphive_protocol: `ClientMessage::SubscribeLogs { tail: Option<usize>, level: Option<String> }` and `ServerMessage::LogEvent(LogRecord)` plus `ServerMessage::LogBackfill(Vec<LogRecord>)` (or a single bounded chunk on subscribe).
- In the daemon server, on SubscribeLogs: send a backfill chunk, then subscribe to the LogStore broadcast and forward LogEvent messages on the client socket until disconnect.
- In wisphive_web, when log_store is None, route /api/logs and /api/logs/ws through a fresh Unix-socket connection to the daemon that sends SubscribeLogs and proxies the LogEvent stream back out to the browser (similar pattern to ws_bridge.rs).
- Consider whether to keep the LogStore-direct path for the embedded mode as an optimization, or route everything through the protocol for consistency. Document the choice.
- Tests: protocol round-trip serde, daemon-side forwarding under lag, web-side proxy end-to-end.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Protocol gains SubscribeLogs client message and LogEvent + LogBackfill server messages; serde round-trip tested.
- [ ] Daemon server handles SubscribeLogs: backfill then live stream.
- [ ] Standalone `wisphive web` serves /api/logs and /api/logs/ws successfully (no more 503).
- [ ] Lag is handled gracefully end-to-end (marker reaches the browser).
- [ ] cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings clean.

issue.title: Web frontend ExitPlanMode shows generic Approve/Deny instead of plan-specific options

issue.title: PreToolUse fallthrough swallows unknown hook events
issue.context:
crates/wisphive_hook/src/main.rs:80-88 dispatches by HookEventType: PermissionRequest, Stop/SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit/ConfigChange, Elicitation, TeammateIdle, TaskCompleted have specific formatters. issue.title: Web security: 404 on /api/devices/{id}/revoke for unknown id
issue.context: Review feedback on itr#214 (R1 S2). state.rs::revoke_web_device is idempotent via WHERE revoked_at IS NULL, which means it is also a no-op on nonexistent ids — the handler returns 200 and writes an audit row regardless. An authenticated device can therefore pollute the web_audit log with arbitrary 'target' strings (capped at 4KB per row by the truncation, but unlimited in row count). Fix: have revoke_web_device return rows_affected, and 404 on zero. Skip the audit row when the row did not exist. Preserves idempotency on already-revoked rows (those still match revoked_at IS NULL? no — they match NOT NULL. Today the query updates zero rows on both 'nonexistent' and 'already revoked', indistinguishable. Keep idempotent-on-already-revoked: the SELECT id existence check + conditional UPDATE is the right shape).

issue.title: Seamless web onboarding: auto-open browser + mobile pairing via QR
issue.context:
Parent/umbrella for the two-stage onboarding flow.

## Flow
**Stage 1 (desktop, loopback only)**: On `wisphive daemon start --web`, detect first-run (no password hash) and auto-open the default browser to the onboarding page. User sets password + optionally registers a desktop passkey. Listener stays bound to 127.0.0.1.

**Stage 2 (mobile pairing, ephemeral LAN)**: User clicks 'Add Device'. Backend generates a pairing token (256-bit, single-use, ~10-min TTL), detects LAN IP, spins up an **ephemeral second listener** on <LAN_IP>:<port>, extends the Origin/Host allowlist, and renders a QR code. Phone scans -> lands on /pair?token=X over HTTPS -> registers a WebAuthn passkey -> gets a device token. Desktop receives a DevicePaired WS event and updates live. Ephemeral listener torn down on token consumed or expired.

## Design decisions locked in
- **No new --onboard flag**: auto-open is a smart default behind first-run detection. Add `--no-open` to suppress. Matches vite dev / jupyter conventions.
- **No 0.0.0.0 bind at startup**: LAN exposure is user-initiated and time-limited via the ephemeral listener.
- **Trusted cert path**: support `--tls-cert <path>` / `--tls-key <path>` so users with a real domain (Tailscale, mkcert, Let's Encrypt) skip self-signed warnings. Self-signed stays the zero-config default.
- **Passkey over HTTPS**: passkey registration requires secure context; self-signed means one-time 'proceed anyway' tap on phone. Documented, acceptable for localhost. Trusted-cert path eliminates it for users who opt in.

## Sub-issues (dependency order)
See child issues - the TLS SAN/cert work blocks Stage 2; Stage 1 can ship independently.

## Security notes
- Pairing token: 256-bit, single-use, 10-min TTL, rate-limited /pair endpoint
- Ephemeral LAN listener: torn down on token consumed/expired; allowlist shrinks back
- web.token stays session-scoped (regenerated per daemon start) - unchanged
- First-run detection must be race-safe (don't auto-open if password is being set concurrently)

## Acceptance
- Fresh install: `wisphive daemon start --web` opens browser to onboarding; user sets password and is logged in without touching the CLI
- Logged-in desktop user clicks 'Add Device' -> QR renders -> phone scans -> registers passkey -> desktop updates live with the new device
- Phone device appears in `wisphive web devices list`
- Second daemon start after onboarding does NOT auto-open browser
- `--no-open` suppresses auto-open on first-run
- User-provided `--tls-cert` / `--tls-key` are honored; no self-signed cert is written when both are provided

issue.title: Stage 2a: TLS cert with LAN IP in SAN + user-provided cert support
issue.context:
The self-signed cert currently generated in `tls.rs` only covers loopback names. Phone browsers hitting `https://<LAN_IP>:<port>` will fail with cert-hostname-mismatch on top of the self-signed warning. Must regenerate with the detected LAN IP in SubjectAltName. Also add a path for users with a real cert.

## Scope
- LAN IP detection via `local-ip-address` crate (pick default-route interface; warn if multiple)
- Regenerate self-signed cert with SANs: `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`, `<detected-LAN-IP>`. Re-regen if detected LAN IP differs from cert metadata (use existing `web.cert.meta.json`).
- CLI: add `--tls-cert <path>` and `--tls-key <path>` flags to `daemon start --web` and `web serve`. When both are provided, load from disk via rustls, skip self-signed generation entirely, and don't write `web.cert.pem`/`web.key.pem`.
- Preserve existing rotation semantics (397-day cap, atomic rotate under `web.cert.lock`)

## Non-goals
- ACME / Let's Encrypt automation (document as a manual option)
- Cert trust install on mobile (out of scope; the trusted-cert path is the answer for users who want zero friction)

## Acceptance
- Self-signed cert includes detected LAN IP in SAN list
- Changing network (different LAN IP) triggers regen on next daemon start
- `--tls-cert` + `--tls-key` pointing at a valid PEM pair skips self-signed entirely
- Phone hitting `https://<LAN_IP>:<port>` gets 'self-signed' warning only (no hostname-mismatch)
- Phone with trusted cert (e.g., Tailscale cert for daemon.<ts-net>.ts.net) gets no warning at all
issue.acceptance: Self-signed cert covers LAN IP; user-provided cert path works end-to-end

issue.title: Stage 2b: pairing token module + ephemeral LAN listener
issue.context:
Backend mechanics for the 'Add Device' flow. No LAN exposure until the user initiates pairing.

## Scope
### Pairing token module (new)
- 256-bit random token, base64url-encoded
- Single-use, ~10-min TTL
- In-memory HashMap keyed by token hash; metadata: created, expires, claimed_at (Option)
- `POST /api/pair/arm` (bearer-gated): consumes nothing, returns { token, url, expires_at } and spins up LAN listener (see below). Only the authenticated user can arm.
- `POST /api/pair/register` (token-gated, NOT bearer): validates token, consumes on success, accepts WebAuthn registration payload, returns device token
- `POST /api/pair/cancel` (bearer-gated): invalidates token, tears down listener early

### Ephemeral LAN listener
- When a pairing token is armed: detect LAN IP, bind a second axum listener on `<LAN_IP>:<port>` (same router), extend Origin/Host allowlist with `<LAN_IP>:<port>` (and origin variants)
- On token consumed/expired/cancelled: shut down listener via `tokio::sync::watch` or graceful-shutdown handle, shrink allowlist back
- At most one ephemeral listener at a time
- Loopback listener is untouched — stays always-on

### WS event
- New `DevicePaired { device_id, name, kind }` event broadcast when /api/pair/register succeeds so the desktop UI updates live without polling

## Security
- Rate-limit /api/pair/register (per-IP, reuse auth throttle)
- Token hash stored, not raw token (defense in depth)
- Log all arm/consume/cancel events to audit

## Non-goals
- QR rendering (frontend)
- TLS SAN work (270 handles that)

## Acceptance
- arm -> listener up on LAN IP, token issued
- Phone GET `/pair?token=X` over LAN IP works; POST /api/pair/register registers a device
- Token single-use: second attempt returns 409/410
- Expiry: listener torn down on timeout; allowlist reverts
- Cancel from desktop tears down listener early
- `DevicePaired` WS event fires on successful registration


## Profile gating (added 2026-05-16, /alignment session)

The ephemeral LAN listener (and the `/api/pair/arm` route that spins it up) is **LocalLAN-only**. Gate via `policy.allow_ephemeral_lan_listener` from #310 (`AuthProfile`):

- `POST /api/pair/arm` returns **409 Conflict** with `{ error: "pairing_disabled_under_enterprise" }` when `policy.allow_ephemeral_lan_listener == false`.
- TTL reaper + listener spawn machinery only runs when at least one armed token exists — under Enterprise the code path is dormant.
- Under Enterprise, device enrollment uses the operator-driven flow in **#313** instead (one-time URL served on the primary listener; no LAN exposure).

This gating is a small change to this issue's scope; the bulk of #271 is unchanged.

issue.title: Stage 2c: frontend add-device QR flow + mobile /pair route
issue.context:
Two frontend surfaces: desktop 'Add Device' page that renders a QR + live status, and mobile `/pair` page that does WebAuthn registration.

## Scope
### Desktop `/settings/add-device`
- CTA button 'Add device' -> POST /api/pair/arm
- Render QR for returned URL (`qrcode` npm package or `react-qr-code`)
- Show expiry countdown (~10 min)
- Subscribe to WS DevicePaired event -> show success UI with device name/kind
- 'Cancel' button -> POST /api/pair/cancel
- Show the URL in text form underneath QR as fallback (for users who can't scan)

### Mobile `/pair?token=X`
- Route is accessible WITHOUT bearer token (gated by pairing token in URL instead)
- Lands on phone after QR scan. Show 'Pair this device' screen.
- Device name input (default: user-agent-derived hint, e.g. 'iPhone (Safari)')
- Invokes `navigator.credentials.create()` with options fetched from backend
- POST /api/pair/register with WebAuthn payload
- Success screen: 'Device paired - return to desktop' + sets device token cookie so phone is now logged in
- Failure states: expired token, already-claimed token, WebAuthn not supported

### Dependencies
- `qrcode` or `react-qr-code` npm package
- Existing WebAuthn helpers from Stage 1c passkey registration

## Acceptance
- Click Add Device -> QR appears with valid URL
- Phone scans -> lands on /pair -> registers passkey -> success
- Desktop live-updates with 'iPhone (Safari) paired' via WS
- Mobile-responsive on both surfaces (pair page is phone-first; add-device desktop-first but must work on tablet)
- Countdown matches backend expiry within reasonable skew
- Cancel from desktop immediately invalidates the QR


## Profile gating (added 2026-05-16, /alignment session)

This flow (Desktop QR + mobile `/pair`) is **LocalLAN-only**. Under Enterprise, devices are added via #313's operator-driven enroll URL flow instead.

Implications:
- Desktop 'Add device' button on Devices.tsx (#220) renders this QR flow **only when** `useAuthProfile().allowEphemeralListener === true`; renders the Enterprise enroll URL flow otherwise.
- Mobile `/pair?token=X` route is reachable only via the ephemeral listener (LocalLAN); does not exist on the primary listener under Enterprise.
- Per #310's RP ID derivation: under LocalLAN the phone authenticates against the LAN-IP origin where RP ID is `None`, so the phone **does not** enroll a passkey in this flow — it receives a device bearer from `/api/pair/register` and uses that. issue.title: Thread AbortController through apiFetch call sites (unmount-safe async)
issue.context:
apiFetch currently has no AbortController plumbing. Any in-flight fetch continues to completion after the component that kicked it off unmounts, and its handler may try to setState on an unmounted component (swallowed by React 18+, but still a latent leak + wasted bandwidth).

Surfaced in itr#217 review by the strict-react reviewer: Login.tsx's onLogin runs while the gate is still on it; if the user closes the tab or gets rug-pulled by a 401 from a sibling fetch, the login POST completes against a dead tree. Same pattern across every apiFetch caller.

## Scope
- Add an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` to apiFetch (already accepted natively via init.signal — just document and thread)
- Add an abort-on-unmount helper for hook call sites (useAuth.login, probeStatus; useWisphive initial dial; Config/History/Sessions/Projects loaders)
- Distinguish AbortError from other failures in error handlers so unmount-aborts don't set error state

## Non-goals
- Rewriting fetch to a custom client
- Retry/backoff (separate concern)

## Acceptance
- Unmounting the Login component mid-POST does not produce React unmounted-setState warnings or set an error state on a stale component
- All apiFetch call sites that run in hooks thread a signal from useEffect's AbortController
- New hook test demonstrates abort semantics (mock fetch + unmount mid-flight)

issue.title: Web auth token storage: evaluate alternatives to localStorage (XSS exfiltration)
issue.context:
The device bearer token is stored in localStorage['wisphive-web-token']. Any script execution in the app — including novel vectors from embedded content like xterm escape sequences, markdown rendering (DetailView, itr#103 XSS), or a hypothetical supply-chain compromise of a dep — exfiltrates the bearer in one read. That bearer gates AI-agent tool approval, so exfil is equivalent to a remote-code-execution primitive through the daemon.

Surfaced in itr#217 review by the security-auditor as a known/acknowledged tradeoff. Worth a dedicated evaluation, not a quick patch.

## Options to evaluate
1. **httpOnly cookie** — server sets on /api/auth/login. Pro: scripts can't read it; browsers manage lifetime. Con: WS upgrade in browsers still needs ?token= query-param (no custom headers), so the cookie would need to be mirrored into a WS-specific short-lived ticket. CSRF surface (SameSite=Strict mitigates but needs thinking).
2. **sessionStorage** — narrow the blast radius to current tab only. Still JS-readable; mostly UX punishment (relog on tab close) for minimal security gain.
3. **In-memory only + device ticket re-issuance** — keep the token in a JS module-scope variable, never persist. On reload, require passkey re-auth to re-mint. Highest security; highest UX cost; depends on itr#219 shipping first.
4. **Web Crypto encrypted storage** — localStorage the token encrypted with a non-extractable CryptoKey. Doesn't actually help against XSS (attacker script can just call decrypt), theatre.

## Deliverable
- Threat-model doc comparing options against: XSS blast radius, supply-chain blast radius, CSRF, UX cost, implementation cost, interaction with itr#219 passkey flow
- Recommendation + ADR
- Linked sub-issues for the chosen path

## Non-goals (in this issue)
- Shipping the implementation — this is evaluation only. Spin out the chosen option as a follow-up.

## Acceptance
- docs/threat-model-web-token-storage.md (or similar) comparing the four options with pros/cons and a recommendation
- ADR or decision note in the PR
- Sub-issue filed for the chosen implementation path
issue.acceptance: Decision doc merged; chosen path filed as follow-up issue with clear scope

issue.title: Harden web approve stash: only track sudo-class tools client-side
issue.context:
Surfaced in itr#255 review (Claim 3 — THEORETICAL). useWisphive.approve() stashes opts for every approve regardless of tool class, keyed by request_id. The third reviewer verified this isn't reachable today because the daemon only emits WebReauthRequired from sudo-class gated arms on the same connection, so a stale event can't replay a Read approve. issue.title: Setup pairing token: defense-in-depth vs local first-run race on /api/auth/set-password
issue.context:
Surfaced in itr#268 security review. POST /api/auth/set-password is unauthenticated and setup-gate-bypassing — the first process on loopback to POST claims the account. try_set_initial_web_password serializes the race, but atomicity doesn't help if a local attacker *wins* the race against the operator's browser. Any local process (malware, other local user on a shared box, LAN if binding is misconfigured) can beat the browser.

## Proposed approach
Match the existing ~/.wisphive/web.token pattern:
- On daemon start in setup-required mode, write ~/.wisphive/setup.token (mode 0600) with a random 256-bit value
- POST /api/auth/set-password requires the token via X-Wisphive-Setup-Token header or ?setup= query param
- Delete the token file atomically on first successful password-set
- Print the setup URL (with the token) in the startup banner alongside the LAN/loopback URL
- The auto-open browser (itr#267) uses the tokened URL

Effect: attacker surface narrows from 'any local process' to 'any local process running as the operator UID' — matches the operator's actual trust boundary.

## Alternative
TOFU pairing code: daemon prints a 6-digit code on stderr; operator confirms in the UI. Heavier UX but no on-disk state.

## Acceptance
- Fresh install: daemon writes setup.token; auto-open URL includes ?setup=<token>; form submits include it; server validates
- Token file is unlinked atomically when the first password-set succeeds
- A script POSTing set-password without the token gets 401 (not 409/400/500)
- Test: concurrent set-password with valid-token wins; concurrent set-password without wins nothing
- Document in README threat-model section

## Related
- itr#267 (auto-open URL would include the setup token)
- itr#268 (the endpoint being hardened)
issue.acceptance: Local non-operator process cannot win the first-run set-password race

issue.title: Global Argon2 semaphore to bound blocking-pool pressure under distributed attack
issue.context:
Surfaced in itr#268 security review. MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_IP caps single-IP attackers but any distributed attacker (botnet, NAT'd clients) can pin a blocking-pool thread per-request. Tokio's default blocking pool is 512 threads — 512 concurrent unique-IP requesters performing ~50ms Argon2 hashes fully starve it, stalling every other blocking-pool user (DB writes, file I/O).

## Scope
- Add a global Arc<tokio::sync::Semaphore> with ~8–16 permits wrapping every Argon2 verify/hash call site
- Acquire the permit BEFORE spawn_blocking so queued requests don't pile up on the blocking pool
- Call sites today: post_auth_login (lib.rs ~227), post_auth_reauth (lib.rs ~351), post_auth_set_password (lib.rs ~516)
- Permit count is a tradeoff: too few → legitimate login latency under load; too many → DoS window stays open. 8 is a reasonable default for loopback/LAN deployments; make it a config knob

## Non-goals
- Replacing the per-IP throttle (it's still valuable for stopping single-source brute-force)
- Switching to a different KDF

## Acceptance
- Bench: 1000 concurrent unique-IP requests saturate the semaphore but don't stall unrelated blocking-pool users
- Login latency under normal load is unchanged
- Test: concurrent login attempts complete in batches matching permit count

## Related
- itr#245 (auth.rs verify-deadline) is orthogonal but adjacent
- itr#243 (MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_IP configurable) similar config-knob thinking
issue.acceptance: Distributed auth attack cannot exhaust the blocking pool

issue.title: Transaction-wrap set-password + device insert for atomic onboarding
issue.context:
Surfaced in itr#268 security review. post_auth_set_password currently does two sequential DB writes: try_set_initial_web_password then insert_web_device. - Existing integration tests still pass

issue.title: Login handleSubmit memoization + HTTP-date Retry-After comment
issue.context:
Minor nits from the itr#268 React review — safe to defer, cheap enough to batch later.

## Items
1. Login.tsx handleSubmit is useCallback([disabled, isSetup, password, confirm, deviceName, ...]) — deps include password/confirm which change on every keystroke, so the callback re-memos per-keystroke. Either switch to refs for password/confirm or drop useCallback (inline arrow is actually cheaper here). Follow #217's stable-handler pattern for consistency.

The HTTP spec also allows HTTP-date form (RFC 7231 §7.1.3: 'Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT'). Our backend only sends integer seconds, but a future transit proxy could theoretically rewrite to HTTP-date. Either parse it or add a comment acknowledging we intentionally ignore that form.

issue.context:

## Why this epic (above the existing #266 umbrella)
#266 is a feature-kind parent that pre-dates the deeper investigation. This epic wraps #266 + security prerequisites + cross-cutting design work (RP ID strategy, browser smoke, trusted-cert guidance) that no single child issue owns.

## Critical path (strict order)
1. itr#227 — TLS SAN filter (Docker/VPN/utun out; RFC1918 in)
2. itr#270 — LAN IP in cert SAN + --tls-cert/--tls-key user-cert flags
3. itr#271 — Pairing token module + ephemeral LAN listener + DevicePaired WS event
4. itr#272 — Desktop QR + mobile /pair + WebAuthn glue

## Parallel required

- itr#269 — Stage 1c onboarding route (#268 is ready-to-close)

## Security prerequisites (must close before LAN exposure ships)

- itr#80 — hook fail-open bypass
- itr#257 — sudo-gate device revoke

## Key design decisions locked in the plan doc
- Per-origin WebAuthn credentials (strategy C) — no cross-origin portability in v1
- Shared TLS cert between primary + ephemeral listeners
- One armed pairing token at a time (409 on double-arm)
- /api/pair/arm is sudo-gated

See docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md for full sizing, risk analysis, and per-issue deep dives.

The original critical path locked 'RP ID strategy C — per-origin credentials' as a single global posture. That decision silently breaks for the LAN-IP-origin phone case (WebAuthn rejects IP literals as RP IDs). The /alignment session resolved this by reframing auth as a **profile** abstraction (#310): operators pick LocalLAN (default) or Enterprise at startup, and each profile locks a coherent set of defaults.

- **Enterprise**: #271/#272 paths are dormant (`/api/pair/arm` → 409). Devices added via #313 (operator-driven one-time enroll URL, served on primary listener, requires real domain + trusted cert). Passkey works on both desktop and phone since RP ID is a real registrable domain.

issue.title: Server-authoritative terminal scrollback on attach (multi-device)
issue.context:
Move terminal scrollback to be server-authoritative so attach-time history works identically across devices, browsers, reconnects, and tab switches.

Today (2026-04):
- Daemon runs vt100 with scrollback=0 (terminal.rs:213-216) — only current screen is held in memory; full history lives in SQLite.
- TermAttach sends a vt100 catchup snapshot only (server.rs:886).
- Frontend calls term.reset() on catchup (TerminalView.tsx:66-68), wiping xterm's local 5000-line buffer.
- Net effect: switching terminals, reconnecting the WS, or attaching from a second device all drop scrollback to 'current screen only'.

Existing plumbing we reuse:
- TermReplay { id, from_seq, speed } is already on the wire (wire.rs:224).
- state_db.replay_terminal_events(id, from_seq) already streams from SQLite (state.rs:1532).

Target shape:
- TermAttach gains an optional from_seq.
- Daemon: if from_seq present, replay from there; else serve a bounded tail (last N lines/bytes) from SQLite, then go live.
- Client tracks last-seen seq per session in localStorage; passes it on re-attach for bandwidth efficiency.
- New device / fresh browser → no from_seq → bounded tail. Identical UX on every device.

Privacy stance (decided 2026-04-24): pairing a device grants full session scrollback access. Justified because all sessions belong to the user; the pairing UI must surface this clearly.

Supersedes the client-side xterm-cache approach discussed earlier (insufficient for the cross-device case).
issue.acceptance: TermAttach carries from_seq; daemon replays bounded tail on attach; client seq tracking persists across refresh; pairing UI explains scrollback access; itr#283 doc updated.

notes.content: Concrete root cause for 'scroll breaks after switching terminals' (from itr#445 debugging): daemon terminal.rs catchup_snapshot() = parser.screen().contents_formatted() — the vt100 CURRENT SCREEN only. Parser is built vt100::Parser::new(rows,cols,0) — scrollback=0 BY DESIGN (terminal.rs:213-216: 'full replay goes through SQLite; keeping scrollback out of memory bounds'). Consequence: every attach/re-attach reproduces just the visible screen with ZERO scrollback, so after switching back BOTH wheel and touch are stuck (nothing to scroll). Verified in a real-app CDP test. Fix = replay a bounded scrollback tail on attach (this epic + from_seq itr#285). vt100 exposes set_scrollback/contents_between if we choose the in-parser route, but that reverses the documented memory-bounds decision — weigh vs SQLite-replay.

e3d29b9 delivers the attach-seed mechanism: TermAttach now serves server-authoritative scrollback (persisted output tail, 256 KiB cap, before_seq-bounded, prepended to the catchup screen; the ESC[H ESC[J repaint cannot disturb seeded history), so re-attach/refresh restores real scrollback for requesters passing the replay ACL. REMAINS: (a) non-creator devices still get screen-only — the cross-surface grant path is itr#623; (b) the denial is silent at attach (no UI guidance); (c) seed cap means very long histories are tail-truncated — full history stays behind audited TermReplay; (d) TUI-side re-attach unaffected by this change.

issue.title: TermAttach: add optional from_seq protocol field
issue.context:
Add an optional from_seq: Option<u64> to ClientMessage::TermAttach in wisphive_protocol/src/wire.rs.

- Backwards compatible: serde default = None means 'no preferred starting point, server picks the tail'.
- Add a round-trip test in wire.rs covering both Some(seq) and None variants (mirror the existing round_trip_term_attach_detach_close_list_replay coverage at wire.rs:1094).
- Update the TS protocol mirror in crates/wisphive_web/frontend/src/types/protocol.ts so the field is plumbed through useWisphive.

Out of scope: any daemon-side handling — that's the next issue.

issue.title: Daemon: bounded-tail replay on TermAttach
issue.context:
Wire bounded-tail replay into the TermAttach handler in crates/wisphive_daemon/src/server.rs (around 875-925).

Behaviour:
- If from_seq is Some(n) and (current_seq - n) <= REPLAY_CAP, stream events from n via state_db.replay_terminal_events, then subscribe to the live broadcast (the existing dedupe at server.rs:897 covers any overlap).
- If from_seq is None, compute a 'last N lines' tail seq from SQLite and replay from there.
- If the gap exceeds REPLAY_CAP, fall back to today's catchup snapshot AND emit a warning event so the client can render 'earlier scrollback unavailable'.
- Make REPLAY_CAP and the tail-window size configurable via wisphive config. Suggested defaults: 10K events, 1MB output bytes, 5K rendered lines — pick whichever single bound is cheapest to compute, layer the others as guards.

Constraint: do NOT introduce a new in-memory scrollback buffer in the daemon. SQLite remains the source of truth — preserves the design intent at terminal.rs:213-216.
issue.acceptance: Fresh-client attach mid-session shows a meaningful tail of scrollback (not just current screen); same-session re-attach with a recent from_seq emits zero duplicate frames (test asserts seq monotonicity); cap-exceeded path falls back gracefully without dropping the live stream.

issue.title: Web: track last-seen seq per session and send from_seq on re-attach
issue.context:
Track the last seq seen per terminal session in the web frontend and pass it as from_seq on TermAttach so the daemon can replay only the gap.

- Extend useWisphive state with a Map<sessionId, lastSeq>.
- term_chunk and term_catchup messages already carry seq info — update lastSeq on every chunk arrival.
- On TermAttach (Terminals.tsx handleSelect → onAttach), include the cached lastSeq as from_seq.
- Persist the map to localStorage so refresh / tab close survives. Bounded LRU (e.g. 50 sessions) to keep storage small.
- Stop calling term.reset() in TerminalView on catchup when the daemon's response is a replay (not a snapshot fallback). The daemon should signal which mode it used; only reset on snapshot-fallback.
issue.acceptance: Switching between terminals preserves xterm scrollback (no visible reset); browser refresh while a session is open re-attaches with from_seq and recovers scrollback up to cap; localStorage survives daemon restart so reconnect benefits from the cached seq.

issue.title: logging: typed JSON visitor — preserve numeric/bool values recorded via %/?
issue.context:
Follow-up from itr#238 review. `FieldVisitor::record_debug` currently stores everything as `serde_json::Value::String(format!("{:?}", value))`. tracing dispatches `info!(count = %n, ...)` and `info!(?vec, ...)` through `record_debug`, so numeric fields become quoted strings and arrays/objects round-trip through Debug-rendering. This will make the future web/TUI log viewer's filter-by-numeric-field UX awkward.

Proposed fix: in `record_debug`, attempt `serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&format!("{:?}", value))` first; fall back to `Value::String` only on parse failure. Watch the edge case where `%display_str` produces `hello` (not valid JSON) vs `"hello"` (valid JSON string) — both should land as `Value::String("hello")` in the end.

Alternative: override `record_*` for as many primitive types as tracing exposes (bytes, error) and leave `record_debug` as the string fallback only.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] `info!(count = %3u64, name = %"alice", "hello")` round-trips with `count` as JSON Number and `name` as JSON String
- [ ] `info!(?my_struct, ...)` for an opaque Debug type still lands as a String fallback
- [ ] No panic on malformed Debug output
- [ ] Test added under `logging::tests`

issue.title: wisphive agent {start,list,stop} reads wrong daemon response after handshake
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (High #1) and docs/code_reivew/03-testing-ci-and-maintainability.md (Medium #3).

handle_tui sends Welcome -> AgentsSnapshot -> QueueSnapshot. commands::agent::connect_to_daemon reads only Welcome, and send_and_recv drains one extra line before sending the command. The drained line is AgentsSnapshot, so the next read after SpawnAgent/ListAgents/StopAgent is the stale QueueSnapshot, not the real response. Users see 'Unexpected response: QueueSnapshot' and the agent CLI looks broken even though the daemon performed the action. crates/wisphive_cli/src/commands/term.rs correctly drains all three startup messages.

Fix: drain Welcome+AgentsSnapshot+QueueSnapshot in connect_to_daemon, mirroring term::connect. Or extract a shared TUI-like client helper (see itr#124).

issue.title: Web: multi sudo-gated approvals strand older requests after reauth
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/02-web-frontend.md (High #6).

approveStashRef stores approvals by request id. When web_reauth_required arrives, pendingReauth is replaced with the newest request id. The comment claims old and new stashes both replay via a secondary drain, but retryPendingApprove only reads and sends the single current pendingReauth.request_id and no secondary drain exists. If a user approves two sudo-class requests before reauthing, the second gate replaces pendingReauth, reauth retries only the newest approve, and the older request remains queued with a stale stash and no modal prompting for retry.

Fix: model pendingReauth as a queue/set of gated request ids, or drain all stashed approvals that still correspond to queued requests after a successful reauth.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Two consecutive web_reauth_required messages followed by retryPendingApprove approve both queued requests (or the UI prompts for the remaining one)
- [ ] Vitest covers the multi-sudo scenario

issue.title: Move terminal output side effects (term_chunk/catchup/replay_chunk) out of useWisphive reducer
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/02-web-frontend.md (High #5).

handleMessage calls setState((prev) => { switch (...) { ... } }). The term_chunk, term_catchup, and term_replay_chunk cases call terminal output handlers (xterm writes) inside that updater. React requires state updaters to be pure; in StrictMode and concurrent rendering, React can invoke the updater more than once, which would corrupt the xterm buffer and replay chunks twice. itr#114 covers document.title+Notification in the same reducer; this is the same anti-pattern in different branches and should be fixed together or as a sibling.

Fix: route terminal/browser side effects outside setState; use setState only for state transitions.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] In StrictMode, feeding a term_chunk invokes the registered terminal handler exactly once
- [ ] term_replay_chunk and term_catchup likewise invoke handlers once
- [ ] Cross-link with itr#114 in the PR

issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #1).

The ApprovePermission arm looks up permission_suggestions[suggestion_index]. If the index is invalid, selected becomes None, but the daemon still constructs RichDecision { decision: Approve, selected_permission: None, ... }, resolves the queue item, and persists the approval. A malformed/malicious local client can resolve a PermissionRequest as approved without actually selecting a permission.

issue.title: Daemon: Ask/defer leaves stale rows in pending_decisions
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #3) and docs/composers_code_review/daemon-and-state.md (High - Ask vs pending_decisions rows).

ClientMessage::Ask resolves the in-memory queue with Decision::Ask but intentionally skips state_db.resolve_pending because Ask decisions are not logged. issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #2) and docs/code_reivew/03-testing-ci-and-maintainability.md (Medium #2).

handle_hook calls state_db.persist_pending(&req) with a comment 'Persist for crash recovery'. Server::new creates an empty DecisionQueue. There is no load_pending, recovery pass, or queue seeding from pending_decisions. After a daemon restart, persisted pending rows are invisible to TUI/web clients and the table accumulates stale rows.

Decide intended semantics:
- If hooks are fail-open on daemon crash, remove the 'crash recovery' claim and aggressively prune stale rows.
- If pending decisions should be recoverable, add a recovery path that marks old requests as timed-out/approved/abandoned (cannot recreate dead oneshot senders).
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Decision documented in CLAUDE.md and source comments
- [ ] Either pending rows are restored on startup OR they are pruned with an explicit policy
- [ ] Integration test: persist a pending row, restart server, assert expected behavior

Semantics documented in CLAUDE.md crash-recovery bullet + source. Restart integration test + StateDb drain test. Commit 63d1273. Review pass running.

issue.title: Daemon: persist_pending omits permission_suggestions despite DB column
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #4).

issue.title: Daemon: event_ingest seeks to EOF — auto-approved events written before startup are skipped
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #5).

run_ingest opens events.jsonl and immediately seeks to EOF, processing only new lines after the watcher starts. wisphive_hook logs auto-approved calls to events.jsonl regardless of whether the daemon is currently ingesting. Auto-approved calls that happen while the daemon is down are never added to decision_log — silent audit gap.

Fix: run reimport_all once at daemon startup before seeking to EOF (existing dedup makes this safe). Alternative: persist and resume an offset, but startup reimport is simpler.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Write an auto-approved event to events.jsonl while daemon is stopped
- [ ] Start daemon; history contains the event without manual ReimportEvents
- [ ] No double-ingestion when ingester restarts mid-stream

E2E with the real daemon binary + temp HOME: event written while daemon stopped → 'startup reimport of events.jsonl backlog count=1' in daemon log and row present in decision_log (acceptance met, no manual ReimportEvents).

issue.title: Daemon: auto-approved PostToolUse results lost in ingest race
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #6).

ToolResult handling calls attach_tool_result. If no decision row exists yet, it logs 'no matching decision yet (may be pending ingest)' and drops the result. Auto-approved decisions are inserted asynchronously by the JSONL ingester. Fast tools can emit PostToolUse before the auto-approved row is ingested, permanently losing the tool result from history.

Fix: buffer unmatched tool results by tool_use_id with a short TTL and retry after ingest. Alternative: write auto-approved decision rows synchronously from the hook path before accepting result attachment.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] ToolResult arriving before ingest is eventually attached to the decision row
- [ ] Test: send ToolResult for a tool_use_id, then ingest_line, assert attachment
- [ ] TTL bound documented to prevent unbounded buffering

notes.content: Fixed in 0e7b7d9. attach_tool_result_with_retry retries on 250ms/1s/3s/10s schedule (~14s TTL, documented in code) in a detached task — no buffering map needed, memory bounded at one task per unmatched result. Exhaustion logs warn (was debug). Test tool_result_attaches_after_ingest_via_retry: attach misses pre-ingest, ingest_line lands mid-schedule, retry attaches, tool_result present on the history row (acceptance met).

issue.title: Daemon: TerminalSessionManager::close ignores `kill` flag
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/01-daemon-hook-cli.md (Medium #7) and docs/code_reivew/03-testing-ci-and-maintainability.md (Low - docs disagreement).

The protocol says TermClose { kill } can distinguish close behavior. TerminalSessionManager::close(&self, id, _kill) ignores the flag and always calls the child killer. `wisphive term close <id>` and `wisphive term close <id> --kill` behave the same. Users cannot request graceful close even though the CLI/protocol promise it.

Fix: implement graceful path (SIGHUP/SIGTERM with timeout, then SIGKILL) OR remove the flag from protocol+CLI so promise matches reality.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Terminal-manager test for kill=false asserts graceful behavior, OR the flag is removed from protocol/CLI
- [ ] Docs/code agree

notes.content: Wave 6 independent review reopened: forced status was set before confirmed SIGKILL, raw PID signaling raced waiter reaping/PID reuse, and tests missed the required TerminalSessionManager lifecycle path. Repair all three before close.

Nested repair review proved raw-PID force signaling remains unsafe under zombie and inherited SIGCHLD auto-reap semantics. Pivoted to the explicit alternate acceptance: remove the unsupported kill distinction from protocol/CLI and retain one honest close behavior.

issue.title: Web: Projects.tsx uses agent_count for live indicator instead of has_live_agents
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/02-web-frontend.md (Medium #2).

Rust ProjectSummary includes pending_count and has_live_agents and the daemon populates both before sending projects_response. The frontend ProjectSummary type omits both fields, and Projects.tsx uses p.agent_count > 0 to render the live/ended indicator. Any historical project with at least one past agent appears 'live' even when no agent is currently connected.

issue.title: Web: terminal replay/chunk handlers ignore Input and Resize directions
issue.context:
Source: docs/code_reivew/02-web-frontend.md (Medium - replay).

The protocol records TerminalDirection::Input, Output, and Resize. term_replay_chunk handling invokes the terminal handler only when msg.direction === 'output'; term_chunk similarly ignores live input and resize. Replay is unfaithful for sessions where input is not echoed by the shell or where resize events are needed to reproduce screen state.

Decide: full-fidelity replay (apply resize events; optionally render input) OR document replay as output-only and update protocol/UI labels accordingly.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Decision documented
- [ ] If full-fidelity: replay applies resize events to xterm; tests assert resize/write call sequence
- [ ] If output-only: docs/labels updated

issue.title: CLI: `daemon start` and `web serve` silently exit 0 when host is invalid
issue.context:
Source: docs/composers_code_review/cli-and-adapters.md (Critical+High - invalid host skips entire start).

In daemon start: web_requested = web || web_dev || host != '127.0.0.1' || port != 3100. If web_requested is true (e.g. --port 8080 or --web) and parse_host_octets returns None, the closure returns Ok(()) immediately and commands::daemon::start is never called. The daemon does not start; exit code is 0. Same pattern in serve_web (crates/wisphive_cli/src/main.rs:575). Stderr may say 'Invalid host address' but the success exit code is easy to miss in scripts/CI.

Fix: return a non-zero exit code on invalid host; OR fall back to starting the daemon without web. Never treat 'daemon start' as success when start was skipped.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] `wisphive daemon start --web --host bogus` exits non-zero
- [ ] `wisphive web serve --host bogus` exits non-zero
- [ ] Test asserts exit code
issue.close_reason: Reject invalid web bind hosts at Clap parsing with exit code 2; runtime parsing also propagates errors. Added regression tests for daemon start and web serve; full Rust gate green.

issue.title: Daemon/CLI: silent fallback on corrupt config files (auto-approve.json + user config.json)
issue.context:
Source: docs/composers_code_review/cli-and-adapters.md (Medium - user config silent fallback) and docs/composers_code_review/daemon-and-state.md (Medium - corrupt auto-approve.json).

auto-approve.json: serde_json::from_str(&content).unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({})) silently replaces config with {} on parse failure, and the rest of the function may rewrite the file — operators lose lists without an error. Same anti-pattern in user config.json (parse failure falls back to defaults silently — operators lose throttle/timeouts without noticing).

Fix: on parse failure, log loudly, refuse to write back over the user file, and either fail-closed (reject startup) or load defaults with a visible warning. Never silently overwrite a corrupted config.
issue.acceptance:
- [ ] Corrupt auto-approve.json: daemon logs error, does NOT overwrite the file
- [ ] Corrupt config.json: daemon logs error, does NOT silently use defaults; either refuses to start or surfaces a warning visible to the operator

issue.title: AuthProfile module + LocalLAN/Enterprise presets + GET /api/auth/profile
issue.context:
Introduce the `AuthProfile` abstraction that selects Wisphive's auth/security posture at startup. Precursor for #219 (WebAuthn handlers), which consumes the resulting `AuthPolicy` to drive RP ID derivation, UV requirement, login throttle, and sudo-on-enroll behavior. Also unblocks profile-aware gating in #271/#272/#220.

## Why

The plan doc (`docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md`) originally locked 'RP ID strategy C — per-origin credentials' as a single global posture. That decision silently breaks for the LAN-IP-origin phone case: WebAuthn forbids IP literals as RP IDs (Chrome and Safari both reject them), so 'per-origin' has no resolution on `https://192.168.1.42:8443`. Rather than picking a single strategy globally, the operator picks a *profile* that locks a coherent set of defaults. The profile makes the IP-RP-ID gap explicit instead of silent: LocalLAN says 'no passkey on LAN-IP origin' via an origin-aware endpoint; Enterprise requires a real domain and dodges the problem entirely.

Profiles also give us a clean QA axis — 'behavior X under profile Y' — instead of testing every knob combination ad-hoc.

## Scope

1. **New module** `crates/wisphive_web/src/auth_profile.rs`:
   - `enum AuthProfile { LocalLAN, Enterprise { rp_id: String, rp_origin: Url } }`
   - `struct AuthPolicy { allow_self_signed: bool, allow_ephemeral_lan_listener: bool, passkey_required: bool, uv_requirement: UvRequirement, challenge_ttl: Duration, login_throttle_threshold: u32, require_sudo_for_passkey_register: bool }` (plus an `rp_id_for_origin(origin: &Url) -> Option<RpId>` strategy function)
   - `enum UvRequirement { Required, Preferred, Discouraged }`
   - `impl AuthProfile { pub fn policy(&self) -> AuthPolicy { /* preset */ } }`

2. **CLI plumbing**: new flag `--auth-profile {local-lan|enterprise}` on `wisphive daemon start --web` and `wisphive web serve`. Default `local-lan`. Enterprise additionally requires `--tls-cert`, `--tls-key`, `--auth-rp-id`. Fail fast at startup if Enterprise is selected without all three; validate that `--auth-rp-id` is a registrable domain (not IP), is a suffix of a DNS SAN in the provided cert, and matches a configured allowed_origin.

3. **AppState wiring**: `AuthPolicy` threaded into `AppState` and `SecurityConfig::build` so downstream consumers (security gates, eventual WebAuthn handlers, pairing module) can branch on profile.

4. **New unauth endpoint** `GET /api/auth/profile` (request-origin-aware) returning:
```json
{
  "profile": "local-lan" | "enterprise",
  "can_enroll_passkey_on_this_origin": bool,
  "passkey_required": bool,
  "allow_ephemeral_listener": bool
}
```
Gated by the same Origin/Host allowlist as `/api/auth/status`; bearer not required. `can_enroll_passkey_on_this_origin` is computed via `policy.rp_id_for_origin(req_origin).is_some()` — under LocalLAN this returns `Some(RpId("localhost"))` for loopback origins and `None` for RFC1918 IP-literal origins; under Enterprise it always returns `Some(rp_id)`.

5. **Profile-switch detection**: on daemon startup, scan `web_passkeys` (if non-empty) and WARN-log any rows whose stored `rp_id` does not match the current profile's expected RP ID set. (Requires the `rp_id` column added in #219 PR-4 — see Note below.)

6. **Plan doc revision** `docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md`: add a new top-level 'Profiles' section that supersedes the standalone 'strategy C' lock; cross-reference this issue. Also fix the RP ID section to acknowledge that 'per-origin' has no resolution on IP literals, and that the resolution is profile-driven.

## Profile content matrix (LOCKED 2026-05-16)

| Knob | LocalLAN (default) | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| TLS | Self-signed OK | User-provided cert required |
| Phone passkey | **None** (device token only, issued at pairing) | Yes (real domain → RP ID works on phone) |
| Desktop passkey | Optional, skippable on first run | Optional, skippable on first run |
| Ephemeral LAN pairing listener | Enabled | **Disabled** (devices added via Devices.tsx + sudo) |
| Sudo gate on passkey-register | No | Yes |
| UV requirement | Preferred | Required |
| Resident keys (discoverable) | Required | Required |
| Challenge TTL | 5 min | 5 min |
| Login throttle threshold (fails before backoff) | 5 (existing) | 3 |
| RP ID derivation | `Some("localhost")` for loopback origin; `None` for RFC1918 IP-literal | Always `Some(--auth-rp-id)` |
| Webauthn instance lifecycle | Lazy + OnceCell cache keyed by (rp_id, rp_origin) | Same (single entry under Enterprise) |

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Per-knob env-var overrides (atomic profiles only in v1)
- A third 'Loopback' profile (LocalLAN covers desktop-only when pairing is never armed)
- Enterprise device-enroll flow (separate issue — depends on this + #220)
- Schema changes to `web_passkeys` (done in #219 PR-4)
- Login.tsx UI changes (done in #219 PR-5)

## Note for #219 PR-4

#219 PR-4 will add `aaguid TEXT` and `rp_id TEXT NOT NULL` columns to `web_passkeys` via migration. The `rp_id` column is what makes profile-switch detection (item 5) possible. This issue does NOT add columns; it only reads them if present.

## Test plan

- Unit: `AuthProfile::policy()` returns expected preset for each profile.
- Unit: `rp_id_for_origin` returns `None` for `192.168.1.42:8443` under LocalLAN; `Some("localhost")` for `http://127.0.0.1:3100`; `Some("localhost")` for `http://localhost:3100`; `Some(<rp_id>)` for any origin under Enterprise.
- Unit: Enterprise validation rejects missing `--auth-rp-id`, IP literal as RP ID, RP ID not in cert SAN.
- Integration: `GET /api/auth/profile` with loopback Origin returns `can_enroll=true`; with LAN-IP Origin returns `can_enroll=false` (LocalLAN); returns true for any Origin matching the cert (Enterprise).
- Integration: startup with mismatched `web_passkeys.rp_id` rows logs a WARN.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `crates/wisphive_web/src/auth_profile.rs` exists with the types and preset above.
- [ ] CLI flag `--auth-profile {local-lan|enterprise}` accepted on `daemon start` and `web serve`; defaults to `local-lan`; Enterprise validates `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`/`--auth-rp-id` at startup, fail-fast with clear error on missing/invalid.
- [ ] `AuthPolicy` threaded through `AppState` and `SecurityConfig::build`.
- [ ] `GET /api/auth/profile` returns origin-aware payload; documented in `docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md`.
- [ ] Profile-switch detection logs a WARN per mismatched row at startup.
- [ ] Plan doc updated: new 'Profiles' section supersedes single-strategy lock; IP-literal-RP-ID limitation explicit.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.

## Dependency on #270 (added 2026-05-16, review feedback)

Enterprise profile selection requires `--tls-cert` and `--tls-key` flags. **Those flags are owned by itr#270 (Stage 2a)** and are not in Sprint-1. This issue ships:

- The Enterprise *policy* (RP ID derivation, UV required, sudo on enroll, etc.)
- CLI flag `--auth-profile`
- CLI flag `--auth-rp-id`
- Fail-fast validation: if `--auth-profile enterprise` is selected and either (a) #270 has not yet shipped the `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key` flags, or (b) the flags exist but were not provided, error at startup with:

  > `Enterprise profile requires user-provided TLS cert (--tls-cert / --tls-key). Either ship itr#270 (Stage 2a) first or select --auth-profile local-lan.`

LocalLAN works fully independent of #270 — that’s the sprint goal. End-to-end Enterprise behavior is validated separately via itr#316 (Enterprise browser smoke) once both #310 and #270 have shipped.

Does **not** add `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key` flags itself; that’s #270’s scope.

Introduce the `AuthProfile` abstraction that selects Wisphive's auth/security posture at startup. Precursor for #219 (WebAuthn handlers), which consumes the resulting `AuthPolicy` to drive RP ID derivation, UV requirement, login throttle, and sudo-on-enroll behavior. Also unblocks profile-aware gating in #271/#272/#220.

## Why

The plan doc (`docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md`) originally locked 'RP ID strategy C — per-origin credentials' as a single global posture. That decision silently breaks for the LAN-IP-origin phone case: WebAuthn forbids IP literals as RP IDs (Chrome and Safari both reject them), so 'per-origin' has no resolution on `https://192.168.1.42:8443`. Rather than picking a single strategy globally, the operator picks a *profile* that locks a coherent set of defaults. The profile makes the IP-RP-ID gap explicit instead of silent: LocalLAN says 'no passkey on LAN-IP origin' via an origin-aware endpoint; Enterprise requires a real domain and dodges the problem entirely.

Profiles also give us a clean QA axis — 'behavior X under profile Y' — instead of testing every knob combination ad-hoc.

## Scope

1. **New module** `crates/wisphive_web/src/auth_profile.rs`:
   - `enum AuthProfile { LocalLAN, Enterprise { rp_id: String, rp_origin: Url } }`
   - `struct AuthPolicy { allow_self_signed: bool, allow_ephemeral_lan_listener: bool, passkey_required: bool, uv_requirement: UvRequirement, challenge_ttl: Duration, login_throttle_threshold: u32, require_sudo_for_passkey_register: bool }` (plus an `rp_id_for_origin(origin: &Url) -> Option<RpId>` strategy function)
   - `enum UvRequirement { Required, Preferred, Discouraged }`
   - `impl AuthProfile { pub fn policy(&self) -> AuthPolicy { /* preset */ } }`

2. **CLI plumbing**: new flag `--auth-profile {local-lan|enterprise}` on `wisphive daemon start --web` and `wisphive web serve`. Default `local-lan`. Enterprise additionally requires `--tls-cert`, `--tls-key`, `--auth-rp-id`. Fail fast at startup if Enterprise is selected without all three; validate that `--auth-rp-id` is a registrable domain (not IP), is a suffix of a DNS SAN in the provided cert, and matches a configured allowed_origin.

3. **AppState wiring**: `AuthPolicy` threaded into `AppState` and `SecurityConfig::build` so downstream consumers (security gates, eventual WebAuthn handlers, pairing module) can branch on profile.

4. **New unauth endpoint** `GET /api/auth/profile` (request-origin-aware) returning:
```json
{
  "profile": "local-lan" | "enterprise",
  "can_enroll_passkey_on_this_origin": bool,
  "passkey_required": bool,
  "allow_ephemeral_listener": bool
}
```
Gated by the same Origin/Host allowlist as `/api/auth/status`; bearer not required. `can_enroll_passkey_on_this_origin` is computed via `policy.rp_id_for_origin(req_origin).is_some()` — under LocalLAN this returns `Some(RpId("localhost"))` for loopback origins and `None` for RFC1918 IP-literal origins; under Enterprise it always returns `Some(rp_id)`.

5. **Profile-switch detection**: on daemon startup, scan `web_passkeys` (if non-empty) and WARN-log any rows whose stored `rp_id` does not match the current profile's expected RP ID set. (Requires the `rp_id` column added in #219 PR-4 — see Note below.)

6. **Plan doc revision** `docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md`: add a new top-level 'Profiles' section that supersedes the standalone 'strategy C' lock; cross-reference this issue. Also fix the RP ID section to acknowledge that 'per-origin' has no resolution on IP literals, and that the resolution is profile-driven.

## Profile content matrix (LOCKED 2026-05-16)

| Knob | LocalLAN (default) | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| TLS | Self-signed OK | User-provided cert required |
| Phone passkey | **None** (device token only, issued at pairing) | Yes (real domain → RP ID works on phone) |
| Desktop passkey | Optional, skippable on first run | Optional, skippable on first run |
| Ephemeral LAN pairing listener | Enabled | **Disabled** (devices added via Devices.tsx + sudo) |
| Sudo gate on passkey-register | No | Yes |
| UV requirement | Preferred | Required |
| Resident keys (discoverable) | Required | Required |
| Challenge TTL | 5 min | 5 min |
| Login throttle threshold (fails before backoff) | 5 (existing) | 3 |
| RP ID derivation | `Some("localhost")` for loopback origin; `None` for RFC1918 IP-literal | Always `Some(--auth-rp-id)` |
| Webauthn instance lifecycle | Lazy + OnceCell cache keyed by (rp_id, rp_origin) | Same (single entry under Enterprise) |

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Per-knob env-var overrides (atomic profiles only in v1)
- A third 'Loopback' profile (LocalLAN covers desktop-only when pairing is never armed)
- Enterprise device-enroll flow (separate issue — depends on this + #220)
- Schema changes to `web_passkeys` (done in #219 PR-4)
- Login.tsx UI changes (done in #219 PR-5)

## Note for #219 PR-4

#219 PR-4 will add `aaguid TEXT` and `rp_id TEXT NOT NULL` columns to `web_passkeys` via migration. The `rp_id` column is what makes profile-switch detection (item 5) possible. This issue does NOT add columns; it only reads them if present.

## Test plan

- Unit: `AuthProfile::policy()` returns expected preset for each profile.
- Unit: `rp_id_for_origin` returns `None` for `192.168.1.42:8443` under LocalLAN; `Some("localhost")` for `http://127.0.0.1:3100`; `Some("localhost")` for `http://localhost:3100`; `Some(<rp_id>)` for any origin under Enterprise.
- Unit: Enterprise validation rejects missing `--auth-rp-id`, IP literal as RP ID, RP ID not in cert SAN.
- Integration: `GET /api/auth/profile` with loopback Origin returns `can_enroll=true`; with LAN-IP Origin returns `can_enroll=false` (LocalLAN); returns true for any Origin matching the cert (Enterprise).
- Integration: startup with mismatched `web_passkeys.rp_id` rows logs a WARN.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `crates/wisphive_web/src/auth_profile.rs` exists with the types and preset above.
- [ ] CLI flag `--auth-profile {local-lan|enterprise}` accepted on `daemon start` and `web serve`; defaults to `local-lan`; Enterprise validates `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`/`--auth-rp-id` at startup, fail-fast with clear error on missing/invalid.
- [ ] `AuthPolicy` threaded through `AppState` and `SecurityConfig::build`.
- [ ] `GET /api/auth/profile` returns origin-aware payload; documented in `docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md`.
- [ ] Profile-switch detection logs a WARN per mismatched row at startup.
- [ ] Plan doc updated: new 'Profiles' section supersedes single-strategy lock; IP-literal-RP-ID limitation explicit.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.

issue.title: #219 PR-4: WebAuthn backend handlers (register/login start/finish) consuming AuthPolicy
issue.context:
Backend half of #219. Ship four WebAuthn HTTP handlers (register/login start/finish) consuming the `AuthPolicy` produced by the AuthProfile precursor. Drops the `TODO(webauthn)` at `crates/wisphive_web/src/auth.rs:17`.

## Why

#219 originally bundled backend + frontend in a single issue. Splitting per the plan doc (PR-4 = backend, PR-5 = frontend) makes review-sized PRs and lets the backend ship and stabilize before frontend integration.

## Scope

1. **New module** `crates/wisphive_web/src/passkey.rs` containing:
   - `webauthn_for(rp_id: &str, rp_origin: &Url) -> Arc<Webauthn>` with `OnceCell` cache keyed by `(rp_id, rp_origin)`. Built via `webauthn-rs::WebauthnBuilder::new(rp_id, rp_origin)?.build()?` with `user_verification_policy` from `AuthPolicy::uv_requirement` and `attestation = AttestationConveyancePreference::None`. Always require resident keys (discoverable credentials) via `require_resident_key(true)` on registration options.
   - `struct ChallengeStore { inner: Mutex<HashMap<String, ChallengeEntry>> }` with TTL eviction. `ChallengeEntry = { state: ChallengeState, created: Instant, expires: Instant }`. `enum ChallengeState { Register(PasskeyRegistration), Login(PasskeyAuthentication) }`. Key is opaque `session_id` (32 bytes random, base64url). Methods: `insert(state, ttl) -> session_id`, `take(session_id) -> Option<ChallengeState>`, `evict_expired()`. Background tokio task ticks `evict_expired` every 60s. Single-use semantics enforced by `take` (removes on read).

2. **Four routes** in `crates/wisphive_web/src/lib.rs::build_router`:
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/register/start` — bearer-gated; if `policy.require_sudo_for_passkey_register` also sudo-gated (reuse the sudo middleware used by `/api/devices/{id}/revoke`). Body empty. Resolves request Origin → calls `policy.rp_id_for_origin(origin)` — returns 400 with `{ error: "passkey_unavailable_on_this_origin" }` if `None`. Calls `webauthn.start_passkey_registration(user_id, user_name, user_display_name, exclude_credentials)` where `user_id` = current `device_id` (bytes of UUID), `exclude_credentials` = existing creds for this device. Stores `PasskeyRegistration` state in challenge store with policy TTL. Returns `{ session_id, public_key: CreationOptions }`.
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/register/finish` — bearer-gated (+ sudo if required). Body `{ session_id, credential: RegisterPublicKeyCredential }`. Loads state via `take(session_id)` → 400 on miss. Calls `webauthn.finish_passkey_registration(&credential, &state)`. On success, inserts row into `web_passkeys` (id = credential ID, device_id = current device, public_key = serialized COSE, sign_count, transports, **aaguid**, **rp_id**, created_at). Writes `web_audit` row `passkey_register`. Returns `{ credential_id, created_at }`.
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/login/start` — UNAUTH (no bearer); rate-limited via existing `LoginThrottle` (shared budget with password login). Body empty. Resolves request Origin → `policy.rp_id_for_origin(origin)` → 400 if `None`. Calls `webauthn.start_discoverable_authentication()` (NOT passkey-bound; we don't know which credential yet). Stores `DiscoverableAuthentication` state in challenge store. Returns `{ session_id, public_key: RequestOptions }` (empty `allowCredentials` — resident key discovery).
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/login/finish` — UNAUTH; rate-limited. Body `{ session_id, credential: PublicKeyCredential }`. Loads state via `take(session_id)`. Looks up credential ID in `web_passkeys` → resolves `device_id`. Loads stored `public_key` + `sign_count`. Calls `webauthn.finish_discoverable_authentication(&credential, &state, &[stored_passkey])`. On success: update `sign_count` + `last_used_at` in `web_passkeys`; issue new bearer token for `device_id` via existing token-rotation path; write `web_audit` row `passkey_login_success`. On failure: increment `LoginThrottle` for source IP; write `passkey_login_failure` audit row. Return `{ token }` on success, 401 on failure.

3. **Schema migration** in `crates/wisphive_daemon/src/state.rs`:
   - `ALTER TABLE web_passkeys ADD COLUMN aaguid TEXT` (nullable; some authenticators don't expose).
   - `ALTER TABLE web_passkeys ADD COLUMN rp_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` — default empty so the migration is non-destructive; new inserts populate. Profile-switch detection (in AuthProfile precursor) reads this column.
   - Update `insert_web_passkey` signature to take `aaguid: Option<&str>, rp_id: &str` and pass through.
   - Update `list_web_passkeys_for_device` to return new columns.

4. **Reuse existing infra**:
   - `LoginThrottle` for passkey-login rate limiting (shared with password).
   - Sudo middleware for register endpoints under Enterprise (don't reimplement).
   - `web_audit` for all four flows (passkey_register, passkey_register_failure, passkey_login_success, passkey_login_failure).

## Design decisions (LOCKED from /alignment session 2026-05-16)

- **Resident keys always required.** Modern authenticator support; enables single 'Login with passkey' button without username; clean fit for single-user model.
- **Webauthn instance lifecycle: lazy + OnceCell cache.** Built on first request for an origin, reused forever. Under Enterprise: one entry. Under LocalLAN: loopback only (LAN-IP returns None → no instance built).
- **Login flow uses opaque session_id.** Random 32-byte base64url. TTL from `policy.challenge_ttl` (default 5min). `take()` removes on read — single-use enforced by data structure.
- **Passkey-login throttle shares budget with password login.** Same `LoginThrottle` per source IP.
- **Enroll binds to current device.** No 'pick target device' flexibility in v1.
- **AAGUID stored but not surfaced in UI.** Future pretty-name feature.
- **Attestation None.** Privacy-preserving default; webauthn-rs default.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Frontend (any `*.tsx` changes) — that's PR-5 (sub-issue split from #219).
- Devices.tsx 'enroll another passkey' button + passkey list — entirely in #220.
- Enterprise operator-driven device-enroll flow — separate new issue (depends on this + AuthProfile + #220).
- `aaguid` UI surfacing.
- Cross-device passkey portability — see plan doc 'Profiles' section.

## Test plan

Automatable (mandatory for PR merge):
- Unit: ChallengeStore insert/take/evict; single-use semantics; TTL expiry.
- Unit: webauthn_for cache returns same Arc for same (rp_id, rp_origin); different instance for different keys.
- Integration: full register start/finish round-trip via webauthn-rs `SoftPasskey` test authenticator; assert row in `web_passkeys` with correct rp_id + aaguid; assert audit row.
- Integration: full login start/finish round-trip; assert token issued, sign_count incremented, last_used_at set, audit rows.
- Integration: replay attack — re-POST the same session_id to /finish → 400.
- Integration: register on LAN-IP origin under LocalLAN → 400 `passkey_unavailable_on_this_origin`.
- Integration: register without sudo under Enterprise → 403 from sudo middleware.
- Integration: failed login increments LoginThrottle (verify by triggering throttle threshold via password fails + 1 passkey fail).

Manual smoke (deferred to issue close — see #219 umbrella):
- Chrome / Firefox / Brave desktop register + login under LocalLAN.
- Chrome / Firefox desktop register + login under Enterprise (with mkcert local CA).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `crates/wisphive_web/src/passkey.rs` exists with `webauthn_for` + `ChallengeStore`.
- [ ] Four routes wired in `build_router` with correct gating per profile.
- [ ] Schema migration adds `aaguid` + `rp_id` columns; `insert_web_passkey` signature updated.
- [ ] All automatable tests above pass.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
- [ ] No frontend code touched.

## Handoff notes from #310 review (added 2026-05-16, sprint-1 wave-1)

#310 shipped and was reviewed by two parallel reviewers (security + code-quality). Both gave `ship-ready` verdicts. Below are the items #311 specifically inherits — re-read before writing code:

**Code-level hooks #310 left for #311:**

- **`scan_passkey_rp_id_drift` is one-line-deletable** but **keep the no-such-column tolerance during the migration window**. A half-merged migration must not crash the daemon. Delete the early-return branch only AFTER the column is fully added; leave the `is_missing_column_error` guard. (Stub currently lives at `crates/wisphive_web/src/auth_profile.rs:316-340`.)

- **`AuthPolicy::challenge_ttl` is plumbed but unused.** #311 must honor it consistently in BOTH the register ceremony AND the authenticate ceremony when building the webauthn-rs `RegisterCredentialOptions` / `AuthenticationOptions`. If only one path honors it, the lock is decorative.

- **`rp_id_for_origin → None` is a HARD CONTRACT meaning "passkey enrollment not possible on this origin," NOT "use a default."** Any handler that calls this and falls back to a hardcoded RP ID re-opens the silent-failure gap the abstraction was built to close. Return 400 `passkey_unavailable_on_this_origin` (per #311 spec).

- **No `OnceCell` cache hook for Webauthn instances exists yet.** #310 deliberately did not pre-build it — that's your job. Add a `OnceCell<HashMap<(RpId, Url), Arc<Webauthn>>>` either on `AppState` or as a method on `AuthPolicy`. Locked design says `webauthn_for(rp_id, rp_origin) -> Arc<Webauthn>` with lazy build + cache.

- **Enterprise `rp_origin` is currently derived as `https://{rp_id}`** in `resolve_auth_profile` (`crates/wisphive_cli/src/main.rs:646`). When #270 ships and lets the operator provide `--tls-cert`, the cert's primary SAN may not match this derivation. Add a `TODO(itr#270)` cross-reference in your webauthn-rs builder construction site so future maintainers know to revisit when #270 lands.

- **LocalLAN webauthn builder must use `https://localhost:<port>`** (NOT `https://127.0.0.1:<port>`) as the RP origin even when the request came in via `127.0.0.1`. Reason: `rp_id_for_origin` collapses all loopback origins to `Some("localhost")`, so the Webauthn builder's `rp_origin` must match (`localhost`-named) or webauthn-rs will reject the ceremony. Use the `RpId` value to drive `rp_origin` construction, not the request URL.

- **`passkey_required: false`** on BOTH profiles in v1. #311 should plumb but **not branch on it yet**. #313 (Enterprise device-enroll) is the flag-flipper.

- **`validate_enterprise_config` + `EnterpriseValidationError` are re-exported at `wisphive_web` crate root** (added by C/D/E review fixes). Use the short import path: `wisphive_web::validate_enterprise_config`, not `wisphive_web::auth_profile::validate_enterprise_config`.

- **`Url` is re-exported at `wisphive_web` crate root.** Use `wisphive_web::Url` from CLI; use the locally-imported `Url` from inside `wisphive_web`. Do NOT reach `webauthn_rs::prelude::Url` directly — that defeats the abstraction.

## Scope

1. **New module** `crates/wisphive_web/src/passkey.rs` containing:
   - `webauthn_for(rp_id: &str, rp_origin: &Url) -> Arc<Webauthn>` with `OnceCell` cache keyed by `(rp_id, rp_origin)`. Built via `webauthn-rs::WebauthnBuilder::new(rp_id, rp_origin)?.build()?` with `user_verification_policy` from `AuthPolicy::uv_requirement` and `attestation = AttestationConveyancePreference::None`. Always require resident keys (discoverable credentials) via `require_resident_key(true)` on registration options.
   - `struct ChallengeStore { inner: Mutex<HashMap<String, ChallengeEntry>> }` with TTL eviction. `ChallengeEntry = { state: ChallengeState, created: Instant, expires: Instant }`. `enum ChallengeState { Register(PasskeyRegistration), Login(PasskeyAuthentication) }`. Key is opaque `session_id` (32 bytes random, base64url). Methods: `insert(state, ttl) -> session_id`, `take(session_id) -> Option<ChallengeState>`, `evict_expired()`. Background tokio task ticks `evict_expired` every 60s. Single-use semantics enforced by `take` (removes on read).

2. **Four routes** in `crates/wisphive_web/src/lib.rs::build_router`:
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/register/start` — bearer-gated; if `policy.require_sudo_for_passkey_register` also sudo-gated (reuse the sudo middleware used by `/api/devices/{id}/revoke`). Body empty. Resolves request Origin → calls `policy.rp_id_for_origin(origin)` — returns 400 with `{ error: "passkey_unavailable_on_this_origin" }` if `None`. Calls `webauthn.start_passkey_registration(user_id, user_name, user_display_name, exclude_credentials)` where `user_id` = current `device_id` (bytes of UUID), `exclude_credentials` = existing creds for this device. Stores `PasskeyRegistration` state in challenge store with policy TTL. Returns `{ session_id, public_key: CreationOptions }`.
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/register/finish` — bearer-gated (+ sudo if required). Body `{ session_id, credential: RegisterPublicKeyCredential }`. Loads state via `take(session_id)` → 400 on miss. Calls `webauthn.finish_passkey_registration(&credential, &state)`. On success, inserts row into `web_passkeys` (id = credential ID, device_id = current device, public_key = serialized COSE, sign_count, transports, **aaguid**, **rp_id**, created_at). Writes `web_audit` row `passkey_register`. Returns `{ credential_id, created_at }`.
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/login/start` — UNAUTH (no bearer); rate-limited via existing `LoginThrottle` (shared budget with password login). Body empty. Resolves request Origin → `policy.rp_id_for_origin(origin)` → 400 if `None`. Calls `webauthn.start_discoverable_authentication()` (NOT passkey-bound; we don't know which credential yet). Stores `DiscoverableAuthentication` state in challenge store. Returns `{ session_id, public_key: RequestOptions }` (empty `allowCredentials` — resident key discovery).
   - `POST /api/auth/passkey/login/finish` — UNAUTH; rate-limited. Body `{ session_id, credential: PublicKeyCredential }`. Loads state via `take(session_id)`. Looks up credential ID in `web_passkeys` → resolves `device_id`. Loads stored `public_key` + `sign_count`. Calls `webauthn.finish_discoverable_authentication(&credential, &state, &[stored_passkey])`. On success: update `sign_count` + `last_used_at` in `web_passkeys`; issue new bearer token for `device_id` via existing token-rotation path; write `web_audit` row `passkey_login_success`. On failure: increment `LoginThrottle` for source IP; write `passkey_login_failure` audit row. Return `{ token }` on success, 401 on failure.

   - `ALTER TABLE web_passkeys ADD COLUMN aaguid TEXT` (nullable; some authenticators don't expose).

   - Update `insert_web_passkey` signature to take `aaguid: Option<&str>, rp_id: &str` and pass through.
   - Update `list_web_passkeys_for_device` to return new columns.

   - `LoginThrottle` for passkey-login rate limiting (shared with password).
   - Sudo middleware for register endpoints under Enterprise (don't reimplement).

- **Webauthn instance lifecycle: lazy + OnceCell cache.** Built on first request for an origin, reused forever. Under Enterprise: one entry. Under LocalLAN: loopback only (LAN-IP returns None → no instance built).

- Integration: register on LAN-IP origin under LocalLAN → 400 `passkey_unavailable_on_this_origin`.
- Integration: register without sudo under Enterprise → 403 from sudo middleware.
- Integration: failed login increments LoginThrottle (verify by triggering throttle threshold via password fails + 1 passkey fail).

Manual smoke (deferred to issue close — see #219 umbrella):

- Chrome / Firefox desktop register + login under Enterprise (with mkcert local CA).

## Handoff notes from #311 review (added 2026-05-17, sprint-1 wave-2)

#311 (backend) shipped with two parallel reviewers (security + code-quality). One MUST-FIX was caught and corrected in the review pass (M1 throttle-bypass via `/login/start`).
