issue.title: Auto-answer audit trail: record every non-human decision with the rule that made it
issue.context:
Command Center P0 (epic #396; spec werkit/command-center-spec.md §4). #380 stopped questions being swallowed, but there is still no record of WHAT gets auto-answered and BY WHICH layer/rule. During the 06-13/14 incident the operator debugged blind, repeatedly asking Claude to re-ask questions to probe config state.

Requirement: every decision resolved without a human — auto-approve tier match, auto_approve_add rule, tool_rules pattern, always-defer bypass under auto_approve_dangerous, Codex-path resolution, event toggles (auto_approve_stop/user_prompt/etc.) — emits an audit event: {ts, project, session_id, agent, tool, decision, decided_by: <layer/rule identifier>, config_snapshot_hash}. Human-made decisions are recorded too (decided_by: human) so the stream is complete.

Consumers: (1) CLI query (e.g. wisphive audit --since 1h --project X), (2) the Command Center inbox's 'auto-answered' feed (wisphive#TBD, Layer 1), (3) postmortems. Storage: daemon event store; must survive daemon restart; subject to existing retention knobs.
issue.acceptance: Behavioral: reproduce an auto-approved Bash call and an always-defer question at level=all — CLI query shows both events with correct decided_by (the tier/rule name for the first, 'always_ask deferral' + eventual human answer for the second). Config-change events include the snapshot hash so a policy weakening is correlatable. Runtime evidence (real session, not fixtures) attached on close. Docs updated.

issue.title: Waiting-on-you inbox: one queue of every human-blocked decision across all sessions + auto-answer audit feed
issue.context: Spec §5.1 — the centerpiece. One aggregated queue across all projects/sessions of everything blocked on the human: AskUserQuestion/Elicitation (question text + options), PermissionRequest items in the daemon decision queue, ExitPlanMode approvals. Each item: project · session · agent · age · the actual question · answer affordance (respond in-console where the protocol allows — ClientMessage::Ask is already wired; otherwise deep-link/focus the owning session). Below the queue: the auto-answer audit feed from #397 (what was decided WITHOUT you and by which rule). Explicit empty state: '0 waiting · N auto-answered in last hour (view)'. Evidence: operator is the approval bottleneck by design (dozens of one-word proceed gates); the 06-13/14 invisible-prompt incident cost an afternoon across 4 projects. Depends on #396 (trust) and #397 (audit feed). Open question per spec §11.1: in-console answering scope — resolve during implementation, deep-link is an acceptable v1 fallback for AskUserQuestion.
issue.acceptance: Runtime: with 2+ concurrent real sessions, a live AskUserQuestion and a PermissionRequest both appear in the queue within seconds, are answerable (in-console or via deep-link), and the session receives the answer. Auto-answered events appear in the feed with the deciding rule. Aging items are visually ordered. Screenshot evidence attached on close (spec §10).

issue.title: Working-tree strip: per-repo dirty summary, pre-generated conventional commit, per-change agent attribution

issue.title: config.json writers race: concurrent read-modify-writes lose updates (no cross-process lock)
issue.context: Found in review of the itr#358/#360/#361 cluster. Three unsynchronized read-modify-write writers on ~/.wisphive/config.json: daemon persist_auto_approve (spawn_blocking), web put_config (read→merge→write_config_atomic), CLI load_for_write→save. Atomic tmp+rename prevents corruption but not lost updates: two hooks resolving 'Always Allow' simultaneously on different tools each read the same base, both write, last rename wins — one tool's auto_approve_add entry silently vanishes and that tool queues forever. Same race between a web PUT and a TUI Always Allow. The repo already uses flock for web.cert.lock (tls.rs) — same pattern fits: take an flock on e.g. ~/.wisphive/config.json.lock around read→mutate→rename in update_config_json and route ALL three writers through it (web put_config and CLI save currently bypass update_config_json).
issue.acceptance: All config.json writers (daemon persist_auto_approve, web put_config, CLI save) serialize through a shared flock-guarded read-modify-write in wisphive_daemon::config. A test spawns N concurrent update_config_json calls adding distinct tools and asserts all N land.

issue.title: Web config merge-patch cannot delete a single tool_rules entry (nested null 400s)
issue.context: Review finding on itr#358. validate_config_json exempts only TOP-LEVEL nulls (merge-patch deletion); a nested deletion like {"tool_rules":{"Bash":null}} fails the HashMap<String,ToolRule> deserialization and returns 400, so a single tool rule cannot be deleted via the patch API — only all of tool_rules at once. Fails closed and no current client sends it, but will bite when the SPA gains tool-rules editing. Fix: validate tool_rules entries individually, treating null as deletion.
issue.acceptance: PUT /api/config with {"tool_rules":{"Bash":null}} returns 200 and removes only the Bash rule; other rules survive. Test covers it.

issue.title: TUI gets no feedback when 'Always Allow' persistence fails (refusal only in daemon logs)
issue.context: Review finding on itr#360. When config.json is corrupt (or auto_approve_add is wrong-typed), persist_auto_approve correctly refuses — but the only signal is a daemon-side warn!. The TUI user who pressed '!' sees the modal close as if it stuck; meanwhile the hook (treating corrupt config as absent) reads the legacy file the daemon refuses to fall back to when config.json exists. Fail-safe direction, but the refusal should reach the human: send an Error/notice ServerMessage back to the resolving TUI client so it can toast/banner it.

issue.context: Deferred from itr#297. issue.title: Spec hardening: policy-learning security invariants (adversarial pass)
issue.context: The policy-learning engine mines decision_log to suggest/auto-apply auto-approve rules — which makes it the mechanism by which a compromised or sloppy agent could widen its own permissions. The plan doc needs an adversarial pass that pins the invariants before any implementation: what may NEVER be learned (always-defer set, deny patterns, dangerous posture), what evidence counts toward a rule and its poisoning resistance, human-confirm gates for rule promotion, and rollback/audit of learned rules.

issue.title: decided_by: distinguish human:individual from human:bulk resolutions
issue.context: Required by ADR-0005 I4 (two asks). (1) Distinguish bulk from individual human resolutions: today decided_by is human:tui / human:web:<id> and does not encode bulk-vs-individual — the learning engine may only count individually-reviewed decisions as evidence. (2) ingest_line must reject/relabel any decided_by copied from events.jsonl that begins 'human:' or 'timeout:' — an agent can append a line with a forged operator attribution, and although it lands as auto_approved=1 (so it is excluded from learning by the column), the forged human:* label would otherwise surface in 'wisphive audit'. Note I4/I7 share the decided_by field: one string must encode resolver AND bulk/individual (e.g. human:tui:individual) — pick a grammar both invariants agree on.

issue.title: webauthn-rs residentKey:'discouraged' enrolls credentials that cannot log in (security-key path)
issue.context: Empirically confirmed by the itr#416 e2e spec (e2e/passkey.spec.ts): webauthn-rs 0.5 hard-codes require_resident_key(false), serialized as residentKey:'discouraged' in /register/start. The CDP virtual authenticator honored the hint and minted a non-resident credential (isResidentCredential:false) that the discoverable-only login route can never find — the spec works around it by rewriting residentKey→'required' via page.route, emulating real platform authenticators (which ignore the hint). Consequence: any authenticator that honors 'discouraged' (typically security keys) enrolls a passkey that silently can never log in. The deviation note at the top of passkey.rs predicted this; now proven at runtime.
issue.acceptance: Either the registration ceremony requests residentKey:'required' server-side (patched webauthn-rs config, response post-processing, or crate upgrade if 0.6+ exposes it), or the login path supports non-discoverable credentials (allowCredentials list). The page.route workaround in e2e/passkey.spec.ts is then removed and the spec still passes without it. Decision + rationale noted in passkey.rs header.

issue.title: e2e boot helpers: handle spawn 'error' event (EACCES/ENOENT race)
issue.context: Codex review of the Sprint 0 harness (confirmed against code). Both boot helpers only await the child 'exit' event. If the wisphive binary is non-executable (EACCES) or vanishes after the existsSync guard (post-check race), Node emits 'error' with child.pid undefined and 'exit' never fires: the readiness loop spins the full 30s before throwing, and the unhandled 'error' event throws an uncaught exception in the Playwright worker. Pre-existing from itr#414/#415.
issue.acceptance: Both helpers register child.once('error', ...) that rejects the ready wait immediately with the spawn error (and triggers cleanup), so a bad/non-executable binary fails fast with a clear message instead of a 30s spin + uncaught worker exception. A test or manual repro (chmod -x the binary) confirms the fast, clean failure.

issue.title: Sprint-2: Command Center Layer 1 — Waiting-on-you inbox
issue.context:
**Sprint Goal:** Deliver the Waiting-on-you inbox so that every human-blocked decision across all concurrent sessions — plus the auto-answered audit feed — surfaces in one answerable web queue, eliminating invisible-prompt debugging.

Implements the Phase 3 centerpiece (itr#399) under Command Center Layer 1 (itr#398). Scope = inbox-only (option A), chosen for highest chance of success over a wider full-Layer-1 sprint.

## Non-Goals
- Agent liveness board / working-tree strip / burn meter (#400/#401/#402 — later Phase 3 sprints)
- Any Phase 5 work: Devices UI #220, scrollback, mobile pairing
- Steering controls (start/stop/retarget agents) — spec §5 locks Layer 1 to state-mirror, not steering-wheel
- Reworking the existing History view (audit stays there; feed is live+recent only)
- In-console answering of always-deferred tools (AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode) — deferred to its own epic + ADR

## Definition of Done (sprint-level, appended to every story)
- cargo test --workspace green; cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all -- --check no diff
- just frontend-lint clean; just frontend-test (vitest) green
- User-visible increment exercised against a REAL running session (spec §10) — screenshot/driven-flow evidence in the closing itr note
- Docs updated when user-facing behavior changes (CLAUDE.md web surface / new ServerMessage / new route)

## Key design boundary (ADR-0002)
AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode / Elicitation are always-deferred at the hook and never reach the daemon decision queue (ADR-0002). The inbox surfaces them from the events.jsonl stream with a deep-link/focus-session affordance; in-console approve/deny applies only to daemon-queued PermissionRequest items. #399 AC explicitly allows "in-console OR via deep-link", so this satisfies the AC without reversing the locked always-defer semantics.

issue.title: Stream auto-answered + deferred audit events to web/TUI clients live
issue.context:
**Why:** The inbox's auto-answer feed (S3) and its deferred waiting-on-you rows (S4) have no live data path — `event_ingest::run_ingest` writes auto-answered/deferred records to SQLite `decision_log` only and never gets `tui_tx`, so nothing reaches the browser live. This is the load-bearing backend gap the whole inbox depends on.

**What:** Give `run_ingest` the `tui_tx` broadcast handle. Add a `ServerMessage::AuditDecision` variant carrying { kind: auto_approved|deferred|denied, decided_by, project, agent_id, terminal_session_id, tool_name, ts }. Broadcast it on each ingested line (in `ingest_line`). On client connect (`handle_tui`), send a bounded recent-audit snapshot (last hour or last N, capped) so the 'N auto-answered in last hour' count renders immediately without waiting for the next live event. Mirror `decided_by` + the new `AuditDecision` type onto `protocol.ts` (the TS `HistoryEntry` currently drops `decided_by`).

**Notes:** Must not perturb the existing `queue_snapshot`/`new_decision`/`decision_resolved` flow. Redaction is already applied upstream (itr#89) — do not put cleartext secrets on the wire. `run_ingest` currently takes only `state_db`; thread `tui_tx` in from `Server::new`.
issue.acceptance:
- A gated auto-approved tool call (e.g. Read under auto_approve_level) produces a ServerMessage::AuditDecision broadcast to connected web/TUI clients within the ingest tick, carrying decided_by (e.g. level:all), project, agent_id, tool_name.
- A deferred tool call (AskUserQuestion) produces an AuditDecision with kind=deferred and decided_by=always_ask:intrinsic.
- On connect, a client receives a bounded recent-audit snapshot (<= configurable cap) sufficient to compute the last-hour auto-answered count.
- protocol.ts exposes the new message + decided_by with no `any`.
- Existing queue_snapshot/new_decision/decision_resolved flow is unchanged (regression test or manual check).
- No cleartext secret added to the wire (redaction preserved).

issue.title: Runtime evidence + close #399: dynamic smoke test of the inbox against 2+ real sessions
issue.context:
**Why:** Spec §10 requires the inbox to be exercised end-to-end against a REAL running session (not fixtures), demonstrating a live AskUserQuestion appearing + answered; itr#399 closes only with attached evidence. This is the gating evidence story.

**What:** Run the inbox against 2+ concurrent real agent sessions in different projects. Append a dated item to `docs/smoke/CHECKLIST.md` (Phase 3 / Command Center section) with the pass/fail + oracle below. Capture screenshots / driven-flow, attach to the itr#399 close note. File any bug found during smoke into itr AT THE TIME (do not defer).

The queue content is non-deterministic (live sessions), so correctness is judged by INVARIANTS + a CLI oracle, not exact values.
issue.acceptance:
SETUP: daemon + web up; 2 real agent sessions in 2 distinct projects.

PASS requires ALL of:
1. A gated decision in session A appears as an Inbox row within ~5s, labeled project A · that agent · a live-incrementing age; approving in-console unblocks the agent (observe it proceed) AND clears the row.
2. An AskUserQuestion in session B appears within ~5s as a deferred waiting-on-you row with question text + a deep-link; the deep-link focuses session B's terminal (or shows the go-to-terminal pointer for hook-only sessions).
3. An auto-approved action appears in the feed with its decided_by rule shown.
4. With the queue drained, the header reads `0 waiting · N auto-answered in last hour (view)` with N>0.
5. Items from the two projects are visually distinguishable.

FAIL if ANY of: a gated decision never surfaces within ~5s; the age is static/absent; project/session/agent label missing or wrong; in-console approve doesn't unblock the agent or the row doesn't clear; deferred item missing its deep-link or focuses the wrong session; an auto-answered event shows without its decided_by rule; empty-state lacks the auto-answered count.

ORACLE (correctness on non-deterministic live data): cross-check each Inbox/feed entry against `wisphive audit --since 10m` — every row's project/agent/decided_by must match an audit record, and the empty-state N must equal the auto-answered count from `wisphive audit` for the window (+/- streaming lag). Any mismatch = FAIL and a bug filed in itr at the time.

CLOSE: screenshots of the three states + the audit cross-check attached to the itr#399 close note; the checklist item recorded in docs/smoke/CHECKLIST.md; itr#399 closed.

issue.title: EPIC: In-console remote answering of AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode (reverses always-defer for remote answer)
issue.context:
Surfaced during Sprint-2 inbox planning (epic itr#433, feature itr#399).

Deferred decision tools (AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode / Elicitation) are always-deferred at the hook (ADR-0002) and answered ONLY via the agent's native prompt. The Sprint-2 inbox surfaces them with a deep-link/focus-session affordance instead of answering them in-console.

To answer them from the web console remotely, an answer-return path must carry the selected option back through the hook to the agent — a significant change to the decision plane and a reversal of the locked always-defer semantics.

**REQUIRES a new ADR** (supersede or extend ADR-0002) defining the remote-answer contract and its trust model BEFORE any implementation. This item is an epic because it would blow up any sprint it is dropped into unscoped.
issue.acceptance:
- A new ADR is proposed and accepted defining: how a remotely-selected AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode answer returns to the agent through the hook, the trust/auth model for remote answering, and how it coexists with (or supersedes) ADR-0002 always-defer.
- A design spike sizes the hook answer-return path (protocol changes, blocking semantics, failure modes).
- Decompose into stories once the ADR is accepted.

notes.content:
SPIKE RESULT — GO (decisive). Empirical probe (pure-logging hook, scratchpad/hook-probe/probe.log + probe-raw.jsonl) proves Claude Code fires PostToolUse when a deferred native prompt is answered, and it is a USABLE resolution signal:
- ExitPlanMode: PreToolUse+PermissionRequest @04:18:33 -> PostToolUse @04:19:01 (28s = human deciding).
- AskUserQuestion: PreToolUse+PermissionRequest @04:19:35 -> PostToolUse @04:19:39; tool_response contains answers:{<question>:<chosen option>} — the literal selection.
- PostToolUse carries the SAME tool_use_id as the PreToolUse that created the deferred row (exact correlation, no heuristics).

Surprise finding: the correlation infra ALREADY EXISTS end-to-end.
- Hook installs PostToolUse (empty matcher = all tools) via CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENTS (project_audit.rs:5). On PostToolUse the hook sends ClientMessage::ToolResult{tool_use_id, tool_result,...} to the daemon (wisphive_hook main.rs:1233).
- deferred record already carries tool_use_id (main.rs:826); decision_log persists it under a UNIQUE index (migrate.rs:200).
- Daemon already correlates: attach_tool_result SELECT ... WHERE tool_use_id=? AND tool_result IS NULL then UPDATE SET tool_result (state/decisions.rs:300-359). So the deferred row ALREADY gets the answer stamped onto it today — an 'ask' row with non-NULL tool_result IS an answered deferral. It is just never broadcast or surfaced.

Latency/reliability: exact tool_use_id match has NO time bound (only fuzzy fallback is 10min), so slow human answers still correlate. attach_tool_result_with_retry covers the ingest race.

issue.title: Terminal area cannot be scrolled on mobile web
issue.context: On mobile web (touch viewport), touching and dragging inside an open terminal session does not scroll the xterm.js viewport back through scrollback. xterm.js's viewport relies on mouse wheel events for scrolling and its own touch handling only covers tap-to-position-cursor / text selection gestures in some builds — it does not translate a vertical touch-drag into a scrollback scroll the way a normal overflow:auto div would. Neither TerminalView.tsx nor the surrounding .terminals-terminal-slot/.terminals-main CSS (app.css ~1594-1636) sets a touch-action or adds a touch-to-scroll handler, so on a phone/tablet browser there is currently no way to review scrollback in a live terminal — only the newest visible rows are reachable.
issue.acceptance: On a touch device (real phone or Chrome DevTools mobile emulation with touch enabled), open the Terminals view, attach to a session with scrollback beyond one screen, and vertical-drag inside the terminal pane. Content scrolls to reveal earlier scrollback lines, and normal terminal interaction (tap-to-focus, on-screen keyboard input) still works afterward.
issue.close_reason: Native capture-phase touch listeners on the terminal mount translate a vertical drag into .xterm-viewport scrollTop changes (commit dcc287c). Verified by TerminalView.test.tsx (real xterm mount, driven touchstart/touchmove asserts viewport scrollTop moves + tap threshold respected); tsc -b + 100 vitest pass + prod build clean. Real-hardware touch feel parked on docs/smoke/CHECKLIST.md 'Terminal touch-to-scroll on a real phone/tablet'.

notes.content: CORRECTION: first close (dcc287c) was premature — that fix wrote .xterm-viewport.scrollTop, a no-op in xterm 6 (custom Monaco scrollable, not native overflow viewport); the jsdom test passed vacuously. Real fix 3f3544a drives public term.scrollLines(). Verified in real Chromium against built xterm 6: downward drag moved visible top LINE_087→LINE_067 through scrollback, reverse drag returned to tail, sub-threshold tap did not scroll (tap-to-focus preserved). Rebuilt frontend + reinstalled binary. Real-hardware touch-feel still parked on smoke checklist.

VERIFIED FIX (real-app test, not jsdom): isolated daemon+web over TLS, real PTY terminal, scrollback generated live while attached, CDP touch through the real input pipeline. Result — fresh terminal WITH scrollback: wheel SCROLL, touch SCROLL (top row 372->362). The scrollLines custom handler (commit ac99e7e) IS required: xterm 6's own touch Gesture does NOT scroll this build (only the wheel path works, and it routes through scrollLines). Prior removal (3dabce0) was reverted. NOTE: 'scrolling breaks after switching terminals' is NOT this bug — on re-attach the WHEEL is stuck too because catchup restores only the current screen, no scrollback. That is itr#284.

issue.title: Spike: native Android app mirroring the web UI (DEFERRED — revisit late)
issue.context:
DEFERRED — do NOT pick up now. Revisit only after much more of the program is complete (post phone-pairing epic itr#283, and after the mobile-web/PWA path has been exercised). Filed to capture the assessment so it is not re-derived.

## Question
How hard is a native Android app that mirrors the web UI but with much better mobile focus?

## Assessment (2026-07-04)
Technically MODERATE, not hard — the client/server contract is clean and fully portable. Rough v1 effort ~4-7 weeks single-dev, ~1/3 of that is the terminal.

### Why it is portable
- Nearly all app data flows over ONE WebSocket (/ws) as enumerable JSON. HTTP /api/* is only auth + config.
- Entire wire protocol already lives in one typed file: crates/wisphive_web/frontend/src/types/protocol.ts -> maps ~1:1 to Kotlin data classes (kotlinx.serialization).
- Client state machine is essentially one hook: useWisphive.ts (~591 lines) — reconnect, notifications, terminal-handler registry, sudo-reauth replay. That is the porting spec.
- Phone auth is a per-device BEARER token (Authorization: Bearer for HTTP, ?token= for WS; native can use a header for both). Skip WebAuthn/passkeys — on LAN IPs the RP ID is None so passkeys are disabled anyway.
- Native wins for free: OS-native push (vs passive banners), background socket, biometric unlock, native touch, offline snapshot.

### Hard parts
1. Terminal: web uses xterm.js; Android has no drop-in. Wire an Android VT emulator to base64 term_chunk (out) / term_input (in) frames. Biggest cost + main jank risk.
2. BACKEND BLOCKER: the phone pairing path does not exist yet. No /api/pair/* route, no pairing-token issuance, no ephemeral LAN listener/QR (itr#271/#272 unshipped, epic itr#283). A native app authenticates THROUGH that path. Foundations (TLS certs, per-device bearer schema, set-password) are landed.
3. Two clients forever: every protocol change ships in TS AND Kotlin.

### Recommendation / pushback
Project own plan (docs/plan-mobile-device-pairing.md) deliberately chose a responsive web PWA over LAN pairing, NOT native. The web is only bad on mobile today because the planned mobile work is unbuilt (no PWA manifest/service worker; responsive CSS is just two @media blocks). Cheapest path to "much better mobile focus":
1. Finish itr#283 (pairing + bearer issuance) — needed for ANY phone client.
2. Mobile-first responsive pass + PWA manifest/service worker (installable, offline snapshot, Web Push on Android Chrome) — most of the win at ~1/3 cost, zero second codebase.
Native only clearly wins if native-push reliability, background socket survival, or native terminal feel prove insufficient AFTER the PWA path ships. Revisit this spike then.
issue.acceptance: Reopened only after itr#283 + the PWA/mobile-web path are shipped and evaluated; decision recorded (build native vs. stay on responsive PWA) with rationale.

issue.title: Spike: per-project 'fleet cockpit' — surface itr/kgr/plr/ccq/gatr signals in the project view
issue.context:
SPIKE (exploratory). Prototype + decide the contract before committing to the full build; this will likely spawn an epic + per-tool fleet-side issues.

## Goal
Turn the flat per-project card in the dashboard Projects view into a "fleet cockpit" that surfaces, per project, all the signals we currently only get by shelling out to CLIs inside a skill: open/next itr issue counts, kgr graph health, ccq session stats, last gatr gate result, open sprint, latest handoff — plus a "save this prompt to plr" action.

## Signals to surface (per project)
- itr: open / ready / blocked counts + oldest_open (`itr stats -f json`), and the next issue (`itr next -f json`). Per-repo db.
- kgr: file/symbol counts, cycles, orphans, rule violations, heaviest files (`kgr check -f json`, `kgr query --heaviest -f json`). Per-repo scan.
- gatr: last verify-gate result — exit code, duration, errors/warnings, tag ("is the gate green?"). `gatr last` (per-project keyed logs).
- ccq: session/corpus rollup for the project — sessions, prompts, tool errors, recurring error signatures (`ccq stats`, `ccq errors --count`), scoped by project.
- plr: ACTION — "save a prompt from history to plr": pick a recent human prompt (via ccq) and persist it as a plr prompt for reuse.
- sprint: is there an open sprint? Read `<project>/sprint/CURRENT` -> folder + plan.md (Goal, Epic itr#, DoD).
- handoff: latest dated file under `<project>/docs/handoff/`.

## Grounding (current architecture)
- A "project" is NOT a stored entity: no projects table. It is an absolute filesystem PATH synthesized on demand by StateDb::query_projects() (crates/wisphive_daemon/src/state/summaries.rs) from decision_log GROUP BY project, enriched in-memory in server.rs (QueryProjects handler) with live-agent + pending counts. ProjectSummary.project is that path.
- The path is already used as a cwd: process_registry::spawn_agent does cmd.current_dir(&project). So it is directly usable to run fleet CLIs. Caveat: not validated to be a git/repo root; a project with no decision history + no live agent does not appear at all.
- Web (ws_bridge.rs) is a transparent JSON relay (8 MiB line cap); the daemon answers queries from SQLite + in-memory registries and NEVER shells out for data today. Closest subprocess patterns: PTY terminals (terminal.rs) and spawn_agent (sets cwd but Stdio::null()s stdout). A cockpit needs a subprocess that CAPTURES stdout.
- Frontend ProjectSummary TS type (types/protocol.ts) is already missing pending_count/has_live_agents the Rust struct sends — fix that parity gap as part of this.
- Sprint/handoff are pure on-disk conventions (no DB rep): detect via <project>/sprint/CURRENT and <project>/docs/handoff/.

## Proposed approach (to validate in the spike)
1. New daemon message pair, e.g. ClientMessage::ProbeFleet { project, tools?: [..] } -> ServerMessage::FleetSnapshot { project, itr, kgr, gatr, ccq, sprint, handoff, errors }. The daemon — NOT the browser — runs a FIXED allowlist of fleet commands (never user-supplied argv) with cwd=project, captures stdout, parses JSON, returns a typed snapshot. Model the subprocess on process_registry but pipe stdout instead of null.
2. Cost/caching: kgr scan (and ccq over a big corpus) can be slow; itr/gatr are fast. Do NOT run all 5 synchronously on every Projects load. Options to weigh: lazy per-card expansion, TTL cache in the daemon, background refresh with a stale marker, or a fast-tier (itr/gatr/sprint/handoff, cheap) shown eagerly + a slow-tier (kgr/ccq) on demand.
3. Security (this is a gate — treat the cockpit as an escalation surface): fixed command allowlist only; canonicalize/validate the cwd; read-only by default; the one write path (plr save) needs explicit confirmation. Enforce per-command timeouts, output-size caps (reuse the 8 MiB line-cap discipline), and concurrency limits. Run ccq output through the wisphive_protocol::redact scrubber before surfacing/persisting so a captured prompt/bash line cannot leak a secret into plr or the UI. Consider an ADR since "daemon shells out to host CLIs, triggered from the web UI" is a non-obvious trust decision.

## Fleet-side additions (WE OWN THE FLEET — add commands rather than parse-hack)
- gatr: add `gatr last --format json` (structured: exit, dur_ms, errors, warnings, tag, log path). Currently text-only.
- ccq: add `--format json` to `stats` and `errors`; support scoping a query by a real filesystem PATH (map path -> ccq project) instead of only the encoded project name.
- plr: add a save-from-stdin path (e.g. `plr new --from-stdin --name ...`) so the dashboard can persist a captured prompt without writing a temp file.
- kgr: add a one-shot `kgr stats` summary (file count, symbol count, #cycles, #orphans, #violations, top heaviest) so the cockpit needs ONE call instead of check+query+symbols.
- itr: already has `-f json` for stats/next/ready — confirm the shapes cover counts + next-issue; add project-scoping only if a single itr db ever spans dirs (it does not today).
These may become issues in each tool own tracker; the spike decides which are actually required for v1.

## Open questions
- Do we key the cockpit on the decision-derived project path, or introduce a real projects table (with validated repo root, git remote, etc.) so projects with no decisions still appear? Latter is a bigger change but fixes the "invisible until first decision" gap.
- Multi-project performance: dashboards may list 20+ projects; a fleet probe per project is expensive — cache strategy is the crux.
- Where does plr "local/project" scope resolve relative to a probed project vs the daemon host?
issue.acceptance: Spike output: a working prototype that renders at least the fast-tier signals (itr counts + gatr last + open sprint) on a project card via a new daemon ProbeFleet message; a decided contract for the FleetSnapshot message; a caching/security model recorded (ADR if warranted); and a concrete list of which fleet-side JSON/stdin additions v1 requires. Then file the follow-on epic + fleet-tool issues.

notes.content:
DESIGN REFINEMENT (owner steer): make the fleet stats commands accept an explicit target DIRECTORY instead of relying on cwd — this removes most of the daemon-side hoops.

- Add `--dir <path>` (target-directory) to each fleet stats command so a single stateless invocation targets any project: `itr stats --dir <path> -f json`, `gatr last --dir <path> --format json`, `ccq stats --dir <path> --format json`, and kgr already takes a PATH positional (`kgr stats <path>`). plr save resolves its scope relative to the passed dir too.
- Daemon impact: the ProbeFleet subprocess no longer needs cmd.current_dir() / cwd canonicalization gymnastics — it runs from a stable daemon cwd and passes the project path as an ARG. Smaller trust surface (path is an explicit, validated argument, not ambient cwd), simpler code, no reliance on the tool discovering its repo by walking up from cwd.
- BATCH FORM is the real win for the caching/perf crux: let the stats commands take MULTIPLE dirs (`itr stats --dir a --dir b ...` -> one JSON object keyed by dir). Then the whole dashboard (20+ projects) is a handful of batched calls instead of projects x tools fan-out — the fast-tier (itr/gatr/sprint) can refresh in one shot per tool.
- Net: this supersedes the per-project cwd-subprocess model in the body as the PREFERRED approach. Update the "Proposed approach" + "Fleet-side additions" sections during the spike accordingly; the `--dir` (and multi-dir batch) flags become the concrete fleet-side asks.

issue.title: Deferred deep-link silently no-ops for a stale / non-embedded terminal session
issue.context:
Surfaced in the Sprint-2 review verification of itr#437.

The deferred-item 'Focus terminal' deep-link (App.tsx focusTerminalId -> Terminals.tsx) works when the deferred item's terminal_session_id is in the live `terminals` list. If it isn't (a stale session, or a hook-only session that was mislabeled with a terminal id), the Terminals focus effect (Terminals.tsx:159-166) silently no-ops: the view switches to Terminals but nothing is selected and onFocusHandled is never called. Graceful degradation, but the user gets a dead click with no feedback.

follows-up: itr#437
issue.acceptance:
- Clicking 'Focus terminal' for a deferred item whose terminal_session_id is not in the live terminal list gives visible feedback (toast / inline note) rather than a silent no-op.
- onFocusHandled is still called (or the pending focus is cleared) so state doesn't leak.
- Covered by a vitest for the stale-session branch.
issue.close_reason: Still-live (itr#464 only drops rows for observed-disconnected agents; a stale/mislabeled terminal_session_id on a live or never-registered session still rendered a dead Focus-terminal click). Fixed in b9daa0c: Terminals.tsx focus effect now bounds the wait (FOCUS_WAIT_MS=2s, deadline anchored in a ref so terminal-list churn can't extend it); on expiry it renders a dismissible inline notice (role=status, styled after the alert banners, top of sidebar so it's visible in the mobile list-only state) and still fires onFocusHandled so the pending focus clears. Proven by test-first: stale-branch vitest failed on pre-fix code (no notice, no ack), green after. 4 new tests: happy path immediate attach+ack+no notice; stale -> notice+ack+dismiss; late arrival within window attaches with no notice and abandoned timer never fires; deadline anchored across unrelated list updates. Frontend suite 237/237 green, eslint+tsc clean. e2e skipped: no routing/nav change (edge-case inline notice only).

issue.title: Add the e2e suite to the per-story verify gate for stories changing a default view / routing / nav
issue.context:
Sprint-2 retro action item (root cause of itr#446).

#435 made the Inbox the default web view, which broke e2e specs (core-flows.spec.ts, smoke.spec.ts) that asserted the old default .queue-layout. The per-story blitz verify gate is `cargo test + clippy + fmt + frontend-lint + frontend-test(vitest)` — it does NOT include the Playwright e2e suite, so the regression wasn't caught until the Wave 3 full-e2e run. A default-view / routing / nav change is exactly the class of change vitest can't catch but e2e can.

Why: catch view/routing regressions at story-close, not at end-of-sprint.
issue.acceptance:
- The verify gate (or blitz per-story gate) runs `just e2e` for stories that touch default view / routing / nav (or e2e runs before closing any web-view story).
- Documented in CLAUDE.md / justfile so future sprints inherit it.
- A story that changes the default view cannot close green while the e2e suite is red.

issue.title: Plan-time AC-contradiction check across dependent data->UI stories
issue.context:
Sprint-2 retro action item (root cause of the Wave 2.5 mid-blitz wire change).

#434 (data layer) AC deliberately EXCLUDED tool_input from the AuditDecision wire (leanness + redaction). #437 (UI) AC REQUIRED showing the deferred question text — which needs tool_input on the wire. The contradiction wasn't caught at /sprint plan time, so it surfaced mid-blitz as a stop-and-report and forced an unplanned Wave 2.5 protocol change + a PO decision.

- /sprint alignment gains a check: for each data->UI dependency edge, verify no field the producer AC excludes is required by the consumer AC.
- Documented as a /sprint alignment step (or STORY_STYLE note).
- Retro-tested against this sprint's #434/#437 case as the worked example.

issue.title: SPIKE: does Claude Code fire ANY hook for ExitPlanMode/AskUserQuestion? (deferred inbox rows never populate in real use)
issue.context:
ROOT-CAUSE SPIKE surfaced by real-use observation during Sprint-2 close: a live ExitPlanMode plan-approval ('Ready to code? / Would you like to proceed?') did NOT appear as a deferred inbox row (itr#437). Investigation of the real daemon shows WHY:

EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE (real ~/.wisphive, session cc-20cf1f47…):
- 242 PreToolUse hook invocations logged this session: Bash/Read/Edit/Write/Agent — but ZERO ExitPlanMode, AskUserQuestion, or EnterPlanMode of ANY event kind.
- ZERO 'deferred' records in events.jsonl, ever (grep -c = 0). No DEFER rows in 'wisphive audit'.
- PermissionRequest hook_event_name has NEVER fired despite being registered; PreToolUse matcher is '' (all tools).
- Hook IS current+active (auto_approved records carry decided_by=level:all + config_hash; installed binaries dated 02:39 today).

DESIGN vs REALITY GAP:
- The always-defer classifier (main.rs:~826-857, itr#380/#388, ADR-0002, unconditional since bab33dd) is WRITTEN to return Decision::Ask AND log a 'deferred' events.jsonl record for the DEFAULT_ALWAYS_ASK set (AskUserQuestion/EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode/Elicitation), for both PreToolUse and PermissionRequest — the record that #437's deferred inbox rows consume.
- The revert da85733 (reverting 3d42aa7's transcript plan-extraction) explicitly rescoped itr#399 to 'the deferral-event feed + deep-link mechanism' — i.e. the whole plan/question inbox rests on that 'deferred' record existing.
- BUT the record is NEVER produced in real use, because Claude Code apparently never invokes the wisphive hook for these tools at all. So itr#437's deferred rows will be perpetually empty for real plan-mode/AskUserQuestion prompts. NOT a rendering bug (itr#438 e2e proved the render path by feeding the hook a synthetic AskUserQuestion PreToolUse on stdin — a fidelity gap: real Claude Code doesn't deliver it that way).

SPIKE QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE:
1. Does current Claude Code fire PreToolUse for ExitPlanMode? For AskUserQuestion? (docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks) Or is plan approval a client-side flow with no external hook?
2. Does PermissionRequest fire for these — and only when the native permission dialog would show (suppressed by the Bash/Edit/Write allowlist wisphive installs)? If so, does wisphive's PermissionRequest registration actually receive them?
3. Is Elicitation the real carrier for any of these?
4. If NO hook observes them: is transcript-file watching (~/.claude transcript JSONL, the reverted 3d42aa7 approach) the only route? Reconcile with ADR-0002 (defer must not auto-resolve the native prompt).

DECISION THIS SPIKE FEEDS: is the fix (a) a hook matcher/registration change, (b) a PermissionRequest-based capture, or (c) transcript-watching (reverted route, needs a new ADR)? Relates to itr#399/#437/#439/#440. Deliverable: a findings note + a recommended path (and whether #437's deferred-row feature should be flagged as non-functional-in-practice until the capture lands).
issue.close_reason: Resolved via controlled logging-hook probe + deterministic wisphive-hook test. ExitPlanMode AND AskUserQuestion DO fire PreToolUse+PermissionRequest in current Claude Code; wisphive (PreToolUse matcher '') defers+logs them as 'deferred' records that the inbox renders (itr#438 chain). Root cause of the observed miss: the screenshotted session's project (controller) had no wisphive hooks installed — an ungated session, not a wisphive bug. Fix is operational: 'wisphive hooks install' in that project. Earlier docs-research 'no hook surface' conclusion retracted; itr#437 non-functional flag retracted.

notes.content:
AUTHORITATIVE HOOK-DOCS FINDINGS (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks + hooks-guide, dated 2026-07-04) + local config check:

1. ExitPlanMode is NOT a PreToolUse tool-hook. Docs route it through the PermissionRequest EVENT with matcher 'ExitPlanMode' (the guide's canonical example auto-approves it there). wisphive already registers PermissionRequest with matcher='' (ALL tools) — so registration is NOT the gap. Yet PermissionRequest fired ZERO times in a 242-PreToolUse session.

2. PermissionRequest only fires when a permission DIALOG would actually appear. It is SUPPRESSED in acceptEdits/auto/bypassPermissions and non-interactive (-p) modes, and when a permission rule already auto-approves the tool. So an auto-accepting agent session legitimately sees zero PermissionRequest events. This is the leading explanation for the zero-fire — NOT a matcher bug.

3. AskUserQuestion has NO documented hook surface of any kind (absent from the 30-event lifecycle table). EnterPlanMode likewise. => transcript-file watching (~/.claude *.jsonl) is the ONLY route to observe these — exactly the reverted 3d42aa7 approach.

4. Elicitation fires only for MCP-server input requests (matcher = MCP server name); NOT the carrier for AskUserQuestion/plan mode.

REFINED CONCLUSION / RECOMMENDED PATH:
- AskUserQuestion + EnterPlanMode: option (c) transcript-watching — genuinely no hook surface. Needs a new ADR reconciling with ADR-0002 (surface/deep-link only; must NOT auto-resolve the native prompt). This is the reverted route.
- ExitPlanMode: option (a/b) hinges on ONE unresolved empirical question the spike must still answer with a hands-on probe: does the ExitPlanMode PermissionRequest actually fire in a NORMAL interactive session, or does the current plan-approval UI ('Ready to code? / use auto mode / Ultraplan', plan saved to ~/.claude/plans/*.md) bypass hooks entirely? PROBE: install a trivial logging PermissionRequest hook (matcher '') in a scratch project, run a real interactive (non-auto) Claude Code session to plan mode, and check whether the hook fires. If it fires -> wisphive ALREADY captures+defers+logs it (deferred record) whenever the session isn't in an auto/bypass mode; the 'fix' is mode-awareness/docs, not code, and the inbox will populate in interactive sessions. If it does NOT fire -> the newer plan flow bypasses hooks and ExitPlanMode ALSO needs transcript-watching.

IMPACT FLAG for itr#437: the deferred-inbox rows are non-functional for AskUserQuestion/EnterPlanMode in real use today (no hook produces the record), and for ExitPlanMode only in interactive (dialog-showing) modes at best. The itr#438 e2e proved the RENDER path via a synthetic AskUserQuestion PreToolUse on stdin — it does not reflect real Claude Code delivery. Recommend a UX/doc note on #437 until this spike lands.

RESOLVED by controlled probe (2026-07-04) — the docs-research conclusion was WRONG; empirical ground truth:

PROBE (pure logging hook on all events, real interactive Claude Code session):
- ExitPlanMode fires BOTH PreToolUse AND PermissionRequest (+ PostToolUse).
- AskUserQuestion fires BOTH PreToolUse AND PermissionRequest (+ PostToolUse).
So these tools DO have a hook surface (PreToolUse, matcher '' catches them). The claim that they are absent from the hook lifecycle / transcript-watch-only is FALSE for current Claude Code.

DETERMINISTIC CONFIRM (real wisphive-hook, isolated HOME, mode=active): feeding an ExitPlanMode PreToolUse and an AskUserQuestion PreToolUse each produced a 'deferred' events.jsonl record with decided_by=always_ask:intrinsic. Combined with the itr#438 e2e (daemon ingest -> inbox render), the deferred-inbox chain WORKS end-to-end for real plan-mode/AskUserQuestion.

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE of the observed 'plan mode didnt hit Inbox': the screenshotted session was the /Users/josefaguilar/AI_Projects/controller project, which has NO wisphive hooks installed (no .claude/settings.json). Ungated session -> no hook -> no deferred record -> nothing in the inbox. The earlier 'zero deferred records' evidence was confounded: the sessions that used these tools (controller 849cb1c7; wisphive 79be48c7 had 0 total records) were not wisphive-gated. NOT a bug in the inbox (itr#437) or the hook.

FIX (operational, not code): run 'wisphive hooks install' in projects where plan-mode/AskUserQuestion sessions run (e.g. controller). Then deferred rows populate.

RETRACTION of the earlier IMPACT FLAG on itr#437: the feature is NOT non-functional in real use — it functions in any gated project. 

MINOR FOLLOW-UP (optional, low pri): the always-defer path logs a deferred record for BOTH the PreToolUse and the PermissionRequest firing of the same tool, so one plan prompt may yield two deferred rows momentarily — cosmetic dedup opportunity, not a defect. Spike questions answered; closing.

issue.title: Cockpit hook-gating: install/repair wisphive hooks into a project from the web UI (one-click)
issue.context:
Problem (surfaced by spike itr#459): un-gated projects silently produce nothing in the inbox, and are invisible in the cockpit Projects view (which is built from agent activity that only flows once hooks are installed). Make gating a one-click cockpit affair.

THREE PARTS:
1. Path-to-gate input in the web UI — type/paste a directory, one click runs 'hooks install' into it. Solves the invisible-un-gated-project case (e.g. controller) that per-project buttons can't reach.
2. Hook-status badges on the Projects view (Gated / Not gated / Needs repair) reusing 'wisphive projects audit' (hook mode + missing_events), with a one-click Gate/Repair per row.
3. Backend: new ClientMessage::InstallHooks { project } -> daemon runs the install logic (lift the CLI hooks-install into a shared fn) -> returns fresh project hook audit so badges update live.

SECURITY (approved): the action writes .claude/settings.json into a filesystem path from the web (possibly LAN) = a capability bump. Gate behind the EXISTING sudo-reauth modal (same as approving Bash/Edit) AND confirm-before-write showing exactly what will be added. Free-form path allowed (option a) but sudo-gated + confirmation preview.

NOTES: installed hook command points at the stable ~/.cargo/bin/wisphive-hook path, so this is 'gate/repair a project', NOT 'refresh the binary'. Reuse audit_project/HookMode/CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENTS. issue.title: Codex managed spawn is ungated AND fails to launch (broken exec flags + no hook trust)
issue.context:
Probe 2026-07-04 (this session) proved daemon-spawned Codex is a security regression, not just incomplete. Two blockers at one fix site (process_registry.rs:97-122 Codex arm): 1) BROKEN LAUNCH: daemon builds 'codex exec --ask-for-approval never --sandbox workspace-write -C

'. codex-cli 0.142.5 rejects it: 'error: unexpected argument --ask-for-approval found' (that flag is not a codex EXEC flag). Spawn dies at arg-parse; no codex process survives (pgrep confirms none, registry empty). 2) UNGATED EXECUTION (the real hole): Codex silently SKIPS untrusted hooks. Empirically: 'codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -C ' with NO persisted hook trust -> command executed successfully, 0 wisphive-hook events fired = fully ungated. Same command WITH --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -> wisphive hook fired (PreToolUse+Stop events logged, agent_type=codex). Codex requires persisted per-hook trust (~/.codex/config.toml [hooks.state] trusted_hash), established interactively via /hooks; the daemon spawn establishes none and passes no bypass -> a Wisphive-spawned Codex agent runs COMPLETELY UNGATED while appearing managed. Also: codex exec refuses non-git dirs ('Not inside a trusted directory') without --skip-git-repo-check. Trust-hash reverse-engineering into the user's global config.toml is brittle/version-specific; --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust is the documented path for automation that vets its own hook source (the daemon installs the hook). Must be gated by a fail-closed check that the wisphive codex hook is actually present, else bypassing trust on an unhooked project is still ungated.

Runtime proof: spawn Codex via the daemon into a wisphive-hooked project and observe a codex-authored PreToolUse decision reach the gate/audit (the exact event that produced 0 records today). just verify green.

issue.title: CLI agent commands can misread interleaved broadcast events (Tui client subscribes to firehose)
issue.context: itr#468 review (P2-C). send_and_recv connects as ClientType::Tui, so handle_tui's select! interleaves BROADCAST events (AgentExited/AgentConnected/DeferredResolved/DiskAlert/decision events) onto the same socket as the direct command reply, nondeterministic order. is_connect_snapshot skips only the 3 connect snapshots, not broadcasts. A concurrent AgentExited{other} while awaiting a stop reply is the SAME variant as the reply -> misreport. Pre-existing (old fixed-count drain was strictly worse); itr#468 did not introduce it. Proper fix: request/response correlation id, or a one-shot CLI client type not subscribed to broadcasts.
issue.acceptance: CLI agent start/list/stop return their own reply even when unrelated agent lifecycle/decision broadcasts arrive concurrently. Approach: correlation id on ClientMessage/ServerMessage, or a non-subscribed CLI client kind. Test: drive a spawn/stop while emitting a concurrent broadcast and assert the correct reply is returned.

issue.title: Codex --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust runs ALL project hooks headlessly, not just Wisphive's
issue.context: itr#467 review (P2-B + P3 TOCTOU). The managed Codex spawn passes --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, which suppresses Codex's interactive trust gate for EVERY hook in the merged .codex/hooks.json (install_codex merges, does not own the file). The itr#467 guard only verifies the Wisphive PreToolUse hook is PRESENT, not that other/foreign hook commands are absent or vetted. Spawning into a cloned/untrusted repo that ships its own .codex hooks runs them headlessly under the agent env. Also TOCTOU: guard reads hooks.json at check time, codex re-reads ms later at exec; a swap could remove the real hook after the check. Documented as an open sub-question in docs/plan-loop-supervisor.md.
issue.acceptance: Either (a) refuse/warn! loudly when the target .codex/hooks.json contains any non-wisphive-hook command before bypassing trust, or (b) provision per-hook trust (write [hooks.state] trusted_hash for ONLY the wisphive hook) instead of the blanket bypass. TOCTOU: pin a content hash of hooks.json across check->spawn. Test covers a project with a foreign hook + wisphive hook.
issue.close_reason: Fixed in 13ed8e5. Managed Codex spawn now detects non-Wisphive hook commands in the project's .codex/hooks.json (hook_install::codex_foreign_hook_commands, strict wisphive-hook matcher across all events/rules), always warn!s what --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust would run headlessly, and REFUSES the spawn unless codex_allow_foreign_hooks=true (new config.json key, default false, captured at daemon start, threaded into ProcessRegistry). Design: kept the trust bypass for reliable gating; rejected per-hook trust-hash provisioning (codex-version-brittle, a hash mismatch would silently un-gate; codex exec has no --hooks-file override). RUNTIME-PROVEN via isolated daemon on the real CLI->daemon path: spawn into a project carrying /usr/bin/evil-third-party.sh is refused by default (error names the foreign hook + the opt-in); setting codex_allow_foreign_hooks=true + restart lets it proceed (Agent started, PID assigned) — proving the flag flips behavior live. Tests: codex_spawn_refuses_foreign_hooks_without_opt_in, foreign_hooks_{empty_for_wisphive_only,lists_non_wisphive_across_all_events,dedupes,empty_when_missing_or_malformed}, codex_allow_foreign_hooks_loads_from_config_json. verify fmt/clippy/rust green. RESIDUAL (accepted, not fixed): TOCTOU between the guard's read and codex's re-read of hooks.json is uncloseable without codex honoring a pinned hash — same trust boundary (project-dir owner controls the file).

issue.title: Create itr issues from inside Wisphive
issue.context:
Operators reviewing agent activity in the Wisphive TUI/web UI can't turn what they see into tracked work without leaving the app. Wisphive already knows a project's cwd and can detect whether itr is available for that project (an .itr.db exists / itr is on PATH). Add a first-class 'new issue' affordance that shells out to (or wraps) itr add so decisions, denials, and observations become tracked issues without a context switch.

Should degrade gracefully: the affordance is only shown when itr is available for the active project; hidden otherwise (same gating the bonus history button will reuse). Fits the itr#448 'fleet cockpit' direction of surfacing itr/kgr/plr/ccq/gatr signals in the project view.
issue.acceptance:
- A 'new issue' action exists in the Wisphive UI (TUI and/or web) that creates an itr issue in the active project.
- Form/flow captures at least title + body; ideally priority and kind.
- The action is shown ONLY when itr is available for the active project; hidden when it is not (no dead button).
- On success the created issue ID is surfaced back to the user; on failure the error is shown, not swallowed.
- Runs against the project's own .itr.db (correct cwd), attributed appropriately (e.g. ITR_AGENT).

notes.content: DEPENDENCY on itr itself: for Wisphive to create/update issues across the fleet, itr must accept an explicit DB directory/path (e.g. a --db <path> or ITR_DB env) rather than relying solely on cwd discovery. Wisphive is a control plane over many projects at once and won't chdir per call, so it needs to point itr at each project's .itr.db directly to add/update/close issues on that project's behalf. This unlocks deeper fleet integration — surfacing and mutating per-project itr state from the central TUI/web view (ties into itr#448 fleet cockpit).

issue.title: Upstream(itr): accept explicit --db path / ITR_DB for a control plane addressing many project DBs
issue.context:
UPSTREAM dependency on the itr tool (not the Wisphive codebase). Blocks itr#474/#475.

itr currently resolves its database via cwd discovery (walk up for .itr.db). Wisphive is a control plane sitting over many projects at once and won't chdir per invocation, so it can't reliably target a given project's tracker. itr needs to accept an explicit database location so a caller can point it at any project's .itr.db directly for add/update/close/get.

Two accepted forms: a --db <path> flag (accepting either a .itr.db file or a directory containing one) and/or an ITR_DB env var, with a clear precedence (explicit flag > ITR_DB > cwd discovery). This is the primitive that unlocks deeper fleet integration — surfacing and mutating per-project itr state from Wisphive's central TUI/web view (itr#448 fleet cockpit).

- --db accepts both a .itr.db file path and a directory containing one.
- Precedence defined and documented: explicit flag > ITR_DB env > cwd discovery.
- Works for the read/write verbs Wisphive needs: add, update, get/list, close, note.
- A missing/invalid path fails with a clear error (not silent fallback to cwd).
- agent-info / docs updated to describe the option.

issue.title: Web: terminal touch-scroll accumulator tracks requested not realized rows — boundary gesture glitch
issue.context: Surfaced by /crossfire-review (codex lane) of the itr#445 touch-scroll handler (commit ac99e7e). In crates/wisphive_web/frontend/src/components/TerminalView.tsx:150-154 the handler sets appliedRows = targetRows after term.scrollLines(delta), but scrollLines clamps at top-of-history and the live tail. The accumulator records REQUESTED rows, not REALIZED scroll, so at a clamp boundary it desyncs from the viewport: a drag at the live tail requests positive rows that do not move the viewport, then a small reversal (finger still above the start point) computes a negative delta and scrolls into history — content moves opposite the finger / dead-zones at boundaries. The mock-based vitest cannot catch it (the mock never clamps).
issue.acceptance: - A touch-drag that overscrolls at the live tail or top-of-history, then reverses, moves content in the same direction as the finger with no dead-zone or jump (verified against a live terminal with scrollback via real/CDP touch). - Handler accumulates realized scroll (read term.buffer.active.viewportY before/after, or reset the gesture anchor on clamp) rather than requested rows. - A regression test with real scrollback exercises a boundary reversal.
issue.close_reason: Fixed in commit 9bb2520: replaced the requested-row accumulator with absolute positioning — anchor = term.buffer.active.viewportY at touchstart, each move commands term.scrollToLine(anchor + offsetRows); xterm clamps internally so no cumulative state can desync at a boundary. Unit test adds a boundary-reversal case asserting the reversal lands on the absolute line (-20 then -5, no drift). Re-verified in real app: touch still scrolls a live terminal 372->362. Real boundary-clamp behavior with scrollback tracked by itr#479 (committed regression).

issue.title: Session transcript view for hooked sessions (incl. claude -p) via transcript_path ingestion
issue.context:
Give hooked Claude Code sessions — interactive AND `claude -p` (headless/print) — a rich "Session Transcript" view: user turns + assistant text + tool_use + tool_result woven into one timeline, stitched to wisphive's own approve/deny decision per tool_use_id.

CONFIRMED FACTS (empirically verified 2026-07, Claude Code 2.1.201):
- `claude -p` fires PreToolUse hooks identically to interactive — even under `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` (bypass skips native prompts, NOT hooks). So `-p` tool calls are already gated and already appear in the decision queue/audit.
- The hook already receives `transcript_path` for `-p`, pointing to Claude's session JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/<munged-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl — the SAME artifact format as interactive (records: user / assistant / tool_use / tool_result / ...). Partial during the session, final at SessionEnd.
- wisphive already reads this file today, but narrowly — only to extract plan text for ExitPlanMode (wisphive_hook/src/main.rs:1775). transcript_path is otherwise consumed in-process and dropped.

WHY ITS OWN SECTION: interactive sessions (when wisphive owns the PTY) are a LIVE-attachable byte stream; `-p` is ephemeral, non-attachable, complete-at-exit. So `-p`'s view is a post-hoc STRUCTURED replay of the JSONL, not a terminal you can attach to. Same conversation model, different affordances.

DISTINCT FROM #284: that epic is PTY vt100 scrollback (raw bytes). This is conversation-JSONL ingestion + a structured transcript model. Complementary, not overlapping.

DESIGN SKETCH:
- Plumb transcript_path from hook into DecisionRequest/event (today dropped in-process).
- Daemon tails/ingests the JSONL (append-only; hook SessionEnd for the finalized file) into a normalized conversation model.

issue.title: Web UI: explicit "fit to my window" resize control — stop passive pane resizes from mutating the shared PTY
issue.context:
Source: terminal-viewer design exploration session 2026-07-05 (per-client view options; user reports views "look broken or missing text").

Every web TerminalView auto-resizes the shared PTY: FitAddon + a ResizeObserver call fit() and send term_resize on mount and on every container/window resize (TerminalView.tsx:56-98, useWisphive.ts:648-653). The daemon applies it with no ownership/arbitration check (server.rs:1833-1844) — one shared PTY geometry, last resize wins. With multiple attached clients (second browser, phone, TUI), passive viewers silently fight over the PTY winsize; the child re-renders for whichever client resized last and everyone else sees corrupted output. The TUI never sends resizes at all — it passively adopts server cols/rows on TermCatchup — so in practice web clients are the aggressors.

Fix (first half of the resize pair; companion issue handles peers reacting to Resize frames):
- Make the ResizeObserver→term_resize path opt-in instead of automatic — merely viewing a session must never mutate the PTY.
- Add an explicit per-client "fit to my window" button in the terminal view that sends term_resize with the current pane's cols/rows — a deliberate, visible geometry take-over.
- No wire changes: ClientMessage::TermResize (wire.rs:227) already carries what's needed.
issue.acceptance:
- With two browser clients attached to one session, resizing one browser window emits no term_resize (verify via ws trace or daemon log) and does not disturb the other client's rendering.
- A "fit to my window" control is visible in the terminal view; clicking it sends term_resize with the pane's current cols/rows and the PTY adopts them (child app re-renders at the new size).
- Runtime evidence per STORY_STYLE: Playwright/CDP drive of the two-client flow with screenshots, not just green vitest.
- Existing single-client UX still gets a correctly sized terminal on create (TermCreate cols/rows from the creating pane remains).

issue.title: Web UI: apply broadcast Resize frames to the local xterm — peers currently render at stale geometry and corrupt
issue.context:
Source: terminal-viewer design exploration session 2026-07-05. Second half of the resize pair (see companion "fit to my window" issue).

The daemon already broadcasts a TermFrame with direction=Resize and payload "{cols},{rows}" on every PTY resize (terminal.rs:353-365), but the web client filters incoming frames to direction==="output" only (useWisphive.ts:289-322) and TerminalView's handler only distinguishes chunk/catchup/replay_chunk (TerminalView.tsx:70-76). So when another client resizes the shared PTY, the local xterm keeps its old cols/rows while the child renders for the new geometry — this is the observed "view looks broken / missing text" failure. The TUI has the same gap (tui.rs:388-435 feeds Output only) but only corrects on the next TermCatchup.

Fix: handle Resize-direction frames in the web client — resize the local xterm to the announced PTY cols/rows so rendering stays coherent (letterbox/scroll the excess when the pane is smaller; tmux-style clip/pad is the model). No wire changes needed.

Related: itr#305 (replay path ignores Input and Resize directions — same blind spot on the replay side; a shared resize-frame handler could serve both).
issue.acceptance:
- Two clients attached: client A resizes the PTY (via the explicit control or term_resize); client B's xterm reshapes to the announced cols/rows and continues rendering without garbling — verified in a real two-client CDP/Playwright run with screenshots.
- Resize payload parsing ("{cols},{rows}") covered by a unit test, including a malformed-payload case that must not throw in the reducer.
- No regression to the itr#284 catchup path: TermCatchup still seeds geometry on attach.

issue.title: Terminal session export: asciinema .cast + plain-text transcript from terminal_events
issue.context:
Source: terminal-viewer design exploration session 2026-07-05 ("can we transcribe a session from a captured log?").

The recording already exists and is complete: terminal_events persists every Input/Output/Resize event as raw bytes with ts_us + seq (reader thread terminal.rs:470-528, batcher terminal.rs:531-580, schema migrate.rs:148-168), and TermReplay already streams it from SQLite (server.rs:1917-1962). Export is a read-model over existing data:

- **.cast (asciinema v2)**: near-mechanical mapping — header from terminal_sessions meta (cols/rows/started_at), then [t, "o", data] per Output row (t from ts_us deltas); resize events map to asciinema resize markers. Playable/scrubbable artifact.
- **Plain-text transcript**: feed Output bytes through an offline vt100::Parser constructed WITH scrollback (the daemon's scrollback=0 memory bound doesn't apply offline), applying recorded Resize rows via set_size for fidelity (same blind spot as itr#305), then dump screen+scrollback contents. Clean for shell scrollback; inherently fuzzy for full-screen apps (vim/TUIs) — the .cast format is the honest artifact there.

Suggested surface: wisphive term export <id> --format cast|txt [--out FILE], reusing the TermReplay wire path (from_seq=0) or a direct DB read.

Constraints:
- **Blocked by itr#98**: TermReplay has no authorization — any client can stream any session's full byte history (typed sudo passwords, cat'd keys). An export feature makes bulk exfiltration one command; authz + replay audit-logging should land first.
- Retention deadline: prune_terminal_events deletes events for ended sessions older than retention_max_age_days (default 30) — export docs must state the window.
- Related: itr#483 (Claude session transcripts via transcript_path) is a different data source; keep surfaces distinct.
issue.acceptance:
- wisphive term export <id> --format cast produces a spec-valid asciinema v2 file that plays in asciinema-player, including at least one mid-session resize.
- --format txt produces a transcript whose content matches a driven shell session (commands + output present, ordering preserved), with Resize rows applied to the offline parser.
- Export requests are refused/audited per the itr#98 authz model (issue remains blocked until #98 lands).
- Docs note the retention window (retention_max_age_days, default 30 days after session end) as the export deadline.

issue.title: Web devices bypass terminal replay ACL through live attach and control
issue.context: TermReplay authorizes a requester against TerminalSessionMeta.created_by/replay_acl, but all other live terminal commands bypass that check. Any authenticated web device receives every session from TermList, can use the exposed UUID in TermAttach to receive the current PTY screen, and can send TermInput/TermResize/TermClose/TermSetGroup/TermReorder for any live session. This defeats the per-session protection introduced by itr#98: a non-owner device token can read secrets still visible on a live screen, execute arbitrary commands in another device's shell, or kill it without a reauth or ACL check.
issue.acceptance: The daemon applies a single documented ownership/ACL policy before all live terminal read/mutation paths: TermList (filter or redact inaccessible rows), TermAttach, TermInput, TermResize, TermClose, TermSetGroup, and TermReorder. A web requester that is neither creator nor in the explicit ACL receives TermError before any snapshot, live output, input write, resize, kill, or metadata mutation; local TUI behavior is explicitly preserved/tested. Integration tests use two distinct web device identities and prove device B cannot list sensitive metadata, attach, inject bytes, resize, or kill device A's session, while the owner/ACL path still works.

issue.title: Reject bearer tokens in API query strings
issue.context: security.rs extract_presented_token() accepts ?token= for every path, not only /ws. Because path_requires_device_token() covers all /api/*, a valid device bearer can be placed in a GET URL and then leak through browser history, reverse-proxy/access logs, Referer propagation, screenshots, and copied links. The comments say query form is needed for WebSocket upgrades, but the implementation applies it to ordinary API requests too. Keep query-token authentication scoped to /ws (or explicitly opt-in), and require Authorization: Bearer for HTTP API routes; add regression tests that /api/config?token=... is rejected while /ws?token=... remains accepted.
issue.acceptance: API endpoints reject query-string bearer tokens; WebSocket query-token auth still works; tests cover both paths

issue.title: Serialize web config read-modify-write updates
issue.context: lib.rs put_config() reads config.json, computes a merge patch, then calls write_config_atomic() without any process/file lock. Two authenticated PUTs can both read the same old document and each atomically rename its own result, so the last writer silently discards fields from the other request. This is especially likely from the SPA's independent settings controls and can lose security-relevant auto-approve/tool-rule changes. Add a lock spanning read, merge, and rename (or delegate to daemon config update code), and add a concurrent-update regression test.
issue.acceptance: Concurrent config updates preserve both patches; writes remain atomic; regression test demonstrates no lost update

issue.title: Sprint-3: Web-auth / TLS hardening
issue.context:
Sprint-3 assembles 22 pre-existing, groomed hardening issues (all <=C2, Sonnet-leadable, unblocked) across the web auth / TLS transport / /api/auth surfaces. Provenance: selected during the 2026-07-11 backlog grooming (complexity:C0-C2, route:sonnet-5 or cheaper); tickets re-parented here, originals unchanged.

Close the known hardening gaps across the web auth, TLS transport, and /api/auth surfaces so a LocalLAN-exposed Wisphive daemon resists credential, transport, and rate-limit attacks - Sonnet-led, <=C2, behavior-preserving.

issue.title: security.rs: password_set cache never invalidates on live reset-password
issue.context: crossfire-review (codex+opus, both independently found this) of commit a38ea02 (itr#256). password_set_cache in SecurityConfigInner only ever latches false->true and is never invalidated in-process. wisphive web reset-password runs in a separate CLI process against the DB directly, with no signal to a live server's cache. After a reset against a running server: /api/auth/status keeps reporting setup_required:false, the SPA renders Login (which then 401s forever since the password hash is gone), and the unauthenticated setup endpoint stays live but hidden from the operator. Recovery requires a full server restart or CLI reseed. This defeats the documented purpose of reset-password when run against a live process.
issue.acceptance: reset-password against a running server causes /api/auth/status to immediately switch to setup-required (or an equivalent bounded-TTL/cross-process invalidation), without requiring a restart. New integration test: reset a running server, verify /api/auth/status flips.

issue.title: auth.rs: record_success wipes whole per-IP throttle entry, breaking configured max_in_flight>1
issue.context: crossfire-review (codex, verified against code by orchestrator) of commit a38ea02, interaction between itr#243 (configurable MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_IP) and the pre-existing AttemptGuard::record_success. record_success unconditionally does state.map.remove(&ip_key), removing the WHOLE per-IP entry including sibling guards' in_flight counts. With WISPHIVE_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_IP configured >1 (the NAT-office scenario itr#243 was built for), one sibling's success wipes the shared counter while other siblings are still outstanding, letting new attempts stack on top without the throttle seeing the true concurrent count -- actual concurrent verifies can exceed the configured cap. Confirmed: the existing test configured_max_in_flight_raises_the_cap only exercises sequential all-success, not mixed success/failure with cap>1 concurrently outstanding. Dormant under the old hardcoded cap=1 (siblings could never coexist), only reachable now that the cap is configurable.
issue.acceptance: On success, release only the calling guard's own reservation (mirror release_slot's decrement-in-place pattern) instead of removing the whole map entry. New test: cap=3, mixed success/failure with siblings still in flight, asserts the throttle's admitted-concurrency count never exceeds the configured cap.

issue.title: auth.rs: locked_until doesn't advance for concurrent failures inside an active lockout under max_in_flight>1
issue.context: crossfire-review (opus) of commit a38ea02, interaction between itr#233 (don't extend locked_until on failures during active lockout) and itr#243 (configurable MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_IP). apply_failure only recomputes locked_until when now >= entry.locked_until. Under a raised max_in_flight (e.g. 3), several guards can fail near-simultaneously: the first sets locked_until = now + backoff_for(1) (250ms); the others land inside that fresh window so the recompute is suppressed. failures still climbs, but the immediate lockout stays pinned at the 1-failure rung until the window lapses, rather than reflecting the full burst size.
issue.acceptance: When now < locked_until but failures grew, still advance locked_until to max(locked_until, now + backoff_for(failures)) so the schedule reflects accumulated failures under a raised in-flight cap. issue.title: tls.rs: DER NotBefore age check trips ~24h earlier than the intended 90-day policy
issue.context: crossfire-review (opus, verified against code by orchestrator) of commit a38ea02 (itr#226). generate_and_persist_inner backdates the cert's DER NotBefore by CERT_NOT_BEFORE_BACKDATE_HOURS (24h) but sets the sidecar's meta.created_at to plain now (no backdate). The DER NotBefore age check (itr#226) computes now - not_before > MAX_CERT_AGE_SECS, which equals now - created_at + 24h > 90d, i.e. it trips at day 89 instead of day 90 -- one extra premature regeneration per rotation cycle, undercutting the TOFU cert-pin stability itr#227 was chasing for paired phones. Confirmed via direct read of tls.rs lines 336 (DER check), 403 (backdate), 422-427 (created_at).
issue.acceptance: Compare DER NotBefore against MAX_CERT_AGE_SECS + backdate, or derive both the sidecar check and the DER check from the same epoch so they agree on the effective threshold.

issue.title: tls.rs: randomized tmp filenames removed self-healing cleanup, crash leaks key material tmp file
issue.context: crossfire-review (opus, verified against code by orchestrator) of commit a38ea02 (itr#235). The old deterministic tmp filename (<path>.tmp) was self-healing: the next write_secret call to the same final path would remove_file the old tmp before writing. itr#235 randomized the tmp suffix per call (correctly closing the TOCTOU symlink-precreate window) but this also removed that self-healing property with no replacement sweep. write_secret's own error-path cleanup only fires within the SAME call that created the tmp; a process crash (SIGKILL, power loss, ENOSPC-abort) between fsync and rename now permanently leaks a 0600 tmp copy of key/cert material into ~/.wisphive, since no later call ever revisits that random filename. Confirmed via grep: no read_dir-based sweep exists anywhere in tls.rs outside test assertions.

issue.title: tls.rs: corrupt-but-parseable key/cert hard-fails startup instead of self-healing via regen
issue.context: crossfire-review (opus) of commit a38ea02 (itr#228/itr#226). key_matches_cert_spki and der_not_before_unix both propagate parse errors (Err) via ? in try_load_existing, rather than mapping them to Ok(None) the way every other corruption check in this function does (mismatched sidecar, expired cert, filtered SANs all self-heal by returning None to trigger regen). A key.pem or cert.pem that's valid PEM but unparseable by rcgen/x509-parser now hard-fails ensure_cert and blocks daemon startup, rather than self-healing. issue.title: Sprint-4: Control-plane robustness hardening
issue.context:
Sprint-4 assembles 59 pre-existing, groomed robustness issues (all <=C2, Sonnet/terra-leadable, unblocked) into a single control-plane hardening pass. Provenance: selected 2026-07-11 from the groomed backlog + sprint-3 carryover (#503, #504, #505). Re-parented here; originals unchanged, grooming tags preserved.

## Sprint Goal
Pay down control-plane robustness debt - eliminate known panics, silent no-ops, races, TOCTOU/permission gaps, and fail-open holes across daemon, hook, TUI, CLI, and web so Wisphive fails safe and legibly under bad input, crashes, and concurrency. <=C2, behavior-hardening, no new features.

## Non-Goals
- No new features or UI surfaces (analytics/journal/pairing epics stay out).
- No taste=2 UI/UX polish (opus lane).
- No C3/C4 refactors or epics (#131, #117, #126, #389 ...).
- No pure test-infra/coverage or docs tickets (spillover).
- No passkey/webauthn, mobile-pairing, enterprise-TLS work.
- Behavior-preserving on public surfaces (protocol/schema/CLI) unless AC says otherwise.

## Lanes (file ownership for /blitz)
A security carryover+tail; B daemon/protocol; C CLI correctness; D TUI robustness; E frontend correctness.

## Definition of Done (sprint-level)
- Story AC passes with its named test/command.
- Every bug fix adds a regression test proving the specific failure mode (panic/no-op/race/fail-open) is gone.
- cargo test --workspace green; cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt applied. Lane E also green on frontend-lint + frontend-test.
- Security-touching stories run cargo deny check / npm audit where deps or auth surfaces are involved.
- Behavior-preserving on public surfaces unless AC explicitly changes it.

issue.title: Align Claude hook timeout with daemon approval timeout
issue.context: Follow-up from itr#94 independent review. Claude command hooks default to 600 seconds when timeout is omitted, while Wisphive's daemon hook approval timeout defaults to 3600 seconds and can be configured up to 86400. install_claude currently omits timeout. A pending approval can therefore outlive the gating hook and be canceled before the daemon resolves it. This predates #94 and should be hardened separately.

issue.title: Audit Codex managed spawn against effective hook inventory
issue.context: Follow-up from itr#94 independent review and official Codex Hooks docs. Managed Codex spawn currently audits only <repo>/.codex/hooks.json before passing --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust. Codex actually merges ~/.codex/hooks.json, user/project inline [hooks] config, project hooks.json, enabled plugin hooks, and managed sources; [features] hooks=false and persisted /hooks disablement also affect whether the Wisphive hook runs. A valid project file is therefore not proof that the child has an enabled Wisphive PreToolUse gate, and foreign effective hooks can evade the current blast-radius audit. Related to closed #467/#471. Official source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks

Add tests for each source/disable path and runtime proof that the spawned child gates a PreToolUse event.
