issue.title: wisphive_hook socket-test harness: listener-thread startup race under machine load
issue.context: Discovered during sprint-5 crossfire-blitz Wave 1 gate (2026-07-13). tests::socket_error_response_fails_closed and tests::socket_garbage_decision_fails_closed (both in crates/wisphive_hook/src/main.rs) use a socket_scenario test helper that spawns a listener thread and connects to it from the test body. Under cargo test --workspace's full parallel load, the connecting side sometimes races ahead of the listener thread actually binding/accepting, producing a connection-refused that the hook classifies as HookFailureKind::DaemonUnreachable instead of the test's expected Runtime — a false test failure, not a logic bug (isolated cargo test -p wisphive_hook runs pass 66/66 reliably; a clean baseline worktree with only the failing task's diff also passed). Confirmed non-deterministic: two separate full-workspace runs each failed a DIFFERENT test in the same family with the identical DaemonUnreachable-vs-Runtime signature. Same category of machine-load test flakiness already tracked for a different test in itr#520.
issue.acceptance: socket_scenario (or its callers) synchronizes on the listener thread actually being ready to accept (e.g. a bind-confirmation channel/barrier) before the test connects, so socket_error_response_fails_closed and socket_garbage_decision_fails_closed no longer flake under cargo test --workspace machine load.

notes.content: Duplicate report (itr#527, closed) sharpened the root-cause hypothesis: the fake-daemon test helper write_all()s the ServerMessage::Error line and immediately drops the socket without waiting for the hook to read it -- under scheduler load the hook can observe connection teardown (DaemonUnreachable, fail-open) before consuming the Error line (Runtime, fail-closed), rather than a listener-thread startup race as originally hypothesized. Fix idea: have the fake daemon wait for the hook to read-to-EOF (or shutdown(Write) + linger) before dropping the socket.

issue.title: ADR candidate: redesign Codex managed-spawn hook audit to avoid reimplementing Codex's config-resolution internals
issue.context: Follow-up from sprint-5 crossfire-blitz itr#511 review round 3 (2026-07-14, fable-5 review). itr#511's Codex effective-hook-inventory audit (crates/wisphive_daemon/src/process_registry.rs) has grown from ~1400 to ~4500+ lines across three hardening passes, reimplementing Codex's own config-resolution internals: semver parsing/precedence, plugin active-version selection, manifest shape resolution, TOML profile layering, kill-switch precedence (features.hooks/codex_hooks alias), and persisted hooks.state key formats. Every one of these is an emulation of an evolving third-party binary's undocumented/partially-documented internal behavior; a future Codex change to any of these desyncs the audit, and desync in the under-detection direction is a direct control-plane bypass (three concrete instances found in round-3 review: disableAllHooks scope ambiguity, features.hooks/codex_hooks precedence assumption, and persisted-disable state-key format assumption -- all three resolved toward fail-closed conservatism in itr#511's round-4 fix, but the underlying structural fragility remains). Reviewer's suggestion: derive the effective hook inventory from Codex itself (e.g. a 'codex config effective-hooks' / 'codex doctor'-style introspection command, if Codex has or could gain one) or spawn Codex into a fully daemon-controlled, isolated CODEX_HOME the audit fully owns (so there's nothing external to emulate), rather than mirroring Codex's merge logic from outside.
issue.acceptance: An ADR at docs/decisions/ (or a scoped design doc) evaluates: (a) whether Codex exposes or could be asked to expose an authoritative 'effective hook inventory' introspection surface the daemon could query instead of re-deriving it; (b) whether spawning into a fully daemon-controlled isolated CODEX_HOME (so the audit owns 100% of what Codex reads, nothing to emulate) is feasible without breaking legitimate user/plugin hook use cases; (c) a recommendation and rough sizing for whichever approach reduces the audit's dependency on reimplementing Codex's undocumented internals. Not required to land code -- decision-record + sizing is the deliverable.

issue.title: EPIC: Upgrade safety — a wisphive upgrade must never brick live gated agents (incident 2026-07-15)
issue.context: Incident 2026-07-15 ~23:46-00:30: ./install.sh installed a hook binary carrying Sprint-4 file-permission hardening (mode file must be 0600 non-symlink owner-owned; state dir 0700). The operator's pre-existing ~/.wisphive/mode had legacy looser perms. New binary refused it; fail-mode defaults to closed; EVERY hook event was denied INCLUDING UserPromptSubmit — the operator could not even send prompts to repair via agents. Claude Code AND Codex (same hook) were both bricked until manual chmod. Two compounding design gaps: (1) a hardening shipped with no migration/auto-repair for state the previous version itself created; (2) the human's own prompt-submission event is subject to fail-closed denial, cutting off the repair channel. Per working agreements: preserve the hardening (do NOT weaken the check), add fail-safes around it.
issue.acceptance: All member issues closed with evidence. Red-team scenario: legacy-perm state dir + fresh install → agents keep running, repair is automatic or one command, UserPromptSubmit never hard-blocked by config/perms errors.

issue.title: install.sh atomic upgrade: build → codesign → self-test against REAL state dir → atomic rename swap, rollback on failure
issue.context: Two failure modes today: (a) in-place overwrite of a signed running binary on macOS invalidates its signature (SIGKILL risk for live processes) and leaves a copy→codesign window where the hook is broken; (b) nothing validates the NEW binary can operate against the operator's EXISTING ~/.wisphive before it becomes live — exactly how incident 2026-07-15 shipped a brick. Stage to temp path, codesign there, run the new wisphive-hook in a validate-only mode against the real state dir (read-only probe), then mv -f (atomic rename) into ~/.cargo/bin. On probe failure: print exactly what would break and the fix, and abort leaving the old binary in place (or auto-repair once the migration issue lands).
issue.acceptance: Scripted test: simulate legacy-perm state dir; install.sh either repairs-and-proceeds or aborts with actionable message — never installs a binary that would deny-all. Old binary untouched on abort. No copy→codesign live window (verified by swap ordering in script). Live hook processes unaffected mid-upgrade.
issue.close_reason: Commit fe3c1ae. install.sh rewritten: build -> stage at hidden names inside the install dir -> ad-hoc codesign the STAGED paths (macOS; abort on failure, old binaries untouched) -> read-only preflight of the operator's real state dir with the NEW binary via new hidden 'wisphive-hook --statecheck [--home <dir>]' (exit 0/1, prints findings + repair commands, performs NO repairs, touches no brick/marker state) -> abort-with-guidance on failure (old binaries byte-identical, no staged leftovers) unless --fix-perms/interactive confirmation runs scripts/wisphive-rescue.sh --fix and re-probes -> atomic mv -f rename swap (no copy->codesign window, no half-written binary ever at the final path). issue.title: Brick detector: N consecutive same-cause config/perms denials → OS notification + marker file with exact repair commands
issue.context: During a bricked window the TUI/web may be unreachable or unwatched; the operator learns of the problem from agent failures. The hook itself is the only component guaranteed to be running — when it denies repeatedly for the SAME config/perms cause it should escalate passively: one OS notification (existing osascript/notify-send path) naming the broken file + 'run wisphive doctor --fix-perms or wisphive emergency-off', plus a ~/.wisphive/BRICKED marker (best-effort, perms-tolerant write) that doctor and the daemon surface. Rate-limited to once per cause per hour.
issue.acceptance: Simulated repeated denials for one cause fire exactly one notification + marker; different cause fires again; repaired state clears marker on next healthy invocation. No notification storm (test 50 rapid denials → 1 notification).
issue.close_reason: Commit ce85d35. crates/wisphive_hook/src/brick.rs: after 3 consecutive same-cause config/perms fail-closed denials the hook fires ONE OS notification (osascript / notify-send, control-chars stripped, AppleScript-escaped) naming the broken file + 'run wisphive doctor --fix-perms or scripts/wisphive-rescue.sh', and drops a ~/.wisphive/BRICKED marker (best-effort perms-tolerant O_NOFOLLOW 0600 write) carrying cause + full denial message for doctor/daemon surfacing. Rate-limited once per cause per hour (cause = truncated SHA-256 of the validator error, which embeds path + observed mode/uid); different cause fires immediately; healthy invocation clears marker + state so repair->re-break re-notifies. Persistence documented in module docs: primary ~/.wisphive/brick-state.json, fallback TMPDIR/wisphive-brick-<uid>.json (0600, O_NOFOLLOW, owner-checked before trust) because the state dir may be the broken thing; all writes + notification best-effort — never a repair, never a decision change (ADR-0010 DENY untouched). WISPHIVE_BRICK_NOTIFY_CAPTURE env redirects notifications to a file for tests (informational only, not a gating surface). Tests (10): 50 rapid denials -> exactly 1 notification+marker; below threshold silent; cause change refires while old cause rate-limited; renotify after an hour; clear-on-healthy refires; unwritable state dir falls back to tmp still firing once; symlinked/foreign state file untrusted; JSON roundtrip; hash distinctness; repair commands + no control chars in body. E2E: redteam scenario (b) 32 real release-binary denials -> 1 captured notification + marker with guidance (q12-redteam.txt). Daemon/doctor surfacing of the marker filed as follow-up #552.

issue.title: Always-defer emits `ask` into headless managed spawns with no native prompt to defer to
issue.context:
ADR-0002 always-defer returns Decision::Ask for DEFAULT_ALWAYS_ASK tools (AskUserQuestion/EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode/Elicitation) to defer to the agent's NATIVE prompt — the ADR's stated premise is that the answer can only come back through that prompt. CLAUDE.md says these defer UNCONDITIONALLY: no posture or override can un-defer them.

But daemon-managed spawns run `claude -p` headless with stdio nulled (process_registry.rs ~2150) and pass --dangerously-skip-permissions (process_registry.rs:2162). There is no native prompt in headless print mode. The hook still emits {"permissionDecision":"ask"} into it.

THE SHARP VERSION: this bug class is ALREADY understood and fixed — for Codex only. main.rs:731-743 fails closed with a reason when agent_type == Codex, commenting: 'Codex has no native PreToolUse prompt to defer to ... so "ask" cannot be expressed — and exit 0 with empty stdout would be a silent approve. Fail closed with a reason instead (itr#366).' That guard branches on AGENT TYPE, but the correct predicate is WHETHER A NATIVE PROMPT EXISTS. Headless `claude -p` is the second member of that class and is not Codex, so it falls through to main.rs:746 and emits ask.

REACHABLE BY DESIGN, not by accident: validate_spawn_request (process_registry.rs:100-104) explicitly PERMITS permission_mode='plan'. A plan-mode spawn exists to make the agent call ExitPlanMode — an intrinsic DEFAULT_ALWAYS_ASK member. A supported, validated spawn config routes straight into the defer guard.

THE FIX HAS ITS INPUT ALREADY: process_registry.rs:2244 sets WISPHIVE_AGENT_ID on the child and the hook already reads it (main.rs:357) — but discards it for managed spawns because resolve_agent_id (main.rs:339-351) prefers session_id and the spawn passes --session-id (:2163). No new plumbing needed; may want an explicit marker since --session-id masks it.

NOT YET PROVEN: which bad outcome results (effective allow / hang / error). That is Claude Code behavior, not ours; no code in the repo settles it. Empirical probe pending — see notes. Candidate (unconfirmed) explanation for PO report that managed agents are currently broken.

DISCOVERED: 2026-07-15 during t3code provider-transport recon. Related: itr#366 (the Codex half), itr#442/#440 (interactive-only probe at docs/research/hook-probe/).

DOC GAPS FOUND: ADR-0002 never uses the words headless/spawn/managed/-p — it assumes a native prompt throughout. docs/GLOSSARY.md states both halves and never connects them: :57-61 says 'claude -p ... has no interactive PTY'; :96-101 defines Ask/defer as 'return the call to the agent's native prompt' with no headless caveat.

ZERO TEST COVERAGE of the intersection: no test sets WISPHIVE_AGENT_ID (main.rs:2665 hardcodes None); all defer tests (main.rs:2347/:2364/:2496/:2577/:2592/:2610) are classification units with no agent-origin dimension; tests/defer_audit_dedup.rs:38 env_remove()s the wisphive vars and fabricates an interactive session_id; process_registry.rs tests contain zero occurrences of AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode/defer/Decision::Ask and never assert on the envs set at :2244-2245. main.rs:2546 codex_ask_fails_closed_with_explicit_deny is the only test modeling a promptless agent — and it's Codex.
issue.acceptance:
1. Empirical probe settles what `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` does with permissionDecision:'ask' (effective allow / hang / error), recorded under docs/research/ with raw evidence like docs/research/hook-probe/.
2. The always-defer guard's predicate is WHETHER A NATIVE PROMPT EXISTS, not agent_type == Codex. main.rs:731-743's Codex branch generalizes to cover headless managed Claude spawns.
3. A managed headless spawn hitting an intrinsic always-defer tool resolves DETERMINISTICALLY and fail-closed (never a silent approve), with a reason the operator can read — consistent with ADR-0010.
4. Test covers the intersection: a managed-origin (WISPHIVE_AGENT_ID set) PreToolUse for ExitPlanMode/AskUserQuestion asserts the fail-closed response. Closes the gap where process_registry and always-defer are only tested in isolation.
5. ADR-0002 amended to state its native-prompt premise explicitly and say what happens when no native prompt exists. docs/GLOSSARY.md :57-61 and :96-101 cross-reference.
6. Decided + recorded: does permission_mode='plan' remain a permitted managed-spawn config given it routes into always-defer by construction (process_registry.rs:100-104)?
issue.close_reason: Landed 9c1c82e (mission no-silent-failures 603#L3). Headless intrinsic asks now deny loud+audited+attributed with escape hatch; block-shaped events untouched; interactive contract pinned unchanged; Chat seam documented; plan-mode KEEP ratified.

notes.content:
EMPIRICAL PROBE DONE (2026-07-15, Claude Code 2.1.211) — evidence at docs/research/headless-ask-probe/. AC1 satisfied.

HYPOTHESIS REFUTED. 'ask' under headless claude -p is a silent BLOCK, not a silent approve:
  A) ask + --dangerously-skip-permissions : tool ran=NO, PostToolUse=NO, exit=0, 6s
  B) ask, no bypass                       : tool ran=NO, PostToolUse=NO, exit=0, 8s
  C) control (no ask, + bypass)           : tool ran=YES, PostToolUse=YES, exit=0, 6s  [rig works]
Execution measured by filesystem sentinel + PostToolUse presence, not by grepping result text (a first pass false-positived: Claude quotes the command back in prose while saying it did NOT run).

KEY CONSEQUENCES:
1. Fail-closed posture HOLDS. No silent approve. No hang. Severity drops from security hole to correctness/observability defect.
2. BYPASS IS IRRELEVANT to 'ask' — A and B identical. An explicit hook 'ask' forces the prompt path that --dangerously-skip-permissions would otherwise skip. **Removing bypass does NOT fix this on its own.** Do not conflate this issue with the bypass-removal work.
3. THE REAL DEFECT is a silent capability hole with ZERO observability: tool never runs, agent burns a turn narrating 'this session is non-interactive so there's no way to approve the prompt', job EXITS 0 = SUCCESS having accomplished nothing. Always-defer resolves in the hook and never reaches the daemon -> no decision_log row, no inbox entry, operator gets no signal.
4. Plausible (still unconfirmed) explanation for PO's report that managed agents are broken — presents as 'runs but does nothing useful'.

METHOD NOTE for re-runs: ExitPlanMode is NOT reliably inducible under -p (first attempt: --permission-mode plan produced num_turns=1 with no tool call at all; Claude just answered in prose). Force the ask on Bash instead — Claude's handling of 'ask' does not depend on which tool it is for. Two-step method keeps quota cost minimal: step 1 drives the real wisphive-hook with synthetic stdin in an isolated HOME to confirm emitted bytes (free), step 2 replays those exact bytes from a stub inside a live claude -p (only this spends quota).

AC3 IMPLICATION: 'deterministic + fail-closed' is already true — what is missing is that it be OBSERVABLE and carry a reason. The bare ask has no permissionDecisionReason at all (main.rs:746), so the agent is not even told why. The Codex branch (main.rs:731-743) supplies one; generalizing that arm gets both.

SCOPE CHANGE 2026-07-16 — THE FIX MUST BE POSTURE-AWARE. Do not simply generalize the Codex fail-closed arm.

PO is adding a CHAT surface (itr#564 spike): Wisphive drives `claude` over bidirectional stream-json from Rust, inherits the hook gate, and routes decisions to the WISPHIVE INBOX (Inbox = Chat's own gate surface; no second gate).

A stream-json Chat session is HEADLESS-SHAPED from the CLI's perspective — no native prompt — so this issue's dead-end applies to Chat too. And Chat is THE surface where AskUserQuestion fires most: it is a conversation.

THEREFORE the fix direction in this issue's AC2/AC3 ('generalize main.rs:731-743's Codex fail-closed arm to cover any promptless agent') IS WRONG FOR CHAT — it would DENY every question the assistant asks. Fail-closed is right for UNATTENDED Spawn Agent; it is wrong for an interactive Chat where a human is present and the Inbox can answer.

THE REAL PREDICATE IS NOT 'does a native prompt exist' EITHER. It is closer to: CAN THIS SESSION'S ANSWER REACH THE MODEL, AND BY WHAT CHANNEL?
  - Unattended headless spawn : no channel -> fail closed with a reason (this issue's original direction, still right for Spawn Agent).
  - Chat over stream-json     : possibly answerable over --input-format stream-json (itr#564 AC10 determines this empirically). If so, the Inbox answers and the tool proceeds.
  - Interactive terminal      : native prompt -> defer (today's behavior, correct).
  - Codex                     : no native PreToolUse prompt -> fail closed (already done, itr#366).

BLOCKED-BY-ish: #564 AC10 decides whether Chat is answerable. Do not land a fail-closed generalization that Chat then has to unwind. Sequence: #564 AC10 first, then fix here with the full posture matrix.

Note this ALSO revises the ADR-0002 amendment in AC5: the ADR must not merely say 'what happens when no native prompt exists' — it must state the CHANNEL matrix above, because the answer differs per surface.

issue.title: Connection-capacity rejection is misclassified as DaemonUnreachable -> silent unaudited auto-approve (fail-OPEN at capacity)
issue.context:
THE GATE FAILS OPEN WHEN THE DAEMON IS AT CONNECTION CAPACITY. Tool calls are silently auto-approved with NO decision_log row. Found 2026-07-15 by a verifier agent during the t3code provider-transport recon — while REFUTING an unrelated t3code-derived claim. Chain verified by hand against the tree afterwards.

THE CHAIN:
1. MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS = 256 (server.rs:30), shared by EVERY client kind (hooks, TUI, web bridge) — itr#99 DoS guard.
2. The permit is acquired in the ACCEPT LOOP (server.rs ~:477) BEFORE Hello, so the daemon cannot prioritize a blocking hook over a TUI/web client.
3. At capacity, reject_connection_at_capacity (server.rs:557-563) writes ServerMessage::Error{'daemon connection capacity reached; retry later'} at the WELCOME position and shuts down, deliberately never constructing a ConnectionContext or handler — so NO Welcome (:681) is ever sent and NO decision_log row is ever written.
4. The hook reads the welcome line and checks only matches!(welcome, ServerMessage::Welcome{..}) (main.rs:~1513). Anything else -> HookFailure::unreachable (main.rs:196-208) -> HookFailureKind::DaemonUnreachable.
5. response_for_failure (main.rs:642, comment at :670-672) -> 'A daemon outage always fails open: with the control plane down there is no path to a human decision, and fail-closing here would brick every agent on the machine.' -> Decision::Approve.

THE CATEGORY ERROR: ADR-0001's daemon-unreachable-fails-open is CORRECT and must stay — a crashed control plane must not brick every agent. But 'at capacity' is NOT a crashed control plane. THE DAEMON ANSWERED. It is reachable by definition; it made a deliberate, healthy decision to shed load. Classifying a live daemon's explicit protocol-level rejection as 'unreachable' is the bug. A live daemon saying 'I am full' should resolve per fail-mode (DEFAULT CLOSED), not fail open.

WHY A WAVE IS THE WORKLOAD THAT REACHES IT: blocking hooks hold their permit for the whole human-decision wait — up to hook_timeout_secs (default 3600s / 1 hour, config.rs:27-31). 256 concurrent connections is not reachable by an operator's handful of interactive sessions, but IS reachable by a wave-spawner fanning out agents whose tool calls queue up while the human is away. The planned wave-spawner is the first workload that would hit this, and it would hit it SILENTLY. This must be fixed BEFORE any wave-spawner ships.

RELATED: neither Wisphive nor t3code caps concurrently RUNNING agents (separate finding, separate issue) — which is what lets the connection count climb unbounded in the first place.
issue.acceptance:
1. A live daemon's explicit capacity rejection is NOT classified DaemonUnreachable. Distinguish 'socket refused/absent = control plane down' (fail open, ADR-0001 preserved) from 'live daemon answered with a protocol-level rejection' (resolve per fail-mode; default CLOSED). The daemon answered => it is reachable.
2. A dedicated protocol variant (e.g. ServerMessage::Overloaded / a typed rejection reason) rather than reusing bare ServerMessage::Error, so the hook can tell 'full' from a generic error without string-matching the message text.
3. The capacity path is OBSERVABLE: an operator-visible signal (warn! + TUI/web alert) that the gate shed a decision, and an audit record that a call was resolved by capacity rather than by a human. Today the daemon writes no decision_log row at all — a silent auto-approve is invisible to .
4. Test proves it: saturate the semaphore, drive a real PreToolUse through target/release/wisphive-hook against an isolated HOME, assert the response is NOT an approve and that the resolution is auditable. Regression-guards the whole class.
5. Consider whether hooks need a reserved permit budget separate from TUI/web clients (a flood of web clients must not be able to starve the gate into shedding decisions), and whether the permit should be acquired after Hello so the daemon can prioritize by client kind.
6. ADR-0001 amended to state the boundary explicitly: unreachable-fails-open covers control-plane ABSENCE, never a live daemon's deliberate load-shedding.
issue.close_reason: Landed fd2d3f9 (mission no-silent-failures 603#L1). Hook fails closed + audited on live daemon rejection; typed Overloaded wire variant; ADR-0001 amended; B-A8 socket-down fail-open regression-guarded. Runtime probe: 257th conn typed-rejected, hook DENY at capacity, events.jsonl decided_by=daemon_overloaded:capacity, socket-absent still approves.

issue.title: stop_agent SIGKILLs the direct PID only — comment claims graceful SIGTERM, tool-subprocess grandchildren are orphaned
issue.context:
Found 2026-07-15 by the t3code recon (docs/research/t3code-recon.md), hand-checked.

THE COMMENT LIES. stop_agent's doc comment says SIGTERM (process_registry.rs:2585) and the inline says 'Try graceful kill first' (:2593) — but :2594 calls tokio kill() = SIGKILL, to the DIRECT PID ONLY. No SIGTERM, no grace, no process-group kill anywhere. grep SIGTERM|process_group|setsid|killpg|kill_on_drop across crates/ returns exactly two hits: that lying comment and an unrelated kill_on_drop in worktree.rs:76.

CONSEQUENCES: (1) the agent gets no cleanup chance (SIGKILL uncatchable) despite the comment claiming it does; (2) every grandchild the agent spawned — the tool subprocesses that actually touch fs/network — is ORPHANED and keeps running: killing 'claude' does not kill the cargo build / npm install it launched; (3) the operator is told the agent stopped. It did not.

BLOCKS THE WAVE-SPAWNER: blast radius scales linearly. 'Stop the wave' over 30 agents reaches 30 direct PIDs, orphans N grandchildren across N worktrees, and reports success. An emergency stop that lies is worse than none. MUST land before any stop-the-wave affordance ships.

t3code's shape is worth copying: opencode spawned detached:true (opencodeRuntime.ts:348) solely to enable a process-GROUP kill via process.kill(-pid, sig) (:374), grace ladder killpg(SIGTERM)/1s/killpg(SIGKILL) (:381-386). Codex: forceKillAfter='2 seconds' (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:56/:733).
issue.acceptance:
1. Managed agents spawn into their own process group (setsid / process_group(0)) so the tree is addressable.
2. stop_agent signals the GROUP not the direct PID: SIGTERM to group, bounded grace, then SIGKILL to group. Grandchildren die with the agent.
3. Comments at :2585 and :2593 match what the code does — they currently describe a SIGTERM+grace path that does not exist.
4. Test: spawn a managed agent that launches a long-running grandchild, stop the agent, assert the grandchild is GONE (not merely reparented).
5. Grace period is a named constant with a rationale, not a magic number.
6. 'Stop the wave' reports per-agent success only when the whole tree is confirmed gone.
issue.close_reason: Landed as 25432ff (Chain-Link: 603#L5). Process-group stop ladder with confirmed-whole-tree-gone semantics; review terrain re-count 9/9 clean; residuals filed #620/#621.

issue.title: detect_agent_type_from_env wildcard defaults unknown providers to ClaudeCode — unparseable deny may be ignored and proceed ungated
issue.context:
Found 2026-07-15 by the t3code recon (docs/research/t3code-recon.md).

detect_agent_type_from_env (main.rs:267-284) matches WISPHIVE_AGENT_TYPE with a wildcard '_ => {}' arm and falls through to an unconditional AgentType::ClaudeCode default — pinned by the test defaults_to_claude_without_codex_signal (:3209-3216), so the behavior is deliberate, not an oversight.

Response FORMATTING branches on agent type (:731 for the Ask arm, :770). So an unknown/future provider receives CLAUDE-SHAPED JSON it cannot parse. A provider that cannot parse the response may IGNORE IT AND PROCEED — i.e. an unparseable DENY becomes an effective allow. The gate silently does not apply to any provider it does not already know.

IMPORTANT — DO NOT cite the closed AgentType enum as the fail-closed mechanism here. It never participates in this path: the hook does not deserialize AgentType from stdin, and both deser sites carry #[serde(default = "default_agent_type")]. The closed enum protects the DAEMON's spawn path (unknown agent_type = compile error + hard bail); it does nothing for the HOOK's env-based detection. The recon flagged this explicitly because it is the wrong-but-plausible reassurance a reviewer reaches for.

Contrast with the Codex arm (:731-743), which already fails closed with an explicit reason for a provider that has no native prompt — the codebase already knows how to refuse a provider it cannot serve correctly. It just does not refuse a provider it does not RECOGNIZE.

Related: itr#559 (same Ask-arm agent-type branching; the guard's predicate is wrong there too — agent identity rather than capability). Consider fixing both in the same pass over that arm.
issue.acceptance:
1. detect_agent_type_from_env returns Option<AgentType>; an unrecognized WISPHIVE_AGENT_TYPE yields None rather than silently becoming ClaudeCode.
2. None routes through response_for_failure — the gate refuses to emit a response shaped for a provider it cannot identify, resolving per the tiered fail posture (ADR-0001) rather than guessing.
3. The ABSENCE of WISPHIVE_AGENT_TYPE (a plain interactive claude session, the common case) still resolves as ClaudeCode — only an unrecognized non-empty VALUE is treated as unknown. Do not break the unset case.
4. Test defaults_to_claude_without_codex_signal (:3209-3216) is updated to pin the corrected contract, plus a new test asserting an unrecognized value does NOT produce Claude-shaped JSON.
5. Documented: adding a provider means adding an AgentType variant AND a formatter arm; the hook refuses rather than guesses until both exist.
issue.close_reason: Landed 8b260e3 (mission no-silent-failures 603#L2). Unknown provider = loud refusal on the bare exit-2 channel, audited; unset/heuristic behavior byte-identical; runtime-probed both fail-modes + pre-parse corner. Read-layer visibility follow-through = itr#607 (chain L2.5).

Found 2026-07-15 by the t3code provider-transport recon (docs/research/t3code-recon.md), hand-checked against the tree.

A grep for SIGTERM|process_group|setsid|killpg|kill_on_drop across crates/ returns exactly two hits: that lying comment, and an unrelated kill_on_drop in worktree.rs:76.

2. Every grandchild the agent spawned — the tool subprocesses, i.e. the things that actually touch the filesystem and network — is ORPHANED and keeps running. Killing  does not kill the  /  /  it launched.

issue.title: SPIKE: Rust-native stream-json driver crate for Claude/Codex CLIs — is the programmatic surface contractual or reverse-engineered? (ADR-0009 test)
issue.context:
Spike for the Chat surface (PO direction 2026-07-16): Wisphive gains a Chat interface reachable through the app, SDK/transport-driven, as its OWN surface with its OWN gate — additive to Spawn Agent, which stays hook-gated and unattended (see docs/research/t3code-recon.md).

THE TRANSPORT QUESTION. t3code uses the Node package @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk because t3code's server IS Node. Wisphive's daemon is Rust, so 'use the SDK' means managing a Node sidecar (runtime dep, supervised process, extra IPC hop, npm in the trust path). But `claude --help` (2.1.211) shows --input-format stream-json (realtime streaming input) + --output-format stream-json + --resume/--fork-session/--no-session-persistence — a bidirectional multi-turn structured session drivable directly from Rust. The Agent SDK is largely a friendly wrapper over that pipe. Same question for Codex: `codex app-server` speaks NDJSON-RPC over stdio (t3code drives it at CodexSessionRuntime.ts:716-736 with an initialize/initialized handshake).

WHY THIS IS AN ADR-0009 QUESTION, AND THE SHARP DISTINCTION. ADR-0009's thesis: do not re-derive undocumented internals of an evolving third-party binary, because a vendor change desyncs the emulation — and desync IN THE UNDER-DETECTION DIRECTION IS A CONTROL-PLANE BYPASS. That reasoning applies with FULL FORCE to anything carrying the GATE, and MUCH LESS to anything carrying only OBSERVATION:
  - Observation-only driver: a desync means missed/mis-rendered events — degraded UI, not a bypass. Reverse-engineering is a maintenance cost, not a security risk.
  - Gate-carrying driver (canUseTool / app-server requestApproval): a desync means a call we thought we gated ran ungated. This is EXACTLY the ADR-0009 trap, in the same shape.
So the spike's real output is a LINE: which parts of the programmatic surface may we depend on, for what purpose, at what risk tier. 'Observation may ride an undocumented pipe; the gate may not' is the hypothesis to confirm or kill.

NOTE the possible collapse: if a Chat session inherits the hook gate anyway (the hook is in the project's .claude/settings.json and fires regardless of who drives the session), then Chat needs NO programmatic permission responder — and the undocumented control protocol becomes the part we do not depend on at all. That would make Rust-drives-the-pipe win outright. CONFIRM OR KILL THIS FIRST; it collapses the whole decision.

OSS ANGLE (PO): if this works, the crate is publishable standalone as a Rust wrapper for these CLIs — there is no Rust equivalent of the Agent SDK today. Own crate from the start, no wisphive_* deps beyond protocol types, clean seam. See docs/open-source-path.md.

1. CONTRACT CLASSIFICATION (the core deliverable): for each surface — Claude stream-json in/out, its control protocol (can_use_tool / interrupt / set_model / context usage), and codex app-server JSON-RPC — classify as DOCUMENTED-AND-VERSIONED / DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNVERSIONED / UNDOCUMENTED-INTERNAL, with the evidence (vendor docs, --help, schema files, changelog, observed-only). No guessing; cite sources.
2. THE ADR-0009 LINE, written down: which surfaces may carry OBSERVATION and which may carry the GATE, with the desync-consequence reasoning per tier. Explicitly answers whether an undocumented pipe is acceptable for observation-only.
3. HOOK-INHERITANCE QUESTION SETTLED FIRST (it may collapse everything else): does a Chat session driving `claude` in a hooked project fire the Wisphive PreToolUse hook regardless of transport? Probe empirically against target/release/wisphive-hook + an isolated HOME, per docs/research/headless-ask-probe/. If YES, Chat needs no programmatic responder and the undocumented control protocol drops out of scope.

notes.content:
PO CLARIFICATION 2026-07-16 — THE COLLAPSING QUESTION IS ANSWERED BY DESIGN INTENT, but still needs empirical confirmation.

'Chat gates through its own surface' means: Chat INHERITS the hook, the hook routes the decision to the WISPHIVE INBOX, and the Inbox is Chat's own surface. There is no second gate. PO: 'Wisphive Inbox is right there. the tasks are gated by its own (wisphive) surface.'

CONSEQUENCE: Chat needs no programmatic permission responder for ordinary tool calls -> canUseTool / the undocumented control protocol drops out of scope for the GATE -> Rust-drives-the-pipe wins, no Node sidecar. AC3 still must CONFIRM the hook actually fires for a stream-json-driven session (do not assume; probe it).

BUT THIS SURFACES A HARD COLLISION — NEW BLOCKING QUESTION, add as AC10:

itr#559 IS A CHAT BLOCKER. Always-defer returns 'ask' for AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode to defer to the NATIVE PROMPT. A stream-json Chat session is headless-shaped from the CLI's perspective — no native prompt — so those tools dead-end exactly as #559 proved empirically (docs/research/headless-ask-probe/). And Chat is THE surface where AskUserQuestion fires most: it is a conversation. A chat where the assistant asking a question silently breaks is not a chat.

WORSE: #559's proposed fix direction (generalize the Codex fail-closed arm at main.rs:731-743) would be ACTIVELY WRONG for Chat — it would DENY every question the assistant asks.

THE TENSION: an AskUserQuestion answer is a MENU SELECTION THAT MUST REACH THE MODEL. The hook's vocabulary is only allow/deny/ask; it cannot inject an answer. So either:
  (a) the control protocol comes back into scope for always-defer tools specifically — the strongest argument FOR the Node sidecar, and it would re-import the ADR-0009 risk; or
  (b) an ALLOWED AskUserQuestion in a bidirectional stream-json session emits the question as a stream EVENT and accepts the answer back over --input-format stream-json (realtime streaming input). If so: the Inbox answers it, no control protocol, no sidecar, and #559's Chat half is solved by the same pipe.

(b) is the hypothesis. It is what a realtime streaming INPUT channel is for. NOT VERIFIED — do not assume it. If (b) holds it is decisive for the whole crate design; if it fails, the sidecar question reopens and #559's fix must be posture-aware (fail closed for unattended Spawn Agent, answerable for Chat).

AC10: Determine empirically how a bidirectional stream-json session handles an ALLOWED AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode. Can the answer be delivered over --input-format stream-json? What message shape? Is a tool_result acceptable as streamed input, or only user messages? This decides (a) vs (b), and therefore decides sidecar-vs-no-sidecar AND the shape of #559's fix.

issue.title: Spawn Agent form does nothing — PO fills out the spawn dialog and no agent starts, no visible error
issue.context:
PO-REPORTED 2026-07-16: 'I fill out the form to spawn one and nothing happens.' This is the operator-facing symptom behind PO's statement that managed agents are currently broken.

NOT itr#559. #559 predicts the OPPOSITE symptom — the agent RUNS, burns a turn, and exits 0 having done nothing (always-defer 'ask' dead-ends in headless). 'Nothing happens at all' means the spawn never starts. Do not conflate them; #559 may be entirely incidental to this.

CANDIDATE FAILURE POINTS (unverified — the investigation should not assume any of these):
1. The web form's submit never produces a SpawnAgentRequest on the wire (frontend bug, ws send, validation swallowing).
2. The request reaches the daemon but dies in validate_spawn_request (process_registry.rs:100-104 and the SYSTEM_PROMPT_DENY_PATTERNS / byte-bound validators at :29-37, :252-262) with the rejection never surfaced to the UI — a silent validation failure looks exactly like 'nothing happens'.
3. Managed spawns require EXPLICIT HUMAN APPROVAL: the launch request is queued for approval (server.rs ~:2412). If that approval request never surfaces in the TUI/web decision queue, the operator sees nothing and nothing ever runs. STRONG CANDIDATE — the whole spawn is gated behind a decision that may not be rendering.
4. require_managed_spawn_mode / the ~/.wisphive/mode kill switch refusing, silently.
5. MAX_PENDING_SPAWNS (=8) saturated by earlier stuck attempts, so subsequent submits are refused.
6. The daemon is not running at all, and the UI does not say so.
7. Codex-specific: the foreign-hook refusal (codex_allow_foreign_hooks, itr#471) declining to spawn while only warn!-ing.

WHATEVER THE CAUSE, THERE IS A SECOND BUG: a spawn that cannot proceed must TELL THE OPERATOR. Silent nothing is an observability defect independent of the root cause, and mirrors the #559/#560 pattern this recon keeps surfacing — the control plane refusing or shedding work without a signal. Fix both: the cause, and the silence.
issue.acceptance:
1. Root cause identified with file:line and a reproduction (drive the real flow, do not infer from code alone).
2. Filling out the spawn form results in either a running agent OR a visible, specific error naming what blocked it and how to fix it. Never silence.
3. If the spawn is waiting on its mandatory approval, the operator can SEE that it is waiting and where to act on it.
4. Runtime-verified end-to-end per CLAUDE.md — drive the actual web flow against a real daemon and observe an agent start (isolated HOME per docs/research/headless-ask-probe/ and the reference_isolated_daemon_verification pattern; SHORT HOME path for SUN_LEN). A green unit test does not close this.
5. Regression test covers the specific failure path found.
6. If the cause is a silent validation/approval/capacity refusal, the fix generalizes: enumerate the other spawn-refusal paths and confirm each surfaces to the operator.
issue.close_reason: Landed 20b0ad7 (mission no-silent-failures 602#L2, chain terminal). Reported symptom resolved end-to-end: refusals loud (602#L1) AND success visible (AgentSpawned producer + Spawned Processes UI), real-exec e2e proof. Distinct visible defect (dropdown-only project picker) = itr#608 (high); TUI parity #609; preflight hint #610.

notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE TRACED 2026-07-16 (read-only investigation, full path frontend->wire->bridge->daemon). PO hint 'picking a project is usually what breaks it' confirmed as consistent with candidates #4/#13/#14 below.

THE ANSWER IS NOT ONE BUG, IT IS THAT THE UI CANNOT TELL YOU ABOUT ANY BUG. Split out as itr#567 (critical, app-wide).

PROVEN, no repro needed — both independently sufficient to produce 'nothing happens':
  #1 useWisphive.ts:421-423 — 'case "error": console.error(...); return prev;'. ZERO error-surfacing infrastructure in the whole frontend (grep toast|Toast|errorBanner|lastError|daemonError = no matches). Every daemon refusal is parsed correctly (protocol.ts:456) and thrown away. App.tsx:411 closes the modal unconditionally, fire-and-forget.
  #2 server.rs:2431 gates the AgentSpawnQueued ack on correlation_id.is_some(); ws_bridge.rs:180 never sets one (wire.rs:326). The CLI does; the browser cannot. No error path AND no success path.

PROVEN STRUCTURALLY, needs runtime repro to confirm it is what PO hit:
  #3 THE PENDING APPROVAL CANNOT RENDER WHERE THE OPERATOR SPAWNED FROM. '+ Spawn' lives in the Agents view (Agents.tsx:181). The synthetic approval row carries agent_id 'wisphive-daemon:spawn' (server.rs:51/:1938). Agents.tsx:187 maps over CONNECTED agents (a pending spawn is not one) and Agents.tsx:56 filters the queue by agent_id === selectedAgent, which never matches. Click Spawn -> modal closes -> list still says 'No agents connected' (Agents.tsx:183-185). The approval IS queued and IS broadcast (queue.rs:110) and DOES render in the Inbox — but nothing on the Agents view points there. Even a PERFECTLY GOOD spawn looks like nothing happened.
  #4 POST-APPROVAL HOOK-GATE REFUSAL — matches PO's project hint. process_registry.rs:2367-2396 (Claude) / :2427-2466 (Codex) refuse a spawn whose target project has no blocking Wisphive PreToolUse hook. NASTY VARIANT: process_registry.rs:22-27 — a legacy pre-itr#510 install wrote no 'timeout', which makes has_blocking_pretool_gate FALSE, so a project that LOOKS hooked still refuses. Routes via conn_tx -> ServerMessage::Error -> dies at #1.

OTHERS: #5 SPAWN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT=5min (server.rs:48) auto-denies and the Inbox row vanishes unexplained — note the asymmetry, ordinary decisions get 3600s, spawn gets 300s. #6 MAX_PENDING_SPAWNS=8 (server.rs:50, enforced :2011-2025) — self-healing via #5 so unlikely to be the standing cause. #7 minor: SpawnModal.tsx:82-88 offers sonnet/opus/haiku regardless of agent type; Codex+sonnet passes validate_short_flag and fails later at the CLI.

RULED OUT — the wire shape is CORRECT: {type:'spawn_agent'} & SpawnAgentRequest (protocol.ts:1119) matches #[serde(tag="type")] SpawnAgent(SpawnAgentRequest) (wire.rs:114-115); AgentType is snake_case (types.rs:10-16) so claude_code/codex decode; project/prompt are the only required fields and both are sent; hook_event_name defaults to PreToolUse (types.rs:77) which parseDecisionRequest accepts (protocol.ts:596). SpawnModal handleSubmit (SpawnModal.tsx:32) only blocks empty project/prompt and disables the button in that state — it does not swallow valid input.

itr#471 SUSPICION HALF-RIGHT: process_registry.rs:2450-2466 always warn!s AND bail!s unless codex_allow_foreign_hooks — so it does NOT merely warn while refusing. The error is real and carries the foreign hook names plus the opt-in instruction. It just dies at useWisphive.ts:421 like everything else. The message is good; nothing shows it.

SEQUENCE: fix itr#567 (the silence) FIRST — it is cheap, it is AC2/AC6 here, and it converts every remaining candidate into a self-diagnosing bug. Then repro #3/#4 with the errors actually visible. Also fix #3 (surface the pending spawn in the Agents view, where the button is).

STILL NEEDED: runtime repro against an isolated short-path HOME to confirm WHICH refusal PO hit (or whether the spawn queued fine and was simply invisible).
REVIEW: unrecognized field(s) ignored: add_tag. Known fields: id, status, priority, kind, title, context, assigned_to, add_tags, remove_tags, add_skills, remove_skills, parent_id, parent, no_parent

MISSION INTAKE NOTE (chain:602): additional root-cause candidate from red-team — send() silently no-ops when ws readyState != OPEN (useWisphive.ts:617-620), so spawnAgent (:773-775) can drop the request client-side with zero trace. Diagnosis link MUST test this path alongside the note-218 candidates (pending-approval not rendering; post-approval hook-gate refusal).
Assigned to mission-lane-A

issue.title: SPIKE: Codex app-server transport for Chat — the pipe carries the config-steering surface argv audit can no longer see
issue.context:
Codex sibling of itr#564 (Claude stream-json spike). PO: Chat should be native through Codex OR Claude. Same dogfooding method — build minimal, have real conversations, see what works.

WHAT CODEX'S TRANSPORT IS (from the t3code recon, docs/research/t3code-recon.md, file:line on the t3code side):
`codex app-server` spawned long-lived (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:716-736), NDJSON-RPC over the child's stdio (packages/effect-codex-app-server/src/_internal/stdio.ts:13-22), handshake initialize -> initialized (:1202-1203). Teardown CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_KILL_AFTER='2 seconds' (:56/:733) = SIGTERM then SIGKILL 2s later; close settles every pending approval with 'cancel' (:1241-1260).

THIS IS NOT A COPY OF #564 — CODEX IS STRUCTURALLY MORE DANGEROUS. The single finding that makes this its own spike:

*** A 'LIFECYCLE-ONLY' TRANSPORT IS NOT SECURITY-NEUTRAL. ***
thread/start, thread/resume and thread/fork are session-CONFIG methods wearing lifecycle names. Each carries config?: Record<String, Unknown> — the JSON-RPC TWIN OF THE `-c key=value` CHANNEL that hook_relevant_codex_override (process_registry.rs:1708-1717) EXISTS TO REFUSE — plus approvalPolicy (incl. 'never'), sandbox (incl. 'danger-full-access'), and approvalsReviewer (incl. 'auto_review', an LLM subagent that approves autonomously).
An app-server child's argv is just ["app-server"]. So audit_codex_session_argv PASSES VACUOUSLY while the ENTIRE steering surface moves onto the pipe. The app-server transport therefore CARRIES the itr#511 bypass rather than avoiding it: it relocates config steering from an AUDITED channel (argv, closed typed constructor, deny-patterns, byte bounds) to an UNAUDITED one (a JSON-RPC message body).
This has no equivalent in Claude's stream-json path. Do not reason about the two transports as if they were the same shape.

THE APPROVAL-PLANE INVARIANT (recon SECURITY §, and it is counterintuitive):
The invariant is NOT 'deny transport-borne approvals and let the hook adjudicate' — that is INCOHERENT. A transport decline suppresses the command BEFORE execution, so the hook never fires; you would blanket-deny every call instead of deferring. The correct invariant is THE APPROVAL PLANE IS NEVER ENGAGED: configure Codex so approvals are not generated, and treat any inbound item/commandExecution/requestApproval (:952), item/fileChange/requestApproval (:1008) or item/tool/requestUserInput (:1066) as an UNEXPECTED-CONFIGURATION SIGNAL — log a security event, tear the thread down, alert. Its arrival PROVES the hook gate was not consulted for that call.
Per PO direction: Chat inherits the hook and decisions land in the WISPHIVE INBOX. That is Chat's gate on Codex too.

WORTH STEALING VERBATIM: methodNotFound hard-deny on any unknown server-to-client method (:1116-1118). Unknown methods are precisely what a vendor upgrade adds. This is the one t3code principle the recon rated worth copying as-is.

REJECTED ALREADY (do not rediscover): silent resume->fresh fallback under the same ThreadId (:463-478) — makes the approved artifact differ from the launched one; subordinate to the existing ownership refusal (process_registry.rs:119-127), which is stricter. Request-supplied CODEX_HOME — see ADR-0009 and the recon's SECURITY §2; if per-agent homes are wanted they must be operator-configured named entries selected by name from an allowlist, threaded through audit AND spawn atomically, never a request field. Note t3code spreads CODEX_HOME LAST into env (:717-720), clobbering the operator's value.
issue.acceptance:
1. CONTRACT CLASSIFICATION: is the app-server JSON-RPC surface DOCUMENTED-AND-VERSIONED / DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNVERSIONED / UNDOCUMENTED-INTERNAL? Cite evidence (vendor docs, schema, changelog, observed-only). Same ADR-0009 line as #564: observation may ride an undocumented pipe; THE GATE MAY NOT.
2. THE CONFIG-STEERING HOLE ANSWERED: if Wisphive drives app-server, what replaces the argv audit that now passes vacuously? Either (a) the thread/start params are constructed by a closed typed constructor with the same deny-patterns/byte-bounds/refusals as build_agent_command and hook_relevant_codex_override, or (b) app-server is rejected as a transport. Do not ship a transport whose steering surface is unaudited. An explicit, recorded decision either way.
3. APPROVAL PLANE NEVER ENGAGED: prove Codex can be configured (approvalPolicy/sandbox at thread/start :289-303, re-asserted per turn :381-389) so no requestApproval is ever generated, with the hook as the gate. Any inbound requestApproval raises an observable security event and tears the thread down. If this is NOT achievable, say so — it likely kills app-server as a Chat transport.

notes.content:
SOURCE VERDICT 2026-07-16 (openai/codex @315195492c, two independent agents — config-steering + approval-plane). CENTRAL CLAIM CONFIRMED, AND WORSE THAN SCOPED. But the resolution is a USE-distinction, not a yes/no.

=== CONFIRMED: thread/start carries the full steering surface, and config reaches the GATE ===
ThreadStartParams (app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:56-148) has as STABLE (non-experimental) fields: approval_policy (:82), approvals_reviewer (:86), sandbox (:88), config: HashMap<String,JsonValue> (:94). thread/resume (:324-398) and thread/fork (:508-590) carry the identical set; TurnStartParams re-asserts approval_policy/approvals_reviewer/sandbox_policy PER TURN (v2/turn.rs:109/113/116) — a pinned thread/start is re-steerable every turn. Permissive values all exist and are client-settable: AskForApproval::Never (shared.rs:179), SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess (shared.rs:294), ApprovalsReviewer::AutoReview (shared.rs:236, an LLM that autonomously approves).

THE config MAP REACHES THE GATE: thread_processor.rs:1116-1117 -> config_manager.load_with_overrides; load_with_cli_overrides (config_manager.rs:224-241) FIRST extracts bypass_hook_trust into ConfigOverrides, then json_to_toml's EVERY remaining key with NO allow/deny-list (utils/json-to-toml/src/lib.rs:5-27) and apply_toml_override writes ANY dotted path (config/src/overrides.rs:7-13). So a thread/start config param can set hooks.*/features.*/plugins.*/profile* AND bypass_hook_trust:true — exactly the keys Wisphive's argv audit (process_registry.rs:1708-1719) refuses. argv is policy-free (app-server/src/main.rs:19-59: only --listen/--session-source/auth/--strict-config/-c), so audit_codex_session_argv passes VACUOUSLY. #566 central claim CONFIRMED.

=== BIGGER THAN #566 SCOPED: sibling methods bypass the turn/hook plane ENTIRELY ===
The risk is the whole client->server method set on the pipe, not just thread/start. STABLE non-experimental methods (common.rs): command/exec (:1069, run argv directly, no thread), thread/shellCommand (:588, docs v2/thread.rs:977-983 'runs UNSANDBOXED with full access'), fs/writeFile (:755)/fs/remove (:775), config/value/write (:1142) + config/batchWrite (:1148, PERSIST arbitrary keys to config.toml on disk with reloadUserConfig hot-reload). process/spawn (:1093) is experimental-gated. The Wisphive hook only fires on MODEL-initiated PreToolUse within a turn — it does NOT gate client-initiated app-server methods. config/batchWrite can persist hooks/features to disk, disabling the gate for FUTURE sessions. Also thread/start with a write-capable cwd AUTO-MARKS the project trusted in config.toml (thread_processor.rs:1132-1183, set_project_trust_level Trusted).

=== APPROVAL PLANE (second agent): approvalPolicy=Never is NOT a sufficient kill switch ===
Never silences exec+patch approvals (safety.rs:57, exec_policy.rs:180/734 — AskUser branches unreachable). But THREE server->client channels fire on SEPARATE switches, policy-independent: item/tool/requestUserInput (gated by experimental_request_user_input_enabled, default off), item/permissions/requestApproval (Feature::RequestPermissionsTool), mcpServer/elicitation/request (any connected eliciting MCP server). So #566's 'treat any inbound approval as a security event and tear down' is NECESSARY, not just defensible. Four switches to hold, not one.

=== AC7: a real server-side FLOOR exists (requirements.toml / MDM) — defense-in-depth, NOT a free pass ===
Enterprise 'requirements' clamp applied AFTER request+CLI merge and WINS: allowed_approval_policies/allowed_approvals_reviewers/allowed_sandbox_modes (config_requirements.rs:1302-1398), apply_requirement_constrained_value (core/src/config/mod.rs:2004-2038, call sites :3781-3838, never+non-danger hard-errors). allow_managed_hooks_only strips ALL non-managed hooks at discovery INDEPENDENT of bypass_hook_trust (hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs:57-61/76-82). Sources: /etc/codex/requirements.toml, enterprise cloud, legacy managed_config.toml, macOS managed prefs (loader/mod.rs:180-191). Client CANNOT disable (ignore_managed_requirements is an internal test-only LoaderOverrides field, state.rs:40-46). CAVEATS: OFF BY DEFAULT (no file => Constrained::allow_any => client freely gets Never+DangerFullAccess+auto_review); clamps only approval/sandbox/reviewer/managed-hooks — NOT the arbitrary config-key vector and NOT the exec/fs/config-write sibling methods.

=== CONTRACT CLASS (AC1): DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNVERSIONED ===
2311-line README + schema generator, but schema is BINARY-SPECIFIC (README:57) and initialize (v1.rs:29-74) negotiates NO numeric protocol version — only a free-form user_agent string + experimentalApi capability bit. Breaking-change detection must be schema/capability probing that fails LOUD, never a version number.

=== THE RESOLUTION — TWO USES OF APP-SERVER, ONLY ONE IS DANGEROUS (see #569/#570 and the new ADR issue) ===
USE 1 — Wisphive-internal control plane: a SHORT-LIVED, Wisphive-authored process where EVERY message is written by Wisphive and the agent never touches the pipe. initialize -> hooks/list -> shutdown (#569); initialize -> config/batchWrite our own trusted_hash -> shutdown (#570). SAFE: none of the dangerous surface is agent-influenceable because there is no agent on this pipe. The danger B found is in what a CLIENT CHOOSES to send; when Wisphive is the sole client sending a fixed script, there is no steering.
USE 2 — agent session transport (Chat over app-server): the agent's turns flow over the pipe, config/steering/sibling-methods become agent-reachable. This is what B evaluated, and the verdict is: DO NOT expose app-server as an agent transport UNLESS (i) a closed typed constructor pins every steering field on start/resume/fork/turn, (ii) the config map is refused/allowlisted incl bypass_hook_trust, AND (iii) an explicit client->server METHOD allowlist blocks exec/fs/config-write/shellCommand. Pinning thread/start params alone is necessary but NOT sufficient.

SPIKE OUTCOME: Chat should NOT use app-server as the agent session transport in v1 (the audit surface is (i)+(ii)+(iii), large and re-asserted per turn). Prefer the stream-json path (itr#564) for the Claude side and treat Codex-Chat as its own decision. hooks/list (#569) and trusted_hash-write (#570) proceed as USE-1 internal operations, independent of this verdict.

issue.title: Web UI discards EVERY daemon error — no error-surfacing infrastructure exists (console.error and return)
issue.context:
Root cause of itr#565 (PO: 'I fill out the form to spawn one and nothing happens'), but the defect is APP-WIDE, not spawn-specific.

THE CODE (useWisphive.ts:421-423):
  case "error":
    console.error("Daemon error:", msg.message);
    return prev;

grep -rn 'toast|Toast|errorBanner|lastError|daemonError' over the frontend returns ZERO matches. There is no error-surfacing infrastructure in the web UI at all. The daemon is WELL-INSTRUMENTED — it emits ServerMessage::Error on every refusal with a good message naming the cause and the fix (e.g. the Codex foreign-hook refusal at process_registry.rs:2450-2466 carries the offending hook names AND the codex_allow_foreign_hooks opt-in instruction). Every one of those messages is parsed correctly (protocol.ts:456) and then thrown away. The operator sees nothing.

SILENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. server.rs:2431 gates the AgentSpawnQueued ack on 'if correlation_id.is_some()'. ws_bridge.rs:180 builds the envelope via ClientCommand::from(body).with_device_id(...) — correlation_id stays None (wire.rs:326). The CLI sets one; THE BROWSER NEVER DOES. So there is no error path AND no success path. App.tsx:411 closes the spawn modal unconditionally, fire-and-forget, awaiting no ack.

THE REFUSAL TABLE (from the itr#565 trace): of SIXTEEN spawn-refusal paths, exactly ONE is visible to the operator — server.rs:1419-1436's sudo reauth, which routes to WebReauthRequired -> SudoModal. And it is not even a refusal. The other fifteen: WS-not-open no-op (useWisphive.ts:617-621), ws_bridge decode failure (:138-144, warn! only), ensure_spawn_mode_active (server.rs:2381-2390), validate_spawn_request (:2394-2409), pending-id collision (:2006), MAX_PENDING_SPAWNS (:2011-2025), duplicate decision id (queue.rs:80-91, warn! only), 5-min approval expiry (server.rs:48/:2085), human deny (:1552), post-approval mode re-check (:2482), Claude hook-gate refusal (process_registry.rs:2367-2396), Codex gate/foreign-hook refusal (:2427-2466), approval-not-durably-recorded fail-closed (server.rs:2145-2175), channel dropped (:2294).

WHY THIS IS CRITICAL AND NOT COSMETIC: it makes every other bug in the system UNFALSIFIABLE FROM THE UI. The operator cannot distinguish 'refused for a good reason' from 'broken'. This is the third instance this session of the same systemic pattern — the control plane refusing or shedding work with no operator signal (see itr#559: headless defer dead-ends, job exits 0=success having done nothing; itr#560: capacity rejection silently auto-approves with no decision_log row). Fixing the silence converts every other candidate into a SELF-DIAGNOSING bug.

Found 2026-07-16 by the itr#565 trace. See also docs/research/t3code-recon.md.
issue.acceptance:
1. Daemon ServerMessage::Error is rendered to the operator — a dismissible banner/toast fed by an 'errors' state in useWisphive, not console.error. The daemon's existing message text is good; just show it.
2. The browser sets correlation_id on outbound commands (ws_bridge.rs:180 — the plumbing already exists in ClientCommand, wire.rs:326), so the daemon's existing acks (server.rs:2431) reach the web UI. Positive confirmation, not just failure.
3. Spawn submit awaits a result: the modal reflects queued / refused / error rather than closing unconditionally (App.tsx:411).
4. AUDIT ALL SIXTEEN paths from the itr#565 table — each is SURFACED or has a recorded reason why not. The two warn!-only paths (ws_bridge.rs:138-144, queue.rs:80-91) need a wire error, not just a log line.
5. Runtime-verified per CLAUDE.md: drive the real web flow against a real daemon, force a refusal (e.g. spawn into a project with no Wisphive hooks installed), and OBSERVE the error in the browser. A green vitest does not close this.
6. Generalizes beyond spawn: any daemon error on any flow surfaces. This is the infrastructure, not a spawn patch.

issue.title: last_seen never refreshed while a hook blocks — false AgentDisconnected at 305s; any registry-counting cap fails OPEN on admission
issue.context:
Found 2026-07-16 by the ADR-0007 evidence-mapping pass. Independent of t3code; every link verified against the tree.

AN AGENT BLOCKED ON A PENDING HUMAN DECISION IS FALSELY BROADCAST AS DISCONNECTED AFTER ~305s, WHILE ITS HOOK STAYS BLOCKED FOR UP TO 3600s.

CHAIN:
1. last_seen has exactly TWO refresh sites, both AFTER the fact: server.rs:930-934 touch(&agent_id) fires after the decision RESOLVES (the select! await at :880-915 has already returned); server.rs:950-955 is ToolResult/PostToolUse, also after the tool ran.
2. Registration cannot refresh it either: register_agent_once (crates/wisphive_hook/src/main.rs:1684-1750) is once-per-session behind an O_EXCL marker — AlreadyExists -> return Ok(()) at :1739. Subsequent hook invocations send no AgentRegister.
3. THEREFORE NOTHING REFRESHES last_seen WHILE A HOOK BLOCKS.
4. agent_timeout_secs = 300 (config.rs:191); HOOK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_SECS = 3600 (config.rs:28). 3600/300 = 12x — an agent legitimately waiting on a human goes 'inactive' TWELVE TIMES OVER before the human's own approval window closes.
5. Reap tick every 5s (server.rs:318); reap_inactive removes rows where last_seen < now - timeout (registry.rs:70-85). First eviction ~t=305.
6. On reap (server.rs:396-414) the session marker is unlinked AND ServerMessage::AgentDisconnected{agent_id} is broadcast to every TUI/web client.

IMPACT TODAY (real but bounded): a FALSE AgentDisconnected to every client while the hook is still blocked and its decision still sits in the queue — the operator sees a pending decision attributed to an agent the agents panel says is gone. connected_at also resets: the unlinked marker lets the next hook re-register as is_new=true (registry.rs:38-48), re-logging 'agent registered' and resetting session uptime. NOT a wave-killer today: reap_inactive only does HashMap::remove (registry.rs:70-85) — it kills no process, and nothing gates on the registry (the one running-agent-shaped cap keys on the QUEUE: queue.managed_spawn_count() >= MAX_PENDING_SPAWNS, server.rs:2011).

*** THE FORWARD-LOOKING HALF IS THE REAL FINDING — AND IT INVERTS THE RECON'S OWN WAVE WARNING. ***
docs/research/t3code-recon.md warns a naive reaper 'would kill the wave from the front while the operator works the back of the queue'. WRONG DIRECTION. If a future running-agent cap (the recon's L4) counts REGISTRY ROWS, agents blocked on the human fall OUT of the count — so the cap admits MORE agents. FAIL-OPEN ON ADMISSION. And the population it under-counts is EXACTLY the population blocked on the human: the cap stops binding precisely at maximum human latency, i.e. exactly when a wave most needs bounding.
CONSTRAINT FOR L4: any running-agent cap MUST count blocked-on-human agents, or key on the queue (as MAX_PENDING_SPAWNS already does, server.rs:2011) rather than the registry.

ALSO PRE-POISONS THE LOOP SUPERVISOR: plan-loop-supervisor.md:150-151 (open question 3) asks whether the supervisor needs an idle-timeout heuristic. If that heuristic keys on last_seen it inherits this bug directly — a loop agent blocked on a human escalation looks idle at 300s and would be aborted 12x before its own escalation window closes. This is the one genuine link between the reaper story and ADR-0007's plan; record it against open question 3 regardless of the ADR's status.

PATTERN: this is the FOURTH instance this session of the control plane mis-handling 'waiting on a human' — see itr#559 (headless defer dead-ends, job exits 0=success), itr#560 (capacity rejection silently auto-approves), itr#567 (every daemon error discarded). Waiting on a human is a first-class state the system keeps failing to model.
issue.acceptance:
1. last_seen reads 'waiting on the human' as ACTIVITY, because it is: touch on DecisionRequest ENQUEUE and/or while the pending row is live — not only on resolution.
2. No AgentDisconnected is broadcast for an agent whose hook is still blocked with a live pending decision. The agents panel and the decision queue never disagree about whether an agent exists.
3. connected_at / session uptime survives a long human-decision wait (no spurious is_new=true re-registration, registry.rs:38-48).
4. Test: enqueue a decision, hold it unresolved past agent_timeout_secs (300s default — use a short test timeout), assert NO AgentDisconnected fires and the registry row survives.
5. RECORDED CONSTRAINT for the future L4 running-agent cap: it must count blocked-on-human agents or key on the queue, never on a registry the reaper prunes — otherwise it fails OPEN on admission exactly at peak human latency.
6. RECORDED against plan-loop-supervisor.md open question 3 (:150-151): an idle-timeout heuristic must not key on last_seen while this asymmetry exists.

THE FINDING: `codex app-server` exposes a **hooks/list** JSON-RPC method that returns the effective per-project hook inventory — the exact thing audit_codex_effective_hooks re-derives across ~800 lines (process_registry.rs:1875-2150 + helpers from ~:1374).

  codex app-server generate-json-schema --out <dir>
  -> 'hooks/list' present in ClientRequest.json and codex_app_server_protocol.v2.schemas.json

HooksListParams = { cwds: string[] } ('When empty, defaults to the current session working directory') — PER-PROJECT, exactly the pre-spawn gate shape. HooksListEntry = { cwd, hooks[], errors[], warnings[] }. HookMetadata carries: enabled | source | sourcePath | isManaged | pluginId | trustStatus (managed|untrusted|trusted|modified) | eventName | matcher | command | timeoutSec | currentHash.

FIELD-FOR-FIELD, IT REPLACES THE EMULATION:
  enabled                 -> kill-switch + hooks.state precedence (round-3 desyncs #2/#3)
  source / sourcePath     -> user/project/profile TOML layering (process_registry.rs:1829-1838)
  pluginId / isManaged    -> plugin semver + allow_managed_hooks_only
  trustStatus             -> --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust exposure (itr#471/#467)
  eventName/matcher/command/timeoutSec -> gate identity + hook_timeout_secs check
  currentHash             -> integrity token for AuditSnapshot::verify_unchanged

TWO PROPERTIES ADR-0009 ASSUMED IT COULD NOT HAVE:
1. HookSource enum = system|user|project|mdm|sessionFlags|plugin|cloudRequirements|cloudManagedConfig|legacyManagedConfigFile|legacyManagedConfigMdm|unknown. ADR-0009:155-157 declares enterprise system/MDM/cloud layers 'non-enumerable trust roots'. hooks/list ENUMERATES THEM. STRATEGICALLY DECISIVE: those layers live OUTSIDE CODEX_HOME, so isolation (option b) CANNOT remove them — only introspection reaches them. (a) and (b) are COMPLEMENTARY, NOT COMPETING.
2. The 'unknown' variant: a new Codex source degrades LOUDLY rather than being silently omitted — the exact anti-desync property ADR-0009:30-34 argues emulation can never have.

*** ADR-0009'S RATIONALE RESTS ON A FALSE PREMISE. *** It rejected option (a) at :80-82 on 'an authoritative non-interactive surface DOES NOT EXIST', and plans at :176-177 to 'file the Codex feature request for codex hooks list --effective --json'. THE ASK IS ALREADY GRANTED, ON A DIFFERENT TRANSPORT. ADR-0009's facts are scoped ':42 from --help surfaces only' — it never probed the JSON-RPC protocol, and app-server is listed at :47 but never opened. The isolation decision may still be right; the alternatives analysis that justified it is wrong, and must be corrected before ADR-0009 is Accepted.

TENSION WITH itr#566 (BLOCKER): #566 treats app-server as a SECURITY RISK (thread/start carries config/approvalPolicy/sandbox/approvalsReviewer while argv is just ['app-server'], so audit_codex_session_argv passes VACUOUSLY — the steering surface moves onto an unaudited pipe). This issue says app-server is also the FIX. Both are true: app-server is simultaneously the risk and the remedy. #566 must settle whether we can speak app-server safely BEFORE this adopts hooks/list over it. If #566 concludes app-server is not safe to drive, hooks/list may still be reachable as a short-lived probe process rather than a session transport — assess that separately.

Isolated temp HOME per docs/research/headless-ask-probe/; never ./install.sh. Record evidence under docs/research/ like the other probes.
2. ADR-0009 AMENDED BEFORE ACCEPT: the Context bullet gains hooks/list with the verified schema; Rationale (a)'s 'does not exist' is struck and replaced with the residual weaknesses that actually apply (TOCTOU between introspection and spawn, [experimental] schema, extra pre-spawn process); Consequences :155-157 strikes 'non-enumerable' for MDM/cloud; :134's 'several-thousand-line audit surface' -> '~800-line' (:1374-2150); Alternatives records t3code as EXAMINED AND REJECTED AS CORROBORATION (its Codex authOverlay symlinks the operator's real config.toml — CodexHomeLayout.ts:19-29, asserted at CodexHomeLayout.test.ts:126 — and the config-blanking pattern belongs to its OpenCode driver, opencodeRuntime.ts:352, a different provider under no gate-integrity requirement).

notes.content:
SOURCE-VERIFIED 2026-07-16 against the real openai/codex checkout (commit 315195492c) — not the generated schema. Every line below is from files read. Net: source STRENGTHENS #569, but three ACs would self-block and the source reveals a better design.

STRENGTHENED — hooks/list is NOT a re-derivation. The single fn discovery::discover_handlers is called from exactly two sites: codex_hooks::list_hooks (what hooks/list returns, registry.rs:213 <- catalog_processor.rs:649) AND ClaudeHooksEngine::new (the runtime that EXECUTES hooks in a session, engine/mod.rs:126). One loop (discovery.rs:510-546) builds both the reported inventory and the executed subset from the same config walk. So the inventory provably equals what the session does — same function. This kills the 'emulation might diverge' risk at the root, stronger than the schema could show. Handler loads config the real layered way: config_manager.load_for_cwd(None, ConfigOverrides::default(), Some(cwd)) (catalog_processor.rs:610-616).

HookSource enum CONFIRMED VERBATIM (protocol.rs:1530-1545): System|User|Project|Mdm|SessionFlags|Plugin|CloudRequirements|CloudManagedConfig|LegacyManagedConfigFile|LegacyManagedConfigMdm|Unknown(#[default]). The MDM/cloud layers ADR-0009:155-157 calls 'non-enumerable' ARE enumerated and resolved from the config-layer stack (discovery.rs:615-652). Unknown #[default] snake_case = the anti-desync forward-compat property. Both #569 claims CONFIRMED.

All HookMetadata fields CONFIRMED (plugin.rs:512-526): enabled/source/sourcePath/isManaged/pluginId/trustStatus/eventName/matcher/command/timeoutSec/currentHash, plus extras #569 didn't list — key (the hooks.state map key for enable/trust writes), handlerType (only Command executes; Prompt/Agent skipped with a warning, discovery.rs:548-555), statusMessage, displayOrder.

=== THREE CORRECTIONS THAT CHANGE THE ACs ===

1. enabled:true != executes. Real execution predicate: enabled && (source.bypass_hook_trust || trust_status in {Managed,Trusted}) (discovery.rs:527-533). AC must map BOTH dimensions, not just enabled. Also is_managed hooks are ALWAYS enabled=true + Managed and cannot be disabled via hooks.state — so AC1's 'deliberately-disabled hook => enabled:false' probe must use a USER/PROJECT hook, not a managed one.

2. *** WISPHIVE'S OWN FRESHLY-INSTALLED GATE REPORTS trustStatus:Untrusted *** (test hooks_list.rs:159-189 asserts a just-written user/project command hook comes back Untrusted — no hooks.state entry yet). Trust logic (discovery.rs:589-603): Managed if managed; else trusted_hash==current_hash -> Trusted, present-but-differs -> Modified, absent -> Untrusted. CONSEQUENCES: (a) AC6/AC5 'untrusted|modified => refuse to spawn' would REFUSE ON OUR OWN GATE — self-block. (b) Under a NORMAL (non-bypass) spawn Codex would not even RUN our Untrusted hook (discovery.rs:527) — which is precisely WHY itr#471 reaches for --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust.

3. *** THE SOURCE UNLOCKS A BETTER DESIGN THAT MAY CLOSE itr#471 STRUCTURALLY. *** Instead of spawning with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (which suppresses trust for EVERY hook, hence codex_allow_foreign_hooks), Wisphive can WRITE ITS OWN HOOK'S currentHash INTO hooks.state.trusted_hash via ConfigBatchWrite (demonstrated hooks_list.rs:537-558 and :795-832), then spawn WITHOUT bypass. Codex then runs the Wisphive hook because it is Trusted, while any OTHER Untrusted/Modified/foreign hook is refused by Codex's own trust gate. #471's blast radius closes structurally, no bypass, no foreign-hook opt-in needed. THIS SHOULD BECOME ITS OWN AC / likely its own issue linked to #471. AC5 (foreign-hook refusal) is then largely superseded by Codex's native trust gate.

currentHash CORRECTED (AC4): it hashes the hook DEFINITION — NormalizedHookIdentity = event_name + matcher + {command STRING, command_windows, timeout_sec, async, status_message}, sha256 canonical-JSON (discovery.rs:497/570-587, fingerprint.rs:37-49). It is stable and good as a CONFIG-integrity token, but it does NOT hash the referenced script's bytes: for command='python3 /tmp/h.py' it covers the string, not /tmp/h.py's contents. An attacker rewriting the script while leaving the config line intact yields an UNCHANGED currentHash. AuditSnapshot::verify_unchanged must keep/add a script-content check if that's in the threat model. Adopt currentHash to replace config byte-comparison; do not oversell it as complete.

errors[]/warnings[] (AC6): errors[] is populated ONLY when config load for a cwd fails outright (catalog_processor.rs:620-630) — 'non-empty errors => refuse' is well-founded fail-closed. warnings[] is softer (skipped prompt/agent hooks, empty commands, plugin parse failures) — recommend errors=>hard stop, warnings=>surface + operator decision, not an unconditional stop.

=== DEPENDENCY REFRAME (see separate undepend) ===
hooks/list is NOT experimental-gated at the METHOD level: HooksList (common.rs:673-677) carries no #[experimental] attribute; experimental_reason()=None, so any initialized session may call it (enforcement message_processor.rs:810-813). The '[experimental]' label is on the app-server TRANSPORT as a whole (the #566 concern). So hooks/list is reachable as a SHORT-LIVED PROBE PROCESS — initialize -> hooks/list -> shutdown, NEVER calling thread/start — which entirely avoids #566's config-steering surface (that risk lives in thread/start params). #569's probe half therefore does NOT depend on resolving whether app-server is safe as a Chat SESSION TRANSPORT. Downgrading blocked-by #566 to related. AC1 runtime probe still warranted: method presence in source != working on the operator's build.

issue.title: Trust-register Wisphive's own Codex hook via hooks.state instead of --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust — closes itr#471 blast radius structurally
issue.context:
Found 2026-07-16 by the codex hooks/list source study (real openai/codex @315195492c). Directly targets itr#471's blast radius.

itr#471 TODAY: a managed Codex spawn passes --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust so the Wisphive hook runs headlessly — but bypass suppresses codex's trust gate for EVERY hook in .codex/hooks.json, so the daemon must refuse to spawn into a project carrying foreign hooks (codex_allow_foreign_hooks opt-in) to avoid running un-vetted foreign hooks headlessly.

WHY BYPASS IS USED: Codex only EXECUTES a hook when enabled && (bypass_hook_trust || trust_status in {Managed, Trusted}) (codex-rs/core .../discovery.rs:527-533). A freshly-installed user/project hook — including Wisphive's own preToolUse gate — is trust_status:Untrusted until trusted (verified: test hooks_list.rs:159-189; trust logic discovery.rs:589-603: absent trusted_hash => Untrusted). So WITHOUT bypass, Codex would refuse to run the Wisphive gate itself. Bypass is the blunt instrument that forces it to run — and unavoidably forces every other hook to run too.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX THE SOURCE REVEALS: Codex persists per-hook trust in hooks.state.trusted_hash, keyed by the hook's stable 'key', settable via the app-server ConfigBatchWrite path (demonstrated hooks_list.rs:537-558 and :795-832). If Wisphive writes ITS OWN hook's currentHash into hooks.state.trusted_hash before spawning, that hook becomes trust_status:Trusted and Codex runs it WITHOUT bypass. Every OTHER hook keeps its real trust status — a foreign/un-vetted hook stays Untrusted/Modified and Codex refuses it via its OWN native trust gate. Result: the Wisphive gate runs, foreign hooks do not, no --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, no blanket suppression, and codex_allow_foreign_hooks becomes unnecessary because foreign hooks are gated by Codex itself rather than by our refuse-to-spawn heuristic.

This is strictly better than the current posture: it removes the blast radius rather than fencing it, and it delegates foreign-hook trust to Codex's own mechanism instead of Wisphive re-deriving it.
issue.acceptance:
1. Runtime-proven: managed Codex spawn WITHOUT --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, with Wisphive's own hook trust-registered via hooks.state.trusted_hash (its currentHash from hooks/list). Confirm (a) the Wisphive preToolUse gate EXECUTES, and (b) a deliberately-planted foreign Untrusted hook does NOT execute — refused by Codex's own trust gate, not by Wisphive. Isolated temp HOME per docs/research/headless-ask-probe/; never ./install.sh.
2. The trusted_hash write is scoped to Wisphive's own hook key only — never writes trust for any hook Wisphive did not author. Re-verified each spawn (currentHash can change if the hook definition changes: Modified => re-register intentionally, never blindly).
3. currentHash covers the hook DEFINITION, not the referenced script bytes (discovery.rs:570-587) — so the script the command points at must still be integrity-checked separately if in scope (ties to itr#569 AC4 / AuditSnapshot).
4. --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust is REMOVED from the managed Codex spawn path once this lands; codex_allow_foreign_hooks (itr#471) is re-evaluated for removal since foreign hooks are now gated by Codex natively.
5. Depends on driving app-server / the ConfigBatchWrite path safely (itr#566) OR a short-lived probe-process form of the same write; sequence accordingly.
6. ADR note: this changes the itr#471 posture materially — record why bypass was replaced (blast radius removed vs fenced) so it is not reintroduced.

notes.content:
USE-1 CLARIFICATION 2026-07-16 (from the #566 source verdict): the config/batchWrite this issue relies on to write hooks.state.trusted_hash is the SAME method Agent B flagged as a gate-bypass sibling method on the app-server pipe (config/batchWrite persists arbitrary keys to config.toml). That is NOT a contradiction — it is the USE-1 vs USE-2 distinction:

USE 1 (this issue): Wisphive drives a SHORT-LIVED, Wisphive-authored app-server process, sends exactly initialize -> config/batchWrite {our own hook's trusted_hash} -> shutdown, and the AGENT NEVER TOUCHES THIS PIPE. Every byte is authored by Wisphive; there is no steering because there is no other client. Writing OUR OWN hook's hash is benign by construction.
USE 2 (the danger): exposing config/batchWrite on a pipe the agent's turns flow over. That is what #566 forbids without the full method-allowlist.

So this issue is safe as an internal control-plane operation and is NOT gated on 'is app-server safe as an agent transport' (#566's USE-2 verdict). REFRAME the blocked-by: #570 needs the ability to drive a Wisphive-controlled short-lived app-server process for config/batchWrite (a subset of #566's transport work — the initialize handshake + one method + methodNotFound hard-deny), NOT the full agent-transport audit. Sequence with #569 (same USE-1 short-lived-process machinery: initialize + one read method). Build the USE-1 harness once, use it for both.

CAVEAT the write must respect: currentHash covers the hook DEFINITION not the script bytes (#569 finding) — so trust-registering our hook's hash does NOT vouch for the script the command points at; that stays a separate integrity check.
